hadith_evidence.ar: الْحَلَالُ مَا أَحَلَّ اللَّهُ فِي كِتَابِهِ
hadith_evidence.en: The lawful is what Allah made lawful in His Book.

meaning.en: Plot, scheme. 35x. Kayd=plot, scheme. 8:18: the plot (kayd) of the disbelievers is weak. 12:76: Yusuf could not have taken his brother—except that Allah willed—the scheme of the brothers.
meaning.en_detailed: Root k-y-d (35x) names cunning stratagem, plot, and deceptive design—the deliberate construction of a trap or snare. The Quran treats worldly plotting as inherently fragile: 'the plot [kayd] of the disbelievers is weak [ḍa'īf]' (8:18)—the repeated divine counter-plot ensuring that human scheming cannot escape divine foreknowledge. In Joseph's narrative, kayd names the brothers' calculated deception against Yusuf (12:76, 'he could not have taken his brother in the religion of the king except as Allah willed'). The root belongs to a constellation of deception terms alongside makr (deliberative plotting) and khud'a (outright deception)—all subordinated to the divine kayd that overturns the human plan.
meaning.ar_definition: جذر كَادَ — 35 مرة — plot, scheme; to deceive

quranic_analysis.theme: Weakness of worldly plots
quranic_analysis.detail: Inna kayda al-kafirina da'ifun—the plot of disbelievers is weak.

hadith_evidence.ar: خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ
hadith_evidence.en: The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it.

meaning.en: To forgive, pardon; efface. 35x. Afa=forgive, efface. Afuww=Oft-Pardoning (divine name). 4:149: if you pardon (ta'fu) and overlook and forgive—Allah is Pardoning, Powerful.
meaning.en_detailed: Root '-f-w (35x) names pardon, effacement, and the wiping-out of offenses. The Quran's ethical ideal: 'if you pardon [ta'fū] and overlook [taṣfaḥū] and forgive [taghfirū]—then indeed Allah is Pardoning, Powerful' (4:149)—a triple ascent of human mercy reflecting the divine al-'Afuww (the Oft-Pardoning, ~5x), the divine name that emphasizes God's effacement of transgressions. Form X ista'fā ('to seek pardon,' 2x) is rare but present. The semantic image: to wipe clean as if the offense had never existed, a divine re-writing of moral history. 'Afw is forgiveness by erasure rather than by memory—the slate washed so clean that the chalk no longer remembers the letters it wrote.

quranic_analysis.theme: Divine pardon
quranic_analysis.detail: In tubdu khayran aw tukhfuhu aw ta'fu an su'in—pardon is closest to righteousness.

etymology.semantic_evolution: P-Semitic *ʿpw = 'to efface, wipe out'. Arabic ʿafā developed the meaning 'to pardon' — to wipe out sins as if they never existed. Al-ʿAfuww = The Oft-Pardoning — the divine name that emphasizes God's effacement of transgressions.

hadith_evidence.ar: وَاعْفُ عَمَّنْ ظَلَمَكَ
hadith_evidence.en: Pardon those who wrong you.

meaning.en: To cut, sever. 36x. Qata'a=cut. 5:33: their hands and feet be cut (tuqatta'a)—hadd punishment. 2:27: those who sever (yaqta'una) what Allah has commanded to be joined.
meaning.en_detailed: The trilateral root qaf-Ta-ayn (q t E, 36 Quranic occurrences) expresses physical severance and the consequent rupture of continuity. Its semantic range spans the literal cutting of limbs in hadd punishments (5:33 tubbat "their hands and feet be cut on opposite sides") and the metaphorical severing of covenantal bonds (2:27 al-ladhina yaqTaEuna ma amarAllahu bihi an yusala, "those who sever what Allah has commanded to be joined," i.e., kinship ties). The active participle qaTiEun also appears in the prophetic warning of 9:46 demanding loyalty over family when the latter opposes faith. Classical exegetes (Tabari, Qurtubi) pair qaTE against waSl: just as joining (Sila) is rewarded by Allah, its severing becomes a defining mark of hypocrisy (2:27). The intensive form taqaTTaEa yields decisive and irreversible severance, as in 4:52 bal huwa qaTiEun min Allah, "a decisive rejection from Allah."

quranic_analysis.theme: Severing what must be joined
quranic_analysis.detail: Yaqta'una ma amara Allahu bihi an yusala—severing family ties.

hadith_evidence.ar: خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ
hadith_evidence.en: The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it.

meaning.en: Falsehood. 36x. Batil=falsehood, void. 2:42: do not mix truth with falsehood (al-batil). 7:118: the truth appeared and what they did was proven false (batila). Antonym of haqq (truth).
meaning.en_detailed: The root ba-Ta-lam (b Tl, 36 occurrences) denotes that which is devoid of enduring reality--falsehood, void, vain. The Quran deploys al-baTil as the structural antonym of al-Haqq: 2:42 la talbisu al-Haqqa bi al-baTili wa taqTube al-Haqqa wa tubTual-baTil, "do not confound truth with falsehood" makes the dichotomy foundational. Its ephemerality is celebrated in 7:118 wa waqaEa al-Haqqu wa baTala ma kanu yaEmalun, "truth came and what they had been doing was rendered baTil," and 8:8 li-yaHaqqiqa al-Haqqa wa yubTila al-baTil. Ma-baTalun in 22:62 has provoked a folk-etymological reading of al-BaTih (a sea-abyss). In usul al-fiqh the term categorizes every transaction, testimony, or creed unanchored in revelation; classical theologians (al-AshEari, al-Maturidi) treat al-baTil as ontologically weaker than al-Haqq.

quranic_analysis.theme: Falsehood is fleeting
quranic_analysis.detail: Fa-waqa'a al-haqqu wa batala ma kanu ya'malun—truth prevailed and falsehood vanished.

hadith_evidence.ar: إِيَّاكُمْ وَالْكَذِبَ فَإِنَّ الْكَذِبَ يَهْدِي إِلَى الْفُجُورِ
hadith_evidence.en: Beware of lying, for lying leads to wickedness.

meaning.en: To precede. 37x. Sabaqa=precede. 10:49: no nation can precede (tastaqdimu) its term or delay it. The root denotes temporal and competitive priority.
meaning.en_detailed: The root sin-ba-qaf (s b q, 37 occurrences) conveys temporal precedence and competitive priority. Its Quranic deployment ranges from the impossibility of advancing one's appointed term (10:49 la tastaqdimu ummatun ajalaha wa la tastaEkhir, "no community can precede its term or delay it") to the heavenly record in which every creature's deeds are inscribed before its actions (41:20, 36:12). The active sabiqun denotes those who outstrip others in race toward Allah (56:10 wa al-sabiqun al-sabiqun, "the foremost of the foremost"); the doubled superlative marks the early Muslims of Badr and prior generations. Form VIII istasbaqa implies competitive hastening, while the noun sabq denotes the act of outpacing. Classical exegetes note the root's twin registers--divine decree (where Allah's foreknowledge sabaqa all events, 57:4 wa huwa al-Hakim al-Khabir) and human striving (where sabiqun race in obedience, 9:100 wa al-sabiqun al-awwalun).

quranic_analysis.theme: None can advance their term
quranic_analysis.detail: La tastaqdimu ummatun ajalaha—no community advances its appointed term.

hadith_evidence.ar: خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ
hadith_evidence.en: The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it.

meaning.en: Desire, passion. 38x. Hawa=desire, passion. 25:43: have you seen one who takes his desire (hawahu) as his god? 79:40: restrained his soul from desire (al-hawa). The root warns against deifying desire.
meaning.en_detailed: The root ha-waw-yaE (h w y, 38 occurrences) denotes natural or acquired inclination--desire, passion, impulse--and warns repeatedly against its enthronement as a rival deity. The Quran elevates al-hawa into a counter-rival to Allah: 25:43 a-raEayta man ittakhadha ilahahu hawahu, "have you seen one who takes his own desire as his god?" identifies this as a defining sin. The verb hawiya indicates the soul's plunge toward earthward passions; in 79:40 wa amma man khafa maqama rabbihi wa naha al-nafsa Eani al-hawa, "whoever feared his Lord's station and restrained the soul from lower desire," the verb naha is the verb of restraint against hawa. Sufi theologians (Ibn AEajiba) distinguish hawa al-muHaqqaq (verified lawful inclination) from hawa al-musakhkhaS (corrupted passion); Ibn al-Qayyim similarly classifies desires into praiseworthy and blameworthy. The etymological kinship with the divine name al-Hayy (Ever-Living) shows the root's ultimate reference to the Allah-directed life.

quranic_analysis.theme: Desire as false god
quranic_analysis.detail: A-ra'ayta man ittakhadha ilahahu hawahu—one who takes desire as his god.

hadith_evidence.ar: خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ
hadith_evidence.en: The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it.

meaning.en_short: To settle; coolness of eyes (qurrat a'yun)
meaning.en: To settle. 38x. Qarra=settle, be still. Qarar=settlement, abode. 32:17: what is hidden for them of joy/coolness of eyes (qurrati a'yun)—Paradise. 25:64: worship for Lord—prostrate and standing. Also: stability, permanence.
meaning.en_detailed: The root qaf-ra-ra (q r r, 38 occurrences) denotes settling, stability, and settled abode--from physical rest to metaphysical permanence. The Quranic phrase qurratu aEyunun ("coolness of the eyes"), first attested in 32:17 la yaElamu ma ukhfiya lahum min qurrati aEyunin, "no one knows what delights of the eye are reserved for them in secret," became the locus classicus for spousal and paradisiacal joy. Qarar in the sense of "abode, resting place" appears in 6:13 qararun mustaqirrun ("an appointed abode") and 25:64 wa alqaw yarkuEun, a verse describing the prostration and standing of true servants. The active participle muqarr names the settled, established state. Classical exegesis (al-Zamakhshari) reads qarr as the opposite of intidhar (dispersion); al-Qushayri treats qarar al-qalb as the heart's settled state in tawakkul, while qurrat al-Eayn denotes the eye's calm through being filled with what is beloved.

quranic_analysis.theme: Qurrat a'yun
quranic_analysis.detail: Qurrati a'yunin—coolness of eyes. The joy reserved for the righteous.

derived_forms.meaning: To settle; coolness of eyes (qurrat a'yun)

hadith_evidence.ar: خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ
hadith_evidence.en: The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it.

meaning.en: To deny. 37x. Nakira=reject, find strange. Munkar=evil, unknown. 3:104: commanding right (ma'ruf) and forbidding wrong (munkar). Amr bi al-ma'ruf wa nahy an al-munkar—the Islamic ethical imperative.
meaning.en_detailed: The root nun-ka-ra (n k r, 37 occurrences) denotes denial, rejection of the known, and moral ugliness--its noun derivative al-munkar becoming the Quranic term par excellence for that which is evil or disapproved. The dialectical pair al-maEruf/al-munkar structures the Quranic ethical imperative: 3:104 wa takun minkum ummatun yadEuna ila al-khayri wa yaEmuruna bi al-maErufi wa yanhawna Eani al-munkar, "let there arise from you a community inviting to good and forbidding evil" (the famous al-amr bi al-maEruf wa al-nahy Ean al-munkar). Classical jurists (ShafiEi, Malik) read the second clause as encompassing the prevention of any act whose ugliness is acknowledged by sound nature (al-fiTra al-salima). The verb nukira additionally yields "to be unfamiliar with" (12:58 ya qawmi inna akhi wa law akrunahu bihi), and Form V tanakkara captures deliberate disguise (20:67 tanakkaru, "they disguised themselves") in Pharaoh's plot against Moses.

quranic_analysis.theme: Forbidding evil
quranic_analysis.detail: Ya'muruna bi al-ma'rufi wa yanhawna ani al-munkar—commanding right, forbidding wrong.

hadith_evidence.ar: خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ
hadith_evidence.en: The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it.

meaning.en: Hurl. 7x. Qadhafa=cast, accuse of adultery. 24:4: those who accuse (yarmuna) chaste women—flog them eighty lashes.
meaning.en_detailed: The root qaf-dhal-faE (q dh f, 9 occurrences) denotes forceful projection--whether literal hurling or rhetorical casting of accusation. Its legal locus classicus is 24:4 wa al-ladhina yarmuna al-muHsanati thumma lam yaEtu bi-arbaEatin shuhadaEa, "those who accuse chaste women then fail to produce four witnesses" (qadhf--false accusation of unchastity--punishable by eighty lashes, 24:2 jilduhum thamanina jaldatan). The same root applies to the cosmic topography of Hellfire (81:17 yulqawna fihi, "they are cast into it") and to the angelic repulsing of devils (67:5 ramayna Ealayka shuhadaEfa). Classical jurists (al-ShafiEi, Ibn Qudama) extend the qadhf prohibition to innuendo (al-tawriya), oblique implication (al-taEriDh), and the metaphorical accusation against specific individuals. The legal maxim al-Hudud yastaqim bi al-shubha exempts doubtful applications; a single shubha (doubt) suffices to lift the hadd.

quranic_analysis.theme: Accusing chaste women
quranic_analysis.detail: Walladhina yarmuna al-muhsanati—those who accuse chaste women.

hadith_evidence.ar: إِنَّ هَذَا الْقُرْآنَ يَهْدِي لِلَّتِي هِيَ أَقْوَمُ
hadith_evidence.en: Indeed, this Quran guides to that which is most upright.

meaning.en_short: Ornament, jewelry, adornment; to adorn, beautify
meaning.en: Ḥilya means ornament, jewelry, adornment. In the Quran: gold, pearls, and fine adornments of Paradise. The verb ḥallā means 'he adorned, beautified'. Also refers to the beautiful description of the Prophet in earlier scriptures. Ḥilya is not merely decoration but that which reveals and enhances inherent beauty.
meaning.ar: الزينة والحلية — ما تزين به المرأة وغيرها
meaning.en_detailed: ح ل ي (ح ل ي), a root appearing 9 times in the Quran, encodes the notion of Ornament, jewelry, adornment; to adorn, beautify across its various verbal and nominal forms. Key Quranic occurrences include 13:13, 7:148, 13:13, 7:148, 13:13, 7:148, 13:13, 7:148. The Proto-Semitic antecedent *ḥaly- (ornament, jewelry) underlies this root, with cognates attested in related Semitic languages. The root yields derived forms including II, V, each extending the core meaning into specific semantic domains.
meaning.ar_definition: جذر ح ل ي — 9 مرة — Ornament

etymology.semantic_evolution: Adornment — the enhancement of beauty through external ornament.

usage_patterns: Ḥilya as paradisal reward — believers adorned in gold and silk

lexicographical_sources: Ibn Faris: al-ḥilya is al-zīna
theological_dimensions: The ḥilya of the Prophet in earlier scriptures — the description of his qualities

hadith_evidence.ar: ح ل ي — وَرَدَ ذِكْرُهُ فِي الْقُرْآنِ 9 مَرَّةً
hadith_evidence.en: The root Hly (ح ل ي) appears 9 times in the Quran, including 13:13.

meaning.en: Heedlessness. 35x. Ghafala=be heedless. Ghaflah=heedlessness. 7:179: they have hearts but understand not, eyes but see not—they are like cattle, nay more astray, they are the heedless (al-ghafilun).
meaning.en_detailed: The root ghayn-fa-lam (gh f l, 35 occurrences) denotes the absence of attention and presence of mind--heedlessness, oblivion, being caught unaware. Its Quranic locus classicus is 7:179 wa laqad dhakkar wa lahum shuhadaEun yadkuruna, "they are the heedless" (al-ghafilun), where humanity's failure to perceive divine signs condemns them as "worse than cattle." The same root pairs the human condition with divine attributes: al-Ghafur (the Forgiving) is paired with al-Wadud in the descent of revelation (41:32) and is named the most-comprehensive of divine mercies (39:53 qul ya Eibadi alladhina asrafu Eala anfusihim la taqnaEu min raHmati Allah). Classical Sufi manuals (al-Qushayri's Risala, al-Ghazali's IyaE) treat ghaflah as the cardinal illness of the soul, remedied only through muHasaba (self-audit) and dhikr (remembrance).

quranic_analysis.theme: Heedlessness condemned
quranic_analysis.detail: Ula'ika hum al-ghafilun—they are the heedless. Worse than cattle.

hadith_evidence.ar: خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ
hadith_evidence.en: The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it.

meaning.en_short: To incline to truth; ḥanīf (primordial monotheist)
meaning.en: Ḥanīf is the Quranic term for the original, pure monotheist — the primordial believer who inclines away from idolatry toward God alone. Ibrāhīm is the paradigmatic ḥanīf (3:67). The root ḥanafa means 'to incline, lean, deviate' — specifically, to incline away from falsehood toward truth. Ḥanīfiyya is the religion of Abraham: pure, unadulterated monotheism.
meaning.ar: الميل عن الباطل إلى الحق — والحنيف المائل عن كل دين باطل إلى دين الحق
meaning.en_detailed: Occurring 12 times in the Quranic text, the root ح ن ف (ح ن ف) conveys the essential concept of To incline to truth; ḥanīf (primordial monotheist). Key Quranic occurrences include 3:67, 10:105, 3:67, 10:105, 3:67, 10:105, 3:67, 10:105. The Proto-Semitic antecedent *ḥanaf- (to incline, lean) underlies this root, with cognates attested in related Semitic languages.
meaning.ar_definition: جذر ح ن ف — 12 مرة — To incline to truth

cognates.hebrew: חנף — to be impious (inverted sense in Hebrew!)

etymology.semantic_evolution: Incline → deviate from falsehood toward truth. Hebrew developed the opposite sense (deviating from God), while Arabic specialized in the positive deviation toward God.

key_nominals.meaning: upright, true in faith, primordial monotheist

usage_patterns: Ḥanīfiyya as the primordial religion of Abraham

lexicographical_sources: Raghib: al-ḥanīf is al-māʾil ʿan al-ḍalāl ilā al-istiwāʾ
theological_dimensions: Dīn al-ḥanīf — the original religion before Judaism and Christianity

hadith_evidence.ar: دَعْ مَا يَرِيبُكَ إِلَى مَا لَا يَرِيبُكَ
hadith_evidence.en: Leave what makes you doubt for what does not make you doubt.

meaning.en: Ḥūt means fish — appearing in the stories of Mūsā's lost fish (the miraculous sign) and Yūnus (Dhū al-Nūn) who was swallowed by the 'fish' (often understood as a whale). The Quranic word is used for both ordinary fish and the great sea creature.
meaning.ar: الحوت — السمك، الكبير منه خاصة
meaning.en_detailed: Root ح و ت (ح و ت), attested 5 times in the Quran, derives its core meaning of Fish, whale from Proto-Semitic sources. Key Quranic occurrences include 18:61, 37:142, 18:61, 37:142, 18:61, 37:142, 18:61, 37:142. The Proto-Semitic antecedent بني underlies this root, with cognates attested in related Semitic languages.
meaning.ar_definition: جذر ح و ت — 5 مرة — Fish

etymology.semantic_evolution: Fish/whale — used for the miraculous fish of Mūsā and the creature that swallowed Yūnus.

usage_patterns: Ḥūt as sign in Mūsā's journey and Yūnus's ordeal

lexicographical_sources: Ibn Faris: al-ḥūt is min ḥayawān al-māʾ
theological_dimensions: The fish as marker of divine intervention — its disappearance signals the meeting with al-Khiḍr

hadith_evidence.ar: ح و ت — وَرَدَ ذِكْرُهُ فِي الْقُرْآنِ 5 مَرَّةً
hadith_evidence.en: The root Hwt (ح و ت) appears 5 times in the Quran, including 18:61.

meaning.en: Blindness. 33x. Amiya=be blind. Ama=blind. 2:18: deaf, dumb, and blind (umyun)—they will not return. 17:72: whoever is blind (a'ma) in this world will be blind in the Hereafter. Spiritual blindness.
meaning.en_detailed: The root Eayn-mi-yaE (E m y, 33 occurrences) denotes physical blindness and--more importantly in the Quran--the far more damning spiritual blindness of hearts that refuse to see. The word's deepest reach is 17:72 wa man kana fi hadhihi aEma fa-huwa fi al-akhirati aEma wa aDallu sabila, "whoever was blind in this world will be blind in the Hereafter and more astray in way." The collective form al-Eumy in 2:18 Summun bukmun Eumyun fahum la yaEqilun, "deaf, dumb, and blind--they will not return," names the inner incapacity of the disbeliever. Classical exegetes (Tabari, Razi) treat these three conditions as descriptive of the spiritual state, not literal: the heart has eyes (baSira) and ears (samE) but the veil of taqwa's absence renders them dysfunctional. The active aEma is also used for the kindly blind companion of Pharaoh who believed (40:28).

quranic_analysis.theme: Spiritual blindness
quranic_analysis.detail: Wa man kana fi hadhihi a'ma—blind in this world, blind in the Hereafter.

hadith_evidence.ar: خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ
hadith_evidence.en: The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it.

meaning.en_short: To gather, contain, encompass; abyss, chasm
meaning.en: Ḥawā means 'he gathered, contained, encompassed'. Ḥawāyā is an encompassing thing — a container. In the Quran, it appears in the context of the 'abyss' or 'chasm' (hāwiya, hāwiya — one of Hell's names). The root denotes gathering things within a boundary.
meaning.ar: الجمع والاحتواء — وحوى الشيء جمعه
meaning.en_detailed: The triconsonantal root ح و ي (ح و ي) — 2 Quranic occurrences — fundamentally expresses To gather, contain, encompass; abyss, chasm. Key Quranic occurrences include 101:9. The Proto-Semitic antecedent بني underlies this root, with cognates attested in related Semitic languages. The root yields derived forms including I, VIII, each extending the core meaning into specific semantic domains. The root carries significant theological weight in the Quranic worldview, recurring in contexts that shape Islamic doctrine and spiritual understanding.
meaning.ar_definition: جذر ح و ي — 2 مرة — To gather

etymology.semantic_evolution: Gathering/encompassing — the root of containment and enclosure.

key_nominals.meaning: abyss, chasm, pit; a name of Hell

usage_patterns: Hāwiya as the bottomless abyss of Hell

lexicographical_sources: Ibn Faris: al-ḥawy is al-jamʿ
theological_dimensions: Al-Hāwiya — the mother whose 'child' is the damned, ever-falling

hadith_evidence.en: The root Hwy (ح و ي) appears 2 times in the Quran, including 101:9.

meaning.en: Ḥaythu means 'where, wherever'. A spatial/conditional particle indicating location or circumstance. In the Quran: 'wherever you are' (aynamā takūnū), 'from wherever you come forth' (min ḥaythu kharajta). Used to establish universal applicability of divine commands and spiritual states.
meaning.ar: حيث — ظرف مكان للتعميم
meaning.en_detailed: ح ي ث (ح ي ث), a root appearing 31 times in the Quran, encodes the notion of Where, wherever; wherever you are across its various verbal and nominal forms. Key Quranic occurrences include 2:149. The Proto-Semitic antecedent *ḥayṯ- underlies this root, with cognates attested in related Semitic languages.
meaning.ar_definition: جذر ح ي ث — 31 مرة — Where

etymology.semantic_evolution: Spatial particle → universal locational indicator.

usage_patterns: Ḥaythu as universal spatial particle

lexicographical_sources: Ibn Faris: ḥaythu is makān

hadith_evidence.en: The root Hyv (ح ي ث) appears 31 times in the Quran, including 2:149.

meaning.en: Ḥāqa means 'it surrounded, encompassed, befell' — used exclusively of divine punishment or the consequences of evil encircling the wrongdoers. The Quranic pattern: 'wa-ḥāqa bihim mā kānū bihi yastahziʾūn' — 'and there surrounded them what they used to mock'. The root conveys inescapable retribution.
meaning.ar: أحاط به ونزل — والحوق نزول العذاب
meaning.en_detailed: Occurring 10 times in the Quranic text, the root ح ي ق (ح ي ق) conveys the essential concept of To surround, encompass, befall (of punishment). Key Quranic occurrences include 6:10. The Proto-Semitic antecedent *ḥawq- underlies this root, with cognates attested in related Semitic languages. The root yields derived forms including I, each extending the core meaning into specific semantic domains. The root carries significant theological weight in the Quranic worldview, recurring in contexts that shape Islamic doctrine and spiritual understanding.
meaning.ar_definition: جذر ح ي ق — 10 مرة — To surround

etymology.semantic_evolution: Surrounding → inescapable punishment. Ḥāqa is always negative in the Quran — the encircling of doom.

derived_forms.key_verse: 6:10 وَحَاقَ بِٱلَّذِينَ سَخِرُوا۟ مِنۡهُم — surrounded those who mocked

usage_patterns: Ḥāqa bi-him as Quranic retribution formula

lexicographical_sources: Raghib: al-ḥawq is iḥāṭat al-shayʾ
theological_dimensions: Divine irony: what was mocked becomes the instrument of punishment

hadith_evidence.ar: ح ي ق — وَرَدَ ذِكْرُهُ فِي الْقُرْآنِ 10 مَرَّةً
hadith_evidence.en: The root Hyq (ح ي ق) appears 10 times in the Quran, including 6:10.

meaning.en_short: Time, period, occasion; when; at the time when
meaning.en: Ḥīn means 'time, period, occasion'. Used for unspecified temporal periods: 'for a time' (ilā ḥīnin), 'at the time when' (ḥīna). Appears in both worldly and eschatological contexts — the appointed time of harvest, the time of death, the time of judgment. The indefinite 'ḥīnan min al-dahr' = 'a period of time'.
meaning.ar: الوقت والزمان — والحين مدة من الزمن غير محددة
meaning.en_detailed: Root ح ي ن (ح ي ن), attested 35 times in the Quran, derives its core meaning of Time, period, occasion; when; at the time when from Proto-Semitic sources. Key Quranic occurrences include 76:1, 16:80, 76:1, 16:80, 76:1, 16:80, 76:1, 16:80. The Proto-Semitic antecedent *ḥayn- underlies this root, with cognates attested in related Semitic languages.
meaning.ar_definition: جذر ح ي ن — 35 مرة — Time

etymology.semantic_evolution: Time/period — one of several Quranic temporal terms. Ḥīn is indefinite compared to ʾajal (fixed term) or yawm (day).

usage_patterns: Ḥīn as indefinite temporal span

lexicographical_sources: Ibn Faris: al-ḥīn is waqt
theological_dimensions: Ḥīn vs ʾajal: indefinite period vs fixed term

hadith_evidence.ar: ح ي ن — وَرَدَ ذِكْرُهُ فِي الْقُرْآنِ 35 مَرَّةً
hadith_evidence.en: The root Hyn (ح ي ن) appears 35 times in the Quran, including 76:1.

meaning.en_short: To be foul, impure, malignant, evil
meaning.en: Khabutha means 'it was foul, impure, malignant'. Al-khabīth is that which is foul, impure, evil — the opposite of al-ṭayyib (good, pure). In the Quran: 'the foul (khabīth) for the foul, and the good (ṭayyib) for the good' (24:26). Used for moral impurity, corrupt wealth, and evil speech. The root establishes a fundamental moral binary.
meaning.ar: ضد الطيب — الخبيث الرديء الفاسد
meaning.en_detailed: Root خ ب ث (خ ب ث), attested 16 times in the Quran, derives its core meaning of To be foul, impure, malignant, evil from Proto-Semitic sources. Key Quranic occurrences include 24:26, 7:157, 24:26, 7:157, 24:26, 7:157, 24:26, 7:157. The Proto-Semitic antecedent *ḫabīṯ- underlies this root, with cognates attested in related Semitic languages. The root yields derived forms including I, II, IV, each extending the core meaning into specific semantic domains.
meaning.trilateral_meaning: To be foul, impure, malignant, evil
meaning.ar_definition: جذر خ ب ث — 16 مرة — To be foul

etymology.semantic_evolution: Foulness/impurity → moral evil. Khabīth/ṭayyib as Quranic moral binary.

usage_patterns: Khabīth/ṭayyib as fundamental Quranic moral binary

lexicographical_sources: Raghib: al-khabīth is mā yakrahuhu al-ṭabʿ
theological_dimensions: The law of moral correspondence: like attracts like

hadith_evidence.ar: إِيَّاكُمْ وَالظَّنَّ فَإِنَّ الظَّنَّ أَكْذَبُ الْحَدِيثِ
hadith_evidence.en: Beware of suspicion, for suspicion is the most false of speech.

meaning.en_short: To estimate, guess, conjecture; to lie
meaning.en: Kharasa means 'he estimated, guessed, conjectured'. In the Quran, it is synonymous with lying and speaking without knowledge — 'they only conjecture (yakhruṣūna)' describes the Meccan deniers who speak about God without evidence. The kharraṣūn are the 'guessers' — those who arrogantly speculate about divine matters.
meaning.ar: الظن والتخمين بلا علم — والخرص الكذب
meaning.en_detailed: The Arabic root خ ر ص (خ ر ص) appears 5 times in the Quran, governing the semantic domain of To estimate, guess, conjecture; to lie. Key Quranic occurrences include 6:116, 51:10, 6:116, 51:10, 6:116, 51:10, 6:116, 51:10. The Proto-Semitic antecedent *ḫarṣ- underlies this root, with cognates attested in related Semitic languages. The root yields derived forms including I, II, each extending the core meaning into specific semantic domains.
meaning.trilateral_meaning: To estimate, guess, conjecture; to lie
meaning.ar_definition: جذر خ ر ص — 5 مرة — To estimate

etymology.semantic_evolution: Estimation without knowledge → lie. The kharraṣūn are condemned as those who speak about God without evidence.

derived_forms.key_verse: 6:116 إِن يَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا ٱلظَّنَّ — they follow only conjecture

usage_patterns: Kharraṣūn as those who speak about God without knowledge

lexicographical_sources: Raghib: al-kharṣ is al-qawl bi-l-ẓann
theological_dimensions: Qutila al-kharrāṣūn — the strongest Quranic condemnation of religious speculation

hadith_evidence.ar: إِيَّاكُمْ وَالْكَذِبَ فَإِنَّ الْكَذِبَ يَهْدِي إِلَى الْفُجُورِ
hadith_evidence.en: Beware of lying, for lying leads to wickedness.

meaning.en_short: To store, treasure, hoard; sadness, grief; treasurer, guardian
meaning.en: Khazana means 'he stored, treasured, preserved'. Khizāna is a treasury, storehouse. Khāzin is a treasurer or guardian. In the Quran: the 'treasuries' of God's mercy, and the guardian angels of Hell (khazanatu jahannam). The root also gives ḥuzn (sadness, grief) — the emotion stored in the heart.
meaning.ar: حفظ الشيء في الخزانة — والخزن بالضم الحزن
meaning.en_detailed: The triconsonantal root خ ز ن (خ ز ن) — 13 Quranic occurrences — fundamentally expresses To store, treasure, hoard; sadness, grief; treasurer, guardian. Key Quranic occurrences include 6:50, 39:71, 6:50, 39:71, 6:50, 39:71, 6:50, 39:71. The Proto-Semitic antecedent *ḫazan- underlies this root, with cognates attested in related Semitic languages. The root yields derived forms including I, VIII, each extending the core meaning into specific semantic domains.
meaning.ar_definition: جذر خ ز ن — 13 مرة — To store

etymology.semantic_evolution: Storing → treasuring. Ḥuzn (grief) from the same root — grief as that which is 'stored' in the heart.

derived_forms.meaning: to store up, treasure for oneself

usage_patterns: Khazāʾin Allāh — divine treasuries beyond human access

lexicographical_sources: Ibn Faris: al-khazn is ṣawn al-shayʾ
theological_dimensions: Khazānat jahannam — the angelic guardians of Hell

hadith_evidence.ar: خ ز ن — وَرَدَ ذِكْرُهُ فِي الْقُرْآنِ 13 مَرَّةً
hadith_evidence.en: The root xzn (خ ز ن) appears 13 times in the Quran, including 6:50.

meaning.en: To incline; peace. 34x. Janaha=incline. 8:61: if they incline (janahu) to peace, then incline (fa-jnah) to it—rely upon Allah. The root denotes peaceful inclination.
meaning.en_detailed: The root jim-nun-Ha (j n H, 34 occurrences) denotes inclination, lateral turning, and--extended figuratively--a peaceful disposition. Its chief Quranic ethical-political application is 8:61 wa in yanHu li al-salm fajanH laha wa tawakkal Eala Allah, "if they incline (yanHu) toward peace, then incline (fajanH) toward it and rely upon Allah"--a directive establishing the principle that Muslim authority is bound to meet peaceful overtures with reciprocal peace. The root's image is the bird's oblique flight (janaH, "wing"), whence "to swerve" or "to incline" toward a side; the noun janih al-Harb names a belligerent combatant in classical jurisprudence (Malik, Abu Hanifa). The verb janHa also covers unauthorized religious deviation (57:27 qad bigha hawaihi, "they followed their caprices," describing a community whose monks went beyond the bounds of obedience).

quranic_analysis.theme: Inclining to peace
quranic_analysis.detail: Wa in janahu li al-silmi fa-jnah laha—if they incline to peace, incline to it.

hadith_evidence.ar: خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ
hadith_evidence.en: The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it.

meaning.en: To suffice. 33x. Kafa=suffice. 3:173: Allah is sufficient (hasbuna Allah) for us and the best Disposer (al-Wakil). 39:36: is not Allah sufficient (kafin) for His servant?
meaning.en_detailed: The root kaf-faE-yaE (k f y, 33 occurrences) denotes sufficiency and adequacy--often the sufficiency of Allah to meet any need, threat, or pursuit. The Quranic locus classicus is 3:173 Hasbuna Allahu wa niEma al-wakil, "Allah is sufficient for us and an excellent Disposer"--the phrase uttered by the muEminun after the Battle of Uhud, who refused to flee because they trusted in divine sufficiency. Even more emphatic is 39:36 a-laysa Allahu bi-kafin Eabduhu, "is not Allah sufficient for His servant?" The active participle kafin names one who fulfills a duty to the exclusion of other claimants (2:139 qul a-tuHajjunanani fi Allahi wa huwa rabbuna). Classical Sufi treatises (al-Qushayri, Ibn AEaTa Allah's al-Hikam) develop kifaya as a state of spiritual contentment with Allah alone; the Hadith al-ghina al-akbar affirms: "the greatest richness is for the servant to be in need of nothing but Allah."

quranic_analysis.theme: Allah suffices
quranic_analysis.detail: Hasbuna Allahu wa ni'ma al-wakil—Allah suffices us.

hadith_evidence.ar: خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ
hadith_evidence.en: The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it.

meaning.en_short: To be disgraced, humiliated, put to shame
meaning.en: Khaziya means 'he was disgraced, humiliated'. Khizy is disgrace, shame, humiliation — especially eschatological disgrace. In the Quran, the 'Day when the wrongdoers will be disgraced' (yawma yukhza al-ladhīna kafarū). The root denotes public humiliation and loss of honor, contrasted with ʿizza (honor, glory).
meaning.ar: الفضيحة والهوان — والخزي ضد العز
meaning.en_detailed: Occurring 26 times in the Quranic text, the root خ ز ي (خ ز ي) conveys the essential concept of To be disgraced, humiliated, put to shame. Key Quranic occurrences include 3:192. The Proto-Semitic antecedent *ḫazay- underlies this root, with cognates attested in related Semitic languages. The root yields derived forms including I, IV, each extending the core meaning into specific semantic domains. The root carries significant theological weight in the Quranic worldview, recurring in contexts that shape Islamic doctrine and spiritual understanding.
meaning.trilateral_meaning: To be disgraced, humiliated, put to shame
meaning.ar_definition: جذر خ ز ي — 26 مرة — To be disgraced

etymology.semantic_evolution: Disgrace → eschatological humiliation. The public shame of the damned.

derived_forms.meaning: to disgrace, humiliate, put to shame
derived_forms.key_verse: 3:192 رَبَّنَآ إِنَّكَ مَن تُدۡخِلِ ٱلنَّارَ فَقَدۡ أَخۡزَيۡتَهُۥ

usage_patterns: Khizy as eschatological opposite of ʿizza

lexicographical_sources: Raghib: al-khizy is al-hawān wa-l-faḍīḥa
theological_dimensions: The disgrace of the Fire as ultimate loss of honor

hadith_evidence.ar: خ ز ي — وَرَدَ ذِكْرُهُ فِي الْقُرْآنِ 26 مَرَّةً
hadith_evidence.en: The root xzy (خ ز ي) appears 26 times in the Quran, including 3:192.

meaning.en: Side; to avoid. 33x. Janb=side, flank. Ijtanaba VIII=avoid. Junub=ritually impure. 4:36: the neighbor by your side (al-jari dhi al-qurba) and the companion at your side (al-sahibi bi al-janb). 2:222: do not approach them until they are pure—junub state.
meaning.en_detailed: The root jim-nun-ba (j n b, 33 occurrences) expresses side, flank, and the act of avoiding or distancing oneself from. The Quranic phrase al-SaHib bi al-janb (4:36, "the companion at your side") and al-jar dhu al-qurba bring the root into the social-ethical register of attentiveness to those physically close. The masculine verbal noun janb in ritual law names the state of junub (major ritual impurity, requiring ghusl), which spouses must observe (2:222 la taqrabuhunna Hatta yaTHurna, "do not approach them until they are pure"). Form VIII ijtanaba means "to shun, avoid" (16:36 ijTanibu al-rijsa mina al-awthan, "shun the abomination of idols"). Classical Sufi manuals use mujanabat al-rijal to denote cutting oneself off from worldly contamination; the active janibun names one positioned at the side of the righteous, while janib Allah describes the angel-elevated souls of 4:172.
meaning.ar_definition: جذر جَنِبَ — 33 مرة — side; to avoid, shun

quranic_analysis.theme: The neighbor at your side
quranic_analysis.detail: Wa al-sahibi bi al-janb—the companion at your side.

hadith_evidence.ar: خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ
hadith_evidence.en: The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it.

meaning.en: To disobey. 32x. Asa=disobey. 20:121: Adam disobeyed (asa) his Lord and went astray. The root denotes intentional violation of divine command.
meaning.en_detailed: The root Eayn-Sad-yaE (E S y, 32 occurrences) denotes willful disobedience to a recognized authority, with an emphasis on conscious rebellion rather than mere error. Its pivotal locus is 20:121 wa Easa Adamu rabbahu fa-ghawa, "Adam disobeyed his Lord and erred"--yet the same root elsewhere names the ongoing rebellion of the Israelites (2:61 wa EaSawtum baEd dhalika), Pharaoh's folk (7:103), and Nuh's opponents (71:7 a-wa Easa r-rasulu yaqunalu lahu rabbi ama yaEulu bi-n-nufus, the verse asking why the messenger should be disobeyed). The noun maSiya (sin/disobedience) is built from the same root and recurs in legal contexts; classical theologians distinguish ESyan mukhtaSS from maSiya muEayyana--the defiance of a specific prohibition versus the general disposition to rebel. Al-Zamakhshari notes that ESyan implies a degree of awareness the element of maErifa (knowing) whereas jahl (ignorance) excludes it. Sufi writers treat ESyan as the opposite of TaEa but not of tawba, since every rebel-repentant has a way back.

quranic_analysis.theme: Adam's slip
quranic_analysis.detail: Wa asa Adama rabbahu—Adam disobeyed his Lord.

hadith_evidence.ar: خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ
hadith_evidence.en: The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it.

meaning.en: To enjoin, instruct. 32x. Wassa II=enjoin. Wasiyyah=testament, will. 2:132: Abraham enjoined (wassa) his sons and Jacob: worship One God. 2:180: prescribed to make a will (al-wasiyyah) when death approaches.
meaning.en_detailed: The root waw-Sad-yaE (w S y, 32 occurrences) denotes formal injunction, commission, and testamentary direction. Its paradigmatic occurrence is 2:132 wa waSSa biha Ibrahimu banihi wa YaEaqub, "Abraham enjoined his sons and Jacob" with the Shahada of tawHid--the root thereby becomes the etymological anchor of all prophetic ethical transmission. The noun waSiyya (testament, will) appears in 2:180 kutiba Ealaykum idha HaDara aHadakumu al-mawtu in taraka khayran al-waSiyyatu li al-walidayn wa al-aqrabin, "prescribed for you, when death approaches one of you, if he leaves goods, the bequest for parents and kin"--the basis of Islamic testamentary law. Form II waSSa intensifies the injunction into a binding and recurring duty; the active participle wasi names the testator; the noun al-musi references the entrusted party. Classical jurists distinguish waSiyya (formal will) from waqf (endowment), though both flow from the same root's sense of lasting religious direction.

quranic_analysis.theme: Abraham's injunction
quranic_analysis.detail: Wa wassa biha Ibrahima banihi—Abraham enjoined his sons.

hadith_evidence.ar: خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ
hadith_evidence.en: The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it.

meaning.en: To kindle; conceal. 32x. Wara=kindle (fire). Tawara V=hide behind. 2:17: like one who kindled (istawqada) a fire—hypocrite parable. The root spans flame and hiddenness behind.
meaning.en_detailed: The root waw-ra-yaE (w r y, 32 occurrences) carries two paired semantic fields: kindling fire and concealment behind. The verb wariya in the sense of "fire is lit" appears in 2:17 mathaluhum ka-mathali alladhi istawqada nara, "his likeness is as one who kindled a fire"--the parable of the hypocrite who lights a fire only to have it extinguished around him, leaving him in darkness. The same root yields tawarra (V) "to hide behind": Adam and Eve hide from Allah's presence in 7:20-22 (fa-tawallaya, then attempted cover with leaves). Classical exegesis (Tabari, Razi) identifies the dual root as symbolic of the hypocrite's project of self-creation and self-concealment. Form II warra appears in scenes of concealment. Sufi manuals (al-Qushayri) note that the stage beyond tawarra is tawajjuh, the openness of the soul before Allah.

quranic_analysis.theme: Hypocrite's fire
quranic_analysis.detail: Mathaluhum kamathali alladhi istawqada naran—parable of one who kindled fire.

hadith_evidence.ar: اتَّقُوا النَّارَ وَلَوْ بِشِقِّ تَمْرَةٍ
hadith_evidence.en: Save yourselves from the Fire, even with half a date.

meaning.en_short: Loss, ruin; to lose, be in loss
meaning.en: Khasira means 'he lost, suffered loss'. Khusrān is loss, ruin, perdition — the ultimate state of the damned. In the Quran, 'al-insāna la-fī khusrin' — humanity is in loss except those who believe and do righteous deeds (103:2-3). The root is one of the Quran's most important eschatological concepts: the absolute, irreversible loss of the Hereafter.
meaning.ar: الخسران — ذهاب رأس المال، وفي الدين الهلاك
meaning.en_detailed: The triconsonantal root خ س ر (خ س ر) — 65 Quranic occurrences — fundamentally expresses Loss, ruin; to lose, be in loss. Key Quranic occurrences include 103:2-3. The Proto-Semitic antecedent *ḫasir- underlies this root, with cognates attested in related Semitic languages. The root yields derived forms including I, II, IV, each extending the core meaning into specific semantic domains. The root carries significant theological weight in the Quranic worldview, recurring in contexts that shape Islamic doctrine and spiritual understanding.
meaning.ar_definition: جذر خ س ر — 65 مرة — Loss

etymology.semantic_evolution: Loss → eschatological ruin. The ultimate loss is not material but spiritual — losing one's soul.

derived_forms.meaning: to lose, be in loss, suffer loss
to make lose; to give short measure

usage_patterns: Khusrān as eschatological opposite of falāḥ

lexicographical_sources: Raghib: al-khusr is al-naqṣ fī raʾs al-māl
theological_dimensions: Al-insānu la-fī khusr — the universal human condition

hadith_evidence.ar: خ س ر — وَرَدَ ذِكْرُهُ فِي الْقُرْآنِ 65 مَرَّةً
hadith_evidence.en: The root xsr (خ س ر) appears 65 times in the Quran, including 103:2-3.

meaning.en: Kindle. 3x. Sa'ara=kindle. 81:12: when Hell is set ablaze (su'irat)—Judgment Day.
meaning.en_detailed: The root sin-Eayn-ra (s E r, 19 occurrences) denotes burning, kindling, and the ablaze state. Its iconic Quranic occurrence is 81:12 wa idha al-jahimu suEirat, "and when Hellfire is set ablaze"--a verse of judgment-day severity whose root conveys both the act of kindling and the burning state. The same root appears in the punishment imagery of 67:7 wa la yus'alu Ean dhanubihim, "He will not be asked about his sins, [for] they will [see] them," and in 4:30 the imagery of the soul that "consumes" itself. The active participle saEirun names those whose hearts burn with the fires of desire or punishment; the verb saEara also names the in-flame state of an enemy fallen under divine wrath. Classical commentators note saEara as the imagery of wrathful separation from Allah, contrasted with divine tarwiya (coolness, q.v.) offered to the souls of the obedient.

quranic_analysis.theme: Hellfire kindled
quranic_analysis.detail: Wa idha al-jahimu su'irat—when Hell is set ablaze.

hadith_evidence.ar: خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ
hadith_evidence.en: The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it.

meaning.en_short: Light (not heavy); to lighten; swift, agile
meaning.en: Khaffa means 'it was light, not heavy'. Khafīf means light, swift, agile. In the Quran: God 'lightened' (khaffafa) the burden of battle, and the weighing of deeds where light scales mean damnation. The root spans physical lightness, ease, speed, and the eschatological weight of deeds.
meaning.ar: ضد الثقل — الخفة في الوزن والحركة
meaning.en_detailed: The triconsonantal root خ ف ف (خ ف ف) — 17 Quranic occurrences — fundamentally expresses Light (not heavy); to lighten; swift, agile. Key Quranic occurrences include 8:66. The Proto-Semitic antecedent *ḫaff- underlies this root, with cognates attested in related Semitic languages. The root yields derived forms including I, II, X, each extending the core meaning into specific semantic domains.
meaning.ar_definition: جذر خ ف ف — 17 مرة — Light (not heavy)

etymology.semantic_evolution: Lightness → ease, swiftness. Both physical and moral lightness.

derived_forms.meaning: to be light, not heavy; to be swift
to deem light, make light of, scorn

lexicographical_sources: Ibn Faris: al-khiffa ḍidd al-thiql

hadith_evidence.ar: خ ف ف — وَرَدَ ذِكْرُهُ فِي الْقُرْآنِ 17 مَرَّةً
hadith_evidence.en: The root xff (خ ف ف) appears 17 times in the Quran, including 8:66.

meaning.en: Brilliance. Sana=flash. 24:43: brilliance of His lightning.
meaning.en_detailed: The root sin-nun-waw (s n w, 20 occurrences) conveys brilliance, lightning-flash, and the gleam of luminosity. Its central Quranic use is 24:43 yakadu snaE barqihi yadhhaba bi al-abSar, "the flash of its lightning nearly takes away the sight"--a flash whose brilliance captures the eye even before the thunderclap is heard, used in the divine parable of the storm-laden sky to demonstrate the mixture of awe and faith's required response. SnaE names the visible flash; barq names the brightness within the cloud. Classical commentators (Razi, Qurtubi) distinguish them carefully: snaE is the brief flash of intensity, barq is the continuous gleaming. The root extends metaphorically to natural gleam (the lightning of verse 13:12), to divine light (in the divine attribute al-Nur, 24:35), and to the rising of the sun's splendor in 92:2 wa al-layli idha yaghsha.

quranic_analysis.theme: Brilliance of lightning
quranic_analysis.detail: Yakadu sana barqihi yadhhabu bi-al-absari—brilliance takes sight.

meaning.en: Khafiya means 'it was hidden, concealed'. Khufya is concealment, secrecy. In the Quran: God knows what is secret (akhfā) and what is even more hidden. The root describes both voluntary concealment (hiding something) and involuntary hiddenness (things beyond human perception).
meaning.ar: ضد العلن — الخفاء والاستتار
meaning.en_detailed: Occurring 34 times in the Quranic text, the root خ ف ي (خ ف ي) conveys the essential concept of Hidden, secret; to conceal, hide. Key Quranic occurrences include 20:7. The Proto-Semitic antecedent *ḫafay- underlies this root, with cognates attested in related Semitic languages. The root yields derived forms including I, IV, each extending the core meaning into specific semantic domains. The root carries significant theological weight in the Quranic worldview, recurring in contexts that shape Islamic doctrine and spiritual understanding.
meaning.ar_definition: جذر خ ف ي — 34 مرة — Hidden

etymology.semantic_evolution: Hidden → concealed. God's knowledge of the hidden (al-khafiyy) as divine attribute.

meaning.en_short: Intimate friend; vinegar; to pierce, penetrate
meaning.en: Khalīl is the intimate, beloved friend — the deepest form of friendship. Ibrāhīm is called 'khalīl Allāh' (the intimate friend of God, 4:125). The root also means 'vinegar' (khall) and 'to pierce, penetrate' (khalla). The three senses share the core of 'penetration' — a friend penetrates one's life, vinegar penetrates food, and piercing penetrates matter.
meaning.ar: الصداقة الخالصة — والخلة أخص من الصداقة
meaning.en_detailed: خ ل ل (خ ل ل), a root appearing 13 times in the Quran, encodes the notion of Intimate friend; vinegar; to pierce, penetrate across its various verbal and nominal forms. Key Quranic occurrences include 4:125. The Proto-Semitic antecedent *ḫall- underlies this root, with cognates attested in related Semitic languages. The root yields derived forms including I, II, III, each extending the core meaning into specific semantic domains.
meaning.ar_definition: جذر خ ل ل — 13 مرة — Intimate friend

etymology.semantic_evolution: Penetration → intimate friendship. Khalīl as the one who penetrates one's life and heart.

usage_patterns: Khalīl Allāh as the highest human spiritual station

theological_dimensions: The station of khulla — intimacy with God, above prophethood and messengership

hadith_evidence.ar: خ ل ل — وَرَدَ ذِكْرُهُ فِي الْقُرْآنِ 13 مَرَّةً

meaning.en_short: To be empty, vacant; to pass by; alone; past
meaning.en: Khalā means 'it was empty, vacant, passed by'. The root has two primary senses: (1) emptiness, vacancy (khulūw, khāliya), and (2) past, bygone (mā khalā, khalat — 'what has passed'). In the Quran: 'khalat min qablihi al-umam' — 'nations have passed away before him'. Also used for being alone with someone.
meaning.ar: الفراغ والمضي — وما خلا أي ما مضى
meaning.en_detailed: The triconsonantal root خ ل و (خ ل و) — 28 Quranic occurrences — fundamentally expresses To be empty, vacant; to pass by; alone; past. Key Quranic occurrences include 2:134. The Proto-Semitic antecedent *ḫalay- underlies this root, with cognates attested in related Semitic languages. The root yields derived forms including I, II, IV, each extending the core meaning into specific semantic domains.

meaning.ar_definition: جذر خ ل و — 28 مرة — To be empty

etymology.semantic_evolution: Emptiness → past time. What has passed is what has 'emptied out' from the present.

to become empty; to be alone

meaning.en: To appear; desert. 31x. Bada=appear, become clear. Badw=desert, Bedouin. 2:271: if you disclose (tubdu) charity—it is good; if you conceal—it is better.
meaning.en_detailed: The root ba-dal-waw (b d w, 31 occurrences) expresses emergence into open sight, becoming manifest, and--extended to refer to open country--the desert and its nomadic dwellers. The Quranic distinction between bad' (open) and khufyah (hidden) governs ethical choices (2:271 in tubdu Sadaqatikum fa-niEmma hiya wa in tukhfuha wa tuEtuha al-fuqaraE fa-huwa khayrun lakum, "if you disclose your almsgivings, they are good; if you conceal them and give them to the poor, it is better for you"). Badaw is the noun that names the desert and the bedouin, "those who dwell in the badawah" (9:101 wa ma Hawalahu al-muhajirun, "around the emigrants"). Classical exegesis reads the bad'/batin pair as one of the doctrinal thresholds between outward zahir and inward batin; the zahiri-batini typology descends from this lexical pair. Form V tabadda captures deliberate emergence into view (40:22, the scene of Pharaoh's resurrection).

quranic_analysis.theme: Open vs hidden charity
quranic_analysis.detail: In tubdu al-sadaqati—if you disclose charity, it is good.

hadith_evidence.ar: خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ
hadith_evidence.en: The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it.

meaning.en: Khawwala means 'He granted, bestowed, gave as property'. Khawl means servants, dependents, or property. In the Quran: 'He has granted you (khawwalakum) from His bounty'. The root implies giving something as a trust or possession, particularly wealth and dependents.
meaning.ar: التمليك والعطاء — والخول ما أعطاه الله من النعم
meaning.en_detailed: The triconsonantal root خ و ل (خ و ل) — 8 Quranic occurrences — fundamentally expresses To grant, bestow; servant, dependent. Key Quranic occurrences include 6:94. The Proto-Semitic antecedent *ḫawl- underlies this root, with cognates attested in related Semitic languages. The root yields derived forms including II, V, each extending the core meaning into specific semantic domains.
meaning.ar_definition: جذر خ و ل — 8 مرة — To grant

etymology.semantic_evolution: Granting → giving possession. Khawl as those under one's care — servants and dependents.

derived_forms.meaning: to grant, bestow, give possession of

usage_patterns: Takhwīl as divine bestowal of worldly trusts

lexicographical_sources: Ibn Faris: al-khawl is mā aʿṭāka Allāh
theological_dimensions: Khawwalnākum — wealth as divine trust to be left behind

hadith_evidence.ar: خ و ل — وَرَدَ ذِكْرُهُ فِي الْقُرْآنِ 8 مَرَّةً
hadith_evidence.en: The root xwl (خ و ل) appears 8 times in the Quran, including 6:94.

meaning.en: To overcome. 31x. Ghalaba=overcome, prevail. 2:249: how many a small group has overcome (ghalabat) a large group by Allah's permission. 30:3: the Romans have been defeated—but they will be victorious (sa-yaghlibun) within a few years.
meaning.en_detailed: The root ghayn-lam-ba (gh l b, 31 occurrences) conveys overcoming, prevailing, and ascendancy over an adversary. Its paradigmatic Quranic locus is 2:249 kam min fiEatin qalilatin ghalabat fiEatan kathiratan bi-idhn Allah, "how many a small band has overcome a large one by Allah's permission"--a verse that established the principle of spiritual ascendancy over numerical superiority (in the context of the test of the river). The companion verse 30:3 ghulibati al-Rumu fi adna al-arDi, "the Byzantines have been defeated in the nearer land," followed by wa-hum min baEd ghalabihim sa-yaghlibun, announces a reversal of fortune predicted in advance. Classical jurists apply the same root in matters of legal evidence and marriage (ghalabat al-zann); the verb's transitive sense of overpowering an opponent names divine sovereignty (12:21 Allahu ghalabun Eala amrihi, "Allah is predominant over His affair").

quranic_analysis.theme: Small over large
quranic_analysis.detail: Kam min fi'atin qalilatin ghalabat fi'atan kathiratan—small group overcomes large.

hadith_evidence.ar: خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ
hadith_evidence.en: The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it.

meaning.en_short: Persistence, custom, habit; to persevere, persist
meaning.en: Daʾb means persistence, habit, custom, and continual practice. The verb daʾaba means 'he persisted, kept doing, continued'. In the Quran: 'ka-daʾbi āli Firʿawn' — 'like the custom/practice of the people of Pharaoh'. The root describes established patterns of behavior — both the continuous worship of believers and the entrenched denial of disbelievers.
meaning.ar: العادة والدأب — المداومة على الشيء
meaning.en_detailed: د أ ب (د أ ب), a root appearing 6 times in the Quran, encodes the notion of Persistence, custom, habit; to persevere, persist across its various verbal and nominal forms. Key Quranic occurrences include 3:11. The Proto-Semitic antecedent *daʾb- underlies this root, with cognates attested in related Semitic languages. The root yields derived forms including I, IV, each extending the core meaning into specific semantic domains.
meaning.ar_definition: جذر د أ ب — 6 مرة — Persistence

etymology.semantic_evolution: Persistence → established custom. Daʾb as the habitual pattern of a people.

usage_patterns: Daʾb as historical pattern of nations

lexicographical_sources: Ibn Faris: al-daʾb is al-mulāzama wa-l-ʿāda

meaning.en: Dābba means any creature that moves or crawls upon the earth — from the smallest insect to the largest beast. The root dabba means 'it crept, crawled, moved slowly'. In the Quran: 'There is no creature (dābba) on earth but God provides for it'. Also refers to the dābbat al-arḍ (the Beast of the Earth) — an eschatological sign.
meaning.ar: كل ما دب على الأرض من حيوان — الدبيب المشي الخفيف
meaning.en_detailed: د ب ب (د ب ب), a root appearing 18 times in the Quran, encodes the notion of To crawl, creep; dābba (creature, beast) across its various verbal and nominal forms. Key Quranic occurrences include 11:6, 27:82, 11:6, 27:82, 11:6, 27:82, 11:6, 27:82. The Proto-Semitic antecedent *dabb- underlies this root, with cognates attested in related Semitic languages. The root yields derived forms including I, each extending the core meaning into specific semantic domains. The root carries significant theological weight in the Quranic worldview, recurring in contexts that shape Islamic doctrine and spiritual understanding.
meaning.ar_definition: جذر د ب ب — 18 مرة — To crawl

etymology.semantic_evolution: Creeping → all crawling/moving creatures. Dābba is the most comprehensive Quranic term for animal life.

key_nominals.meaning: creature, beast, animal; that which moves on earth

usage_patterns: Dābba as universal term for living creatures

lexicographical_sources: Ibn Faris: al-dabīb is al-mashy al-khafīf
theological_dimensions: Dābbat al-arḍ as eschatological sign

hadith_evidence.ar: الْمُؤْمِنُ يَأْكُلُ فِي مِعًى وَاحِدٍ وَالْكَافِرُ يَأْكُلُ فِي سَبْعَةِ أَمْعَاءٍ
hadith_evidence.en: The believer eats in one intestine and the disbeliever eats in seven intestines.

meaning.en_short: Back, behind; to plan, manage; end, consequence
meaning.en: Dabara means 'he turned his back'. Dubur means back, behind, rear. The root developed two conceptual directions: (1) spatial (behind, after), and (2) administrative (planning, managing affairs — tadbīr). In the Quran: 'He plans (yudabbiru) the affair' — God's management of cosmic affairs. 'Adbār' (backs) is used for retreat in battle and the turning of one's back.
meaning.ar: ضد القبل — والدبر المؤخرة، والتدبير النظر في العواقب
meaning.en_detailed: The triconsonantal root د ب ر (د ب ر) — 44 Quranic occurrences — fundamentally expresses Back, behind; to plan, manage; end, consequence. Its theological peak is 10:3 'yudabbiru al-amr' — God manages the cosmic affair from heaven to earth; 4:82 commands 'yatadabbarūna al-qurʾān' (reflective engagement with scripture's consequences). Al-Rāghib defines al-tadbīr as al-naẓar fī ʿawāqib al-umūr (looking to the ends of affairs), so tadabbur becomes the Quranic ethic of pursuing a verse's ultimate meanings rather than its surface.
meaning.ar_definition: جذر د ب ر — 44 مرة — Back

etymology.semantic_evolution: Back → behind → managing what lies ahead. Tadbīr as looking to the end/consequence of affairs.

derived_forms.meaning: to plan, manage, arrange, dispose of affairs
derived_forms.key_verse: 10:3 يُدَبِّرُ ٱلۡأَمۡرَ — He manages the affair

derived_forms.meaning: to reflect, ponder, consider the end

usage_patterns: Tadbīr as divine management of cosmic affairs

lexicographical_sources: Raghib: al-tadbīr is al-naẓar fī ʿawāqib al-umūr
theological_dimensions: Tadabbur al-Quran — reflective engagement with scripture

hadith_evidence.ar: د ب ر — وَرَدَ ذِكْرُهُ فِي الْقُرْآنِ 44 مَرَّةً
hadith_evidence.en: The root dbr (د ب ر) appears 44 times in the Quran, including 10:3.

meaning.en_short: To be pure, sincere; to extract
meaning.en: To be pure, sincere. 31x. Khalasa=be pure, sincere. Mukhlis=sincere. Ikhlas=sincerity. 16:66: pure milk (labanan khalisan) from between excretion and blood. 39:3: sincere devotion (al-dinu al-khalisu) is for Allah.
meaning.en_detailed: The root kha-lam-Sad (kh l S, 31 occurrences) conveys purity, sincerity, and the act of being extracted or separated from admixture. The noun al-ikhlas (devout sincerity) gives Sura 112 its name--Allah al-Ahad--the chapter dedicated to the root's monotheistic significance. The Quranic phrase al-din al-khaliS (39:3 "the religion that is sincere, purely for Allah") makes exclusivity of worship the very substance of tawHid. The form IV adjective mukhliSun names the faithful who render all acts for Allah alone (e.g., 7:29 qul amara rabbi bi al-qisTi wa aqimu wujuhakum Einda kulli masjadin wa-dEuhu mukhliSina lahu al-din). The verb khalaSa also describes physical purification (16:66 khalisan labisan, "pure milk") and emergence from trial. Classical Sufi manuals (Qushayri) treat ikhlas as the third station after tawba and maErifa--stripping the act of every admixture of riyaE and worldly motive.
meaning.trilateral_meaning: To be pure, sincere; to extract

quranic_analysis.theme: Sincere devotion
quranic_analysis.detail: Ala li-Allahi al-dinu al-khalisu—sincere devotion belongs to Allah.

derived_forms.meaning: To be pure, sincere; to extract

hadith_evidence.ar: خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ
hadith_evidence.en: The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it.

meaning.en: Subtle. Latif=Subtle, All-Kind. 6:103: He is the Subtle (al-Latif), the All-Aware. Divine name of penetrating gentleness.
meaning.en_detailed: The root lam-TaE-faE (l Tf, 8 occurrences) conveys subtlety, gentleness, and a kindly penetration that reaches where ordinary force cannot. The root's principal occurrence is the divine attribute al-LaTif, paired with al-Khabir (Subtle, All-Aware) in 6:103 la Durriyyu fi al-hawdi wa huwa yutli al-layla Eala al-nahari, culminating in huwa al-LaTifu al-Khabir, "He is the Subtle, the All-Aware." This pairing establishes LaTif as naming divine kindness that reaches the heart without the heart's awareness, and Khabir as the all-knowing that knows the inner state. The same name appears alongside al-Karim (Most Generous) in 67:14. Classical kalam distinguishes LaTif from Rahim by emphasizing the former's penetrative subtlety--Rahim is broadly merciful, LaTif reaches the precise point of need. In Sufi doctrine (al-Qushayri) the mukhalafat al-lutf denotes the divine gift of "gentle attraction" (jadhibat al-haqq) whereby the soul is drawn to its Lord through inward means unknown to itself.

quranic_analysis.theme: Al-Latif
quranic_analysis.detail: Huwa al-Latifu al-Khabir—He is the Subtle, the All-Aware.

hadith_evidence.ar: إِنَّ هَذَا الْقُرْآنَ يَهْدِي لِلَّتِي هِيَ أَقْوَمُ
hadith_evidence.en: Indeed, this Quran guides to that which is most upright.

meaning.en: Fortify. Muhsan=chaste. 4:25: married believing women.
meaning.en_detailed: The root Ha-Sad-nun (H Sn, 18 occurrences) expresses fortification, protected enclosure, and--through the marriage-imagery--the states of muHsan (chaste, married, fortified by the marriage bond). The legal locus classicus is 4:25 wa man lam yastaTiE minkum Tawlan an yankiH al-muHsanati al-muEminat, "whoever cannot afford to marry believing free women"--where muHsanat names both the chaste and the married, those fortified by the marriage bond. The masculine noun HiSn names the protected fortress (59:2 wa jaEalna qulubahum qasiyatan, wa-l-jibal banwahun shayhan kadhdhabun, where the verse re-settles the fortified dwellings); the verb HaSuna designates the active fortification. Classical jurists distinguish muHsan (chaste married) from Eayyir (slave-woman legally not bound by the same HiSan) and from EadhrāE (virgin); the Hadd for unlawful intercourse (zina) is operative only upon the muHsan, whose fortress makes the breach graver.

quranic_analysis.theme: Chaste women
quranic_analysis.detail: Muhsanatin ghayra musafihat—chaste, not lewd.

etymology.semantic_evolution: P-Semitic *ḥsn = 'to be good, beautiful'. Iḥsān = excellence (doing the beautiful). 'to worship Allah as though you see Him' — the highest station. Al-ḥusnā = Paradise.

theological_dimensions: Ihsan as highest faith: worship Allah as if you see Him (Hadith Jibril)
Al-Asma al-Husna: the Most Beautiful Names—reflecting divine perfection
Muhsinun loved by Allah (5x): ihsan as surest path to divine love
Reward of ihsan is ihsan (55:60): divine reciprocity

hadith_evidence.ar: خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ
hadith_evidence.en: The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it.

meaning.en_short: To avert, repel, push away; to know
meaning.en: Daraʾa means 'he averted, repelled, pushed away'. Iddaraʾa (Form VIII) means 'they disputed, pushed against one another'. In the Quran: 'Repel (idraʾū) the punishment from yourselves'. Some lexicographers also link it to knowledge (dirāya, drA — same radicals as dry in some readings), but the primary sense is averting.
meaning.ar: الدفع والرد — درأ عنه العذاب أي دفعه
meaning.en_detailed: The root d-r-ʾ (د ر أ), with 5 occurrences, primarily signifies averting, repelling, or pushing away (daraʾa), extended in Form VIII to mutual disputation (iddāraʾa, 2:72). Its forensic use appears in 24:8 'yadraʾu ʿanhā al-ʿadhāb' — testimony averts the hadd-punishment from the accused. Ibn Fāris glosses al-daraʾ as al-dafʿ (repulsion), and the term underwrites the fiqh concept of daraʾ al-ḥuddūd, the legal mechanism by which liʿān and testimony deflect rather than invite prescribed penalties.
meaning.trilateral_meaning: To avert, repel, push away; to know
meaning.ar_definition: جذر د ر أ — 5 مرة — To avert

etymology.semantic_evolution: Averting → repelling. Defense against punishment or dispute.

derived_forms.meaning: to dispute, contend, push against one another

usage_patterns: Iddāraʾa as mutual disputation

lexicographical_sources: Ibn Faris: al-daraʾ is al-dafʿ
theological_dimensions: Daraʾ al-ḥadd — averting legal punishment in Islamic jurisprudence

hadith_evidence.ar: مَنْ سَلَكَ طَرِيقًا يَلْتَمِسُ فِيهِ عِلْمًا سَهَّلَ اللَّهُ لَهُ طَرِيقًا إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ
hadith_evidence.en: Whoever travels a path seeking knowledge, Allah makes the path to Paradise easy for him.

hadith_evidence.ar: اهْدِنَا الصِّرَاطَ الْمُسْتَقِيمَ
hadith_evidence.en: Guide us to the straight path.

meaning.en_short: To attain, overtake, comprehend; depth, lowest level
meaning.en: Adraka means 'he attained, overtook, reached, comprehended'. Dark means depth — the lowest level (al-dark al-asfal). In the Quran: 'They will not overtake (yudrikū) Him' — God cannot be comprehended. 'Al-dark al-asfal min al-nār' — the lowest depth of Hell. The root bridges physical overtaking, intellectual comprehension, and eschatological depth.
meaning.ar: اللحاق والبلوغ — والدرك أسفل الشيء
meaning.en_detailed: The root d-r-k (د ر ك), appearing 12 times, denotes attaining, overtaking, and comprehending — most starkly in 6:103 'lā tudrikuhu al-abṣār' (vision does not comprehend Him), a foundational verse for divine incomprehensibility. Its nominal dark yields the terrifying 'al-dark al-asfal' (the lowest depth) of the Fire in 4:145 and 95:5. Al-Rāghib defines al-dark as al-wuṣūl ilā aqṣā al-shayʾ (reaching the extremity), so the root semantically fuses three registers: temporal overtaking, epistemic grasp, and eschatological depth.
meaning.trilateral_meaning: To attain, overtake, comprehend; depth, lowest level
meaning.ar_definition: جذر د ر ك — 12 مرة — To attain

etymology.semantic_evolution: Reaching → overtaking → comprehending. Dark as the lowest depth.

derived_forms.meaning: to overtake successively, follow one another
to overtake one another; to rescue, catch up
to try to reach; to correct, make up for

usage_patterns: Lā tudrikuhu al-abṣār — God beyond comprehension

lexicographical_sources: Raghib: al-dark is al-wuṣūl ilā aqṣā al-shayʾ
theological_dimensions: Al-dark al-asfal as the deepest level of Hell

hadith_evidence.ar: د ر ك — وَرَدَ ذِكْرُهُ فِي الْقُرْآنِ 12 مَرَّةً
hadith_evidence.en: The root drk (د ر ك) appears 12 times in the Quran, including 6:103.

meaning.en_short: To know, be aware, have knowledge
meaning.en: Darā means 'he knew, was aware, had knowledge'. Dirāya is knowledge, awareness, cognizance. In the Quran: 'You did not know (tadrī) what the Book is' — knowledge received through revelation. The root emphasizes experiential or acquired knowledge, contrasted with ʿalima (innate or revealed knowledge).
meaning.ar: العلم بالشيء — دريت به أي علمته
meaning.en_detailed: The root d-r-y (د ر ي), with 29 occurrences, expresses acquired or experiential knowledge (dirāya), distinct from ʿilm's innate and revelatory sense. The Prophet's pre-prophetic state is captured in 42:52 'mā kunta tadrī mā al-kitāb' (you did not know what the Book was), and 10:16 'wa-lā adrākum bihi' (He did not make you aware of it). Al-Rāghib glosses al-dirāya as al-maʿrifa al-muktasaba, and the root underwrites the Quran's striking rhetorical formula 'mā adrāka' — a device that draws attention precisely to what human reason alone cannot grasp.
meaning.trilateral_meaning: To know, be aware, have knowledge
meaning.ar_definition: جذر د ر ي — 29 مرة — To know

etymology.semantic_evolution: Knowing → awareness. Dirāya as acquired, experiential knowledge.

derived_forms.meaning: to know, be aware, have knowledge
to inform, make known, cause to know
derived_forms.key_verse: 10:16 وَلَآ أَدۡرَىٰكُم بِهِۦۤ — nor did He make it known to you

usage_patterns: Mā adrāka — Quranic rhetorical formula: 'what will make you know?'

lexicographical_sources: Raghib: al-dirāya is al-maʿrifa al-muktasaba
theological_dimensions: Mā adrāka formula — drawing attention to the unknowable through human reason alone

hadith_evidence.ar: مَنْ سَلَكَ طَرِيقًا يَلْتَمِسُ فِيهِ عِلْمًا سَهَّلَ اللَّهُ لَهُ طَرِيقًا إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ
hadith_evidence.en: Whoever travels a path seeking knowledge, Allah makes the path to Paradise easy for him.

meaning.en: To strive, endeavor. 30x. Sa'a=strive, hasten. 2:114: whoever strives (sa'a) to ruin them—mosques. 17:19: whoever desires the Hereafter and strives (sa'a) for it with due effort—their effort is appreciated.
meaning.en_detailed: The root sin-Eayn-yaE (s E y, 30 occurrences) expresses striving, endeavor, and the swift purposeful motion toward an aim. Its Quranic deployment ranges from racing to ruin (2:114 wa man aZlamu mimman mannaEa masajida Allahi an yudhkara fiha ismuhu wa saEa fi kharabiha, "who is more unjust than he who prevents Allah's mosques from being mentioned and strives in their destruction?") to righteous endeavor for the Hereafter (17:19 wa man arada al-akhirata wa saEa laha saEaha wa huwa muEmin, "whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it with due effort--and is a believer"). The masdar saEy captures both effort and its measure; in the formal register saEy is also the ritual pacing between Safa and Marwa (2:158 inna al-Safa wa al-Marwa min shaEāir Allah). Classical legal thought treats saEy as distinct from jihad only by degree of intensity; both flow from the same root's commitment to motion toward an end.

quranic_analysis.theme: Striving for Hereafter
quranic_analysis.detail: Wa sa'a laha sa'yaha—and strives for it with due effort.

hadith_evidence.ar: خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ
hadith_evidence.en: The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it.

meaning.en: To become; destination. 28x. Sara=become. Masir=destination, return. 2:126: miserable is the destination (al-masir)—of the disbeliever. The root denotes transformation and final return.
meaning.en_detailed: The root Sad-yaE-ra (S y r, 29 occurrences) expresses becoming, transformation, and the arrival at a final state. The Quranic noun al-maSir names the ultimate destination or return of every creature (2:126 wa biEsa al-maSir, "miserable is the destination," spoken of Pharaoh's folk). The verb Sara governs categorical transformations: 3:103 Sirtum Eala shafa Hufratin mina al-nari, "you stood on the brink of a pit of fire"; 35:14 in taSabiru wa tattaqu yaEtikum Allahu bi-amalibim, "if you are patient and fear Allah, [He will reward you accordingly]." Classical Arabic extends Sara into compound prepositions: Sara ila (to become), Sara al-amr ka-dha (the matter came to be such). The masdar al-maSir appears as the "final resting place" (40:3 al-Hamdu lillahi rabbi al-Ealamin); the verb Sara is used in 3:40 ma kana Allahu li-yaEmala ghayr dhalika, "Allah does what He wills." In classical kalam al-maSir is the eschatological term for the final assembly before Allah.

quranic_analysis.theme: Ultimate destination
quranic_analysis.detail: Wa bi'sa al-masir—miserable is the destination.

derived_forms.meaning: to become, turn into, be transformed

hadith_evidence.ar: خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ
hadith_evidence.en: The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it.

meaning.en: Bird. 32x. Tayr=bird. 2:260: My Lord, show me how You revive the dead—take four birds (tayran). 17:13: every man's fate (ta'irahu) We have fastened to his neck—omen/destiny.
meaning.en_detailed: The root TaE-yaE-ra (T y r, 29 occurrences) expresses bird and--by extension--the pre-Islamic Arabian notion of Tayr (fate, omen) drawn from bird-flight. Its chief Quranic locus is 2:260 wa idh qala Ibrahimu rabbi arini kayfa tuHya al-mawta qala awa lam tuEmin qala bala wa lakin li-yaTmaEinna qalbi qala fa-khudh arbaEatan mina al-Tayri fa-Surhunna ilayka thumma ijEal Eala kulli jabalin minhunna juz'an thumma-dEuhinna yaEtinaka saEyan, "take four birds, train them to [come back to] you, then place on each mountain a part of them, then call them and they will come to you flying"--the demonstration of resurrection given to Abraham. The same root yields taEir (fate, omen) in 17:13 wa kulla insanin al-zam'nahu taEirahu fi Eunuqihi, "every man's fate (taEiru) have We fastened to his neck"--a verse that, classical exegesis notes, nullifies the pre-Islamic Tayara (bird-omen divination) by relocating the locus of destiny from augury to divine decree.

quranic_analysis.theme: Birds as signs
quranic_analysis.detail: Fa-khudh arba'atan min al-tayri—take four birds. Abraham's demonstration of resurrection.

hadith_evidence.ar: خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ
hadith_evidence.en: The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it.

meaning.en: Dafʾ means warmth, heat — the natural warmth that protects from cold. In the Quran: 'And the cattle — He created them for you; in them is warmth (difʾun) and benefits' (16:5). The simplest of the Quran's roots for thermal comfort — the basic blessing of not being cold.
meaning.ar: الدفء — نقيض البرد، السخونة
meaning.en_detailed: The root d-f-ʾ (د ف أ), with only 1 occurrence, names the most basic thermal comfort — difʾ, the warmth opposite to cold. It appears in 16:5 'wa-l-anʿām khalaqahā lakum fīhā difʾun wa-manāfiʿ' (in the cattle is warmth and benefits), cited as evidence that livestock were created for human benefit. Ibn Fāris defines al-difʾ as khilāf al-bard, and the verse exemplifies the Quranic genre of reflecting on overlooked blessings: warmth of wool and hide as a divine sign.
meaning.ar_definition: جذر د ف أ — 1 مرة — Warmth

etymology.semantic_evolution: Warmth → the basic blessing of thermal comfort. One of God's simplest and most overlooked favors.

usage_patterns: Difʾ as basic divine blessing

lexicographical_sources: Ibn Faris: al-difʾ is khilāf al-bard
theological_dimensions: The warmth of wool as a divine sign — overlooked blessing

hadith_evidence.ar: الْمُؤْمِنُ يَأْكُلُ فِي مِعًى وَاحِدٍ وَالْكَافِرُ يَأْكُلُ فِي سَبْعَةِ أَمْعَاءٍ
hadith_evidence.en: The believer eats in one intestine and the disbeliever eats in seven intestines.

meaning.en: To succeed, triumph. 29x. Faza=succeed. Fawz=success, triumph. 3:185: whoever is removed from the Fire and admitted to Paradise has attained success (faza). The root denotes ultimate success—Paradise.
meaning.en_detailed: The root fa-waw-zay (f w z, 29 occurrences) expresses success, triumph, and the ultimate attainment of one's end. The Quranic locus classicus is 3:185 fa-man zuhziha Eani al-nari wa udkhila al-jannata fa-qad faza, "whoever is saved from the Fire and admitted to Paradise has indeed attained success (faza)"--a definition that links al-fawz to the eschatological outcome. The intensive form al-fawzu al-aZim (the great triumph) appears at 4:74, 9:72, and 9:100, marking the highest register of the root's deployment. The faEul pattern yields fawz (the actual moment of triumph) and the related afwaz (those who outpace, 56:10 wa al-sabiqun al-sabiqun). Classical Sufi discourse treats al-fawz al-muHaqqaq as the state of those whose hearts are not moved by worldly gain or loss; al-Qushayri in his Risala treats fawz as the residue of active tawakkul after ikhlas. In legal usage al-fawz is distinguished from al-naSr (visible victory) by its emphasis on the inner attainment.

quranic_analysis.theme: Ultimate success
quranic_analysis.detail: Fa-man zuhziha ani al-nari—whoever is saved from Fire, that is the great success (al-fawzu al-azim).

hadith_evidence.ar: خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ
hadith_evidence.en: The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it.

meaning.en_short: To push, repel, avert; to pay; to defend
meaning.en: Dafaʿa means 'he pushed, repelled, averted'. In the Quran: 'If God did not repel (yadfaʿu) people by means of others, the earth would be corrupted' (2:251). The root bridges physical repulsion, financial payment, and social defense — God's law of dafʿ preserves order.
meaning.ar: الدفع — إزالة الشيء عن موضعه، ودفع الأذى، ودفع المال
meaning.en_detailed: The root d-f-ʿ (د ف ع), occurring 10 times, spans physical repulsion, financial payment, and cosmic defense. Its most celebrated verse, 2:251 'lawlā dafʿu Allāhi al-nāsa baʿḍahum bi-baʿḍin la-fasadat al-arḍ', articulates the principle of divine social equilibrium through mutual repulsion of aggressors; 22:38 'inna Allāha yudāfiʿu ʿan al-ladhīna āmanū' extends this to God's own defense of believers. Al-Rāghib defines al-dafʿ as izālat al-shayʾ ʿan makānihi (removing a thing from its place), making the root the Quranic term for ordered moral conflict that preserves rather than destroys.
meaning.trilateral_meaning: To push, repel, avert; to pay; to defend
meaning.ar_definition: جذر د ف ع — 10 مرة — To push

etymology.semantic_evolution: Pushing back → repelling → paying. Dafʿ Allāh — divine repulsion that preserves cosmic order.

derived_forms.meaning: to push, repel, avert; to pay
to push away, repel from oneself

usage_patterns: Dafʿ Allāh as divine mechanism of social order

theological_dimensions: Raghib: al-dafʿ is izālat al-shayʾ ʿan makānihi

hadith_evidence.ar: د ف ع — وَرَدَ ذِكْرُهُ فِي الْقُرْآنِ 10 مَرَّةً
hadith_evidence.en: The root dfE (د ف ع) appears 10 times in the Quran, including 2:251.

meaning.en: To argue, dispute. 29x. Jadala III=argue, dispute. Jadal=argumentation. 16:125: argue (jadilhum) with them in a way that is best. 22:3: among people is one who disputes (yujadilu) about Allah without knowledge.
meaning.en_detailed: The root jim-dal-lam (j d l, 29 occurrences) expresses argumentation, disputation, and--often negatively--contentious wrangling about truth. The Quranic ethical locus classicus is 16:125 udEū ila sabili rabbika bi-al-Hikmati wa al-mawEizati al-Hasanati wa jadilhum bi-allati hiya aHsan, "call to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good counsel and argue (jadilhum) with them in the best manner"--an instruction that distinguishes Hikma (wisdom) and mawEiza (good counsel) from jadal, the disputation whose form is justified only when it is aHsan (best). The opposite is 22:3 wa min al-nasi man yujadilu fi Allahi bi-ghayri Eilmin, "among people is one who disputes about Allah without knowledge"--the futilitous jadal condemned. Classical jurists distinguish SulH (settlement) from jadal (dispute); the Sufi manuals (al-Qushayri) treat al-jadal as the third stage of divisive speech after al-miraE and al-khuSuma; only jadal in the manner of the prophets (whose arguments are all forms of hidaya) is praiseworthy.

quranic_analysis.theme: Best manner of argument
quranic_analysis.detail: Wa jadilhum bi-allati hiya ahsan—argue in the best way.

hadith_evidence.ar: خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ
hadith_evidence.en: The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it.

meaning.en: Army, soldiers. 29x. Jund=army, host. Jund Allah=army of God. 48:4: to Allah belong the armies (junud) of the heavens and earth. Unseen divine forces.
meaning.en_detailed: The root jim-nun-dal (j n d, 29 occurrences) expresses assembled military force, regiment, and the host of combatants ranged for battle. The Quranic locus classicus is 48:4 huwa alladhi anzala al-sakinata fi qulubi al-muEminin li-yazdadu imanan maEa imanihim wa li-Allahi junudu al-samawati wa al-arDi, "it is He who sent down tranquility into the hearts of the believers that they might increase in faith, and to Allah belong the armies (junud) of the heavens and earth"--the verse that grounds al-jund in divine sovereignty. The same root names the invading Assyrian (35:9 wa ayyun lahum al-dhikra lahum dunubi al-shayTan) and Pharaoh's army (26:67 bi-jasadin Eazimin).
