Occurring 15 times, the root's most famous instance is 3:14 — 'beautified for mankind is love of desires: women, children, heaps of gold and silver, branded horses [al-khayli al-musawwama],' where the muṣawwama horses (well-bred, marked, fat) serve as a symbol of worldly luxury. The same verse's 'pasturage [sawm]' reading (those things that drive one out to graze) reflects the root's pastoral dimension. With the verbal sāma in 4:128 referring to a husband's deserting/estranging his wife, the root's semantic core is the act of marking or directing toward a destination — whether branding, trading, or driving to pasture.
meaning.trilateral_meaning: To brand, mark; to offer for sale; pasturage
meaning.ar_definition: جذر س و م — 15 مرة — To brand

etymology.semantic_evolution: Marking → trading → grazing. The root connects economic and pastoral spheres.

derived_forms.meaning: to offer for sale, drive to pasture

hadith_evidence.ar: س و م — وَرَدَ ذِكْرُهُ فِي الْقُرْآنِ 15 مَرَّةً
hadith_evidence.en: The root swm (س و م) appears 15 times in the Quran, including 3:14.

meaning.en: Orphan. 23x. Yatim=orphan. 93:9: do not oppress the orphan (al-yatima). 2:220: they ask about orphans (al-yatama)—the best is to put their affairs right. The orphan as primary object of Quranic compassion.
meaning.en_detailed: The noun yatīm ('orphan', lit. 'the lone one') derives from the root ي-ت-م and is the central moral category of Quranic social ethics, occurring approximately twenty-three times. Its prohibitive weight is anchored in 93:9, fa-ammā al-yatīma fa-lā taqhar, 'as for the orphan, do not oppress him', where the verb taqhar (from qahara, 'to subdue') sharply prohibits the exploitation of parental-loss vulnerability, and 107:1-3 condemns him who 'drives away the orphan'. The protective maṣdar of the root, itm/aytām, yields detailed legal prescriptions (2:220; 4:2-6, 127) regarding the management of orphans' wealth, and classical fiqh treats yatīm as a perpetual rather than age-bound category until the orphan achieves economic and emotional maturity.

quranic_analysis.theme: Care for orphans
quranic_analysis.detail: Fa-amma al-yatima fa-la taqhar—do not oppress the orphan.

hadith_evidence.ar: أَنَا وَكَافِلُ الْيَتِيمِ فِي الْجَنَّةِ هَكَذَا
hadith_evidence.en: I and the guardian of the orphan will be in Paradise like this.

meaning.en: To pour, pour forth; torrent
meaning.en_detailed: The Arabic root ص ب ب (ص ب ب) appears 5 times in the Quran, governing the semantic domain of To pour, pour forth; torrent. Occurring 5 times total, the root's signature verse is 89:13 — 'your Lord poured [ṣabba] upon them a scourge of punishment' — describing God's destructive assault on the ancient city (variously identified with Lūṭ's people or Madyan) as a torrent descending from above. The semantically related II form ṣabbaba is not Qurʾānic, and the verbal root's scarcity underscores its poetic concentration. Ibn al-Qayyim's description of the root emphasizes downward, cascading motion, conceptually linking physical rainfall (water poured from heaven) to divine punishment (judgment poured upon the wicked). The root thus fuses meteorology with moral causation.
meaning.ar_definition: جذر ص ب ب — 5 مرة — To pour

etymology.semantic_evolution: Pouring → torrent. Ṣabba as the intense downward flow of water or punishment.

hadith_evidence.ar: ص ب ب — وَرَدَ ذِكْرُهُ فِي الْقُرْآنِ 5 مَرَّةً
hadith_evidence.en: The root Sbb (ص ب ب) appears 5 times in the Quran, including 89:13.

meaning.en: Present. 11x. Hadara=be present. 2:133: were you present (kuntum shuhada'a) when Jacob faced death?
meaning.en_detailed: The root ح-ض-ر signifies 'to be present, attend, draw near', yielding the verbal ḥaḍara and a network of derived nominals (ḥuḍūr, ḥāḍirūn, muḥaḍarah). With twenty-five Quranic occurrences, its most legally consequential deployment is in 2:133, am kuntum shuhadāʾa idh ḥaḍara Yaʿqūba al-mawt, 'were you present when death approached Jacob?', a question that establishes eyewitness presence as a precondition for testamentary transmission. The same root appears in 3:25 (fa-hal naẓuruūna illā al-sāʿata an taʾtiyahum baṭatan), ʿilm al-ghayb ('knowledge of the unseen') being God's alone, and in 4:18 (wa-lā taqūlanna li-shayʾin innī fāʿilun dhālika ghadan illā an yashāʾ Allāh), marking divine presence as comprehensive.

quranic_analysis.theme: Witness to death
quranic_analysis.detail: Am kuntum shuhada'a idh hadara Ya'quba al-mawtu—present at Jacob's death.

hadith_evidence.ar: خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ
hadith_evidence.en: The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it.

meaning.en: Companion, associate; to accompany; ṣāḥib
meaning.en_detailed: The Arabic root ص ح ب (ص ح ب) appears 97 times in the Quran, governing the semantic domain of Companion, associate; to accompany; ṣāḥib. The singular ṣāḥib ('companion,' 54 occurrences) and the plural aṣḥāb ('companions, people of,' 43 occurrences) — frequently combined with definite qualifiers (aṣḥāb al-fīl, aṣḥāb al-nār, aṣḥāb al-janna) — designate groups defined by shared history or destiny. The root's most rhetorically pointed use is 53:2 — 'your companion [ṣāḥibukum, the Prophet] has not gone astray, nor erred' — where Muḥammad is defended against Meccan mockery as one who is faithfully intimate with the people. The Form III ṣāḥaba ('to accompany, keep company with,' 5 occurrences) is rarer, but the noun's dominance underscores the Qurʾānic concept of moral solidarity: one is known and judged by one's aṣḥāb.
meaning.ar_definition: جذر ص ح ب — 97 مرة — Companion

etymology.semantic_evolution: Accompanying → companionship. Ṣāḥib as close companion — the Prophet is not 'mad' but a sincere ṣāḥib.

hadith_evidence.ar: ص ح ب — وَرَدَ ذِكْرُهُ فِي الْقُرْآنِ 97 مَرَّةً
hadith_evidence.en: The root SHb (ص ح ب) appears 97 times in the Quran, including 53:2.

meaning.en: Page, sheet, scroll; ṣuḥuf (scriptures)
meaning.en_detailed: The Arabic root ص ح ف (ص ح ف) appears 9 times in the Quran, governing the semantic domain of Page, sheet, scroll; ṣuḥuf (scriptures). The root is reserved in the Qurʾān for sacred writings: 87:18–19 refers to 'this [Qurʾān] is in the earlier scriptures [al-ṣuḥuf al-ūlā], the scriptures of Ibrāhīm and Mūsā,' locating the Qurʾān within a continuous chain of revealed pages. 80:13 ('on pages [ṣuḥufin] honored, exalted, purified') and 98:2 ('a messenger from God reciting pages [ṣuḥuf] purified') similarly elevate the physical medium of scripture. The semantic evolution from raw sheet (papyrus, parchment) to the sanctified 'scrolls of revelation' makes this root a technical term for the original, pre-canonical form of divine communication before codification.
meaning.ar_definition: جذر ص ح ف — 9 مرة — Page

etymology.semantic_evolution: Page → scripture. Ṣuḥuf as the original written form of revelation — the scrolls of Ibrāhīm and Mūsā.

hadith_evidence.ar: ص ح ف — وَرَدَ ذِكْرُهُ فِي الْقُرْآنِ 9 مَرَّةً
hadith_evidence.en: The root SHf (ص ح ف) appears 9 times in the Quran, including 87:18-19.

meaning.en: Beware. 4x. Hadhira=beware. 2:231: fear Allah and know that Allah is Knowing of all things.
meaning.en_detailed: The root ح-ذ-ر (ḥā-dhāl-rāʾ) carries the sense of 'guarding against, beware, take caution', yielding the verb ḥadhira/ḥadhdhara and the intensive Form II haḍḍara. Occurring twenty-one times in the Qurʾān, the verbal noun of caution often appears in proximity to the verb ittaqā (e.g., 2:231, ittaqū Allāha), warning believers that 'whoever heeds caution and piety (man yattaqī)', where haḍhar and ittiqāʾ are functionally linked but lexically distinct: ḥaḍhar connotes active vigilance against a known threat, while taqwā connotes sustained protective piety. In 2:282 the root appears in the witness clause (idhā tadāyantum bi-daynin ilā ajalin musamman fa-ktubūhu), caution against the credit-due in commercial matters.

quranic_analysis.theme: Caution and fear
quranic_analysis.detail: Wa ittaqu Allaha—fear Allah and be cautious.

hadith_evidence.ar: خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ
hadith_evidence.en: The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it.

meaning.en: Dust, soil. 22x. Turab=dust, soil. 2:264: like a rock with dust (turabun) on it—charitable deeds. 3:59: Adam from dust (turab). Human creation from earth.
meaning.en_detailed: The root ت-ر-ب yields the nomen turāb ('dust, dry earth'), etymologically connected with the root t-r-b 'to be dusty, to be impoverished', and produces some twenty-two Quranic occurrences. Its most narratively resonant use is in 3:59, khalaqahu min turābin, 'He created him [Adam] from dust', locating the primordial substance of humanity in dry crumbled earth, a creation from the lowest of materiality before the breathed-in rūḥ. The same noun appears in 22:5 (wa-tarā al-arḍa hāmiyatan fa-idhā anzalnā ʿalayhā al-māʾa idhtāddat wa-rabat), the awakening of dead earth, and in the parable of 2:264 (mithalu mā yunfiqu 'a māla 'alā jibālin turābun) describing the futility of boastful charity.

quranic_analysis.theme: Creation from dust
quranic_analysis.detail: Khalaqahu min turabin—He created him from dust.

hadith_evidence.ar: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنَ الْكُفْرِ وَالْفَقْرِ
hadith_evidence.en: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from disbelief and poverty.

meaning.en_short: To turn away, divert; to dispense, spend; change
meaning.en: To turn away, divert; to dispense, spend; change
meaning.en_detailed: ص ر ف (ص ر ف), a root appearing 30 times in the Quran, encodes the notion of To turn away, divert; to dispense, spend; change across its various verbal and nominal forms. Occurring 30 times, the root's signature theological use is 6:46 — 'see how We diversify [nuṣarrifu] the signs' — presenting the Qurʾān's multiform argumentation as itself a divine sign. Taṣrīf in 6:105 and 6:128 names the varied linguistic and rhetorical presentation of Qurʾānic verses, while Form II also covers 'disbursing' (spending in charity). The verbal network consistently presents human responsibility as response to divine 'turning' (diverting from truth, distributing sustenance, varying the signs).
meaning.trilateral_meaning: To turn away, divert; to dispense, spend; change
meaning.ar_definition: جذر ص ر ف — 30 مرة — To turn away

etymology.semantic_evolution: Turning → diverting → spending. Taṣrīf as the varied presentation of Quranic verses.

derived_forms.meaning: to dispose, manage; to vary, present diversely

hadith_evidence.ar: اهْدِنَا الصِّرَاطَ الْمُسْتَقِيمَ
hadith_evidence.en: Guide us to the straight path.

meaning.en: Defect; one-eyed. 21x. Awar=defect. 24:61: no blame on the blind, lame, sick—or yourselves from eating. The root spans physical defect and the antichrist (Dajjal a'war).
meaning.en_detailed: The root ع-و-ر centers on the concept of 'defect, blemish, missing one eye' (ʿawr), with derived nominal aʿwar ('one-eyed') and defective form. Although the bare root appears in only four verbal occurrences, the lexical family (aʿwar, ʿawrah, etc.) recurs throughout the Qurʾān and hadīth. Its principal Quranic instantiation is 24:61, laysa ʿalā al-aʿmā ḥarajun wa-lā ʿalā al-aʿraj ḥarajun wa-lā ʿalā al-marīḍ ḥarajun, 'no blame lies on the blind, nor the lame, nor the sick', an exemption clause that disables social stigma against the physically impaired. The same root underlies the doctrine of ʿawrah (the uncoverable, the inviolable), though it appears there in 33:13 and 24:58 in its noun-form sense rather than as verbal ʿāwir.

quranic_analysis.theme: No blame on disabled
quranic_analysis.detail: Laysa ala al-a'ma harajun—no hardship on the blind.

hadith_evidence.ar: إِنَّ هَذَا الْقُرْآنَ يَهْدِي لِلَّتِي هِيَ أَقْوَمُ
hadith_evidence.en: Indeed, this Quran guides to that which is most upright.

meaning.en: To ascend, climb; difficulty, hardship
meaning.en_detailed: ص ع د (ص ع د), a root appearing 9 times in the Quran, encodes the notion of To ascend, climb; difficulty, hardship across its various verbal and nominal forms.  Occurring 9 times, the root's defining verse is 72:17 — 'We will make him [the disbeliever] climb [nuṣʿidhu] a mountain of punishment [ṣaʿūdan]' — paired with 74:17, which similarly promises to 'make him scale (saʿūdan) of fire.' The nominal ṣaʿīd ('surface of the earth, elevated ground,' 4 occurrences) appears in 20:12 ('remove your sandals; you are in the sacred valley ṭuwā' and the holy ground') and 5:6 ('wipe your faces and hands with ṣaʿīd,' the surface of the earth, in tayammum). The semantic range thus covers upward motion, exposed ground, and infernal climbing — physical and moral ascent.
meaning.ar_definition: جذر ص ع د — 9 مرة — To ascend

etymology.semantic_evolution: Ascending → difficulty. Ṣaʿūd is a mountain of fire in Hell that the damned must climb.

key_nominals.meaning: ascent, climb; a mountain of fire in Hell
surface of the earth; elevated ground

hadith_evidence.ar: ص ع د — وَرَدَ ذِكْرُهُ فِي الْقُرْآنِ 9 مَرَّةً
hadith_evidence.en: The root SEd (ص ع د) appears 9 times in the Quran, including 72:17.

meaning.en: To remain. 21x. Baqiya=remain. Al-Baqi=the Everlasting. Baqiyyah=remainder. 11:86: the remainder (baqiyyatu) of Allah is better for you.
meaning.en_detailed: The root ب-ق-ي conveys the semantic core of 'remaining, persisting, lasting', and yields the verbal baqiya, the intensive abqā ('to make remain forever'), and the nomen baqiyyah ('remnant, remainder'). Occurring roughly twenty-one times in the Qurʾān, its most ethically pointed use is 11:86, baqiyatu Allāhi khayrun lakum in kuntum muʾminīn, 'what remains from God is better for you, if you are believers', contrasting the fragile surplus of worldly trade with the enduring provision of divine blessing. The same root names one of God's names in classical theology, al-Bāqī ('the Everlasting'), a nomen actionis derived from baqāʾ; the Qurʾān itself uses the predicate kāna baqiyyah (4:78) and abqā (28:60), emphasising the lasting over the transient.

quranic_analysis.theme: Allah's remainder is best
quranic_analysis.detail: Baqiyyatu Allahi khayrun lakum—Allah's remainder is better.

hadith_evidence.ar: خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ
hadith_evidence.en: The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it.

meaning.en: Young man; youth. 21x. Fata=young man. 18:10: the youths (al-fityatu) took refuge in the cave. 21:60: a youth (fatan) called Ibrahim mentions them.
meaning.en_detailed: The root ف-ت-ي denotes a 'young man, youth' (fatā, pl. fityah), with semantic overtones of virility and service; it occurs roughly twenty-one times in the Qurʾān. Its most narratively dense use is in the Cave story, 18:10, idh awā al-fityatu ila al-kahf, 'when the youths took refuge in the cave', a narrative that anchors an entire eschatological framework in the figure of youthful piety fleeing coercive unbelief. The same noun appears in 21:60 (wa-qālū ḥarnā man baʿathanā min marqadinā, qāla fī fatan yudhkurukum) where the word fatan (variant of fatā) marks the prophetic agent invoking them; classical tafsīr (Ṭabarī) traces fatā to the prime of life, and the term suffuses early Islamic political vocabulary (banī Abī Tālib as fityān).

quranic_analysis.theme: Youth of the Cave
quranic_analysis.detail: Idh awa al-fityatu ila al-kahfi—the youths took refuge in the cave.

hadith_evidence.ar: خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ
hadith_evidence.en: The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it.

meaning.en: Thunderbolt; to be stunned, thunderstruck
meaning.en_detailed: The triconsonantal root ص ع ق (ص ع ق) — 11 Quranic occurrences — fundamentally expresses Thunderbolt; to be stunned, thunderstruck. The root names God's 'instant-strike' weapon — His most abrupt intervention: 2:55 records that 'the thunderbolt [al-ṣāʿiqa] seized you while you looked on,' striking the Children of Israel at Sinai for demanding sight of God; 4:153 similarly demands that the People of the Book 'ask not for a sign to be sent down' given the ṣāʿiqa already sent. The semantic evolution from the meteorological thunderbolt (the natural lightning that the Arabs knew) to the divine weapon of instant annihilation makes ṣāʿiqa a synonym for sudden, decisive punishment.
meaning.ar_definition: جذر ص ع ق — 11 مرة — Thunderbolt

etymology.semantic_evolution: Thunderbolt → being struck down. Ṣāʿiqa as the divine weapon of instant death.

hadith_evidence.ar: ص ع ق — وَرَدَ ذِكْرُهُ فِي الْقُرْآنِ 11 مَرَّةً
hadith_evidence.en: The root SEq (ص ع ق) appears 11 times in the Quran, including 2:55.

meaning.en: To conceal. 21x. Katama=hide, conceal. 2:42: do not conceal (la talbisu) the truth while you know. 2:159: those who conceal (yaktumuna) what We sent down—cursed by Allah.
meaning.en_detailed: The Arabic root ك ت م (كَتَمَ) appears 21 times in the Quran, governing the semantic domain of To conceal, hide. Its most polemically charged use is in 2:159, inna alladhīna yaktumūna mā anzalnā mina al-bayyināti wa al-hudā min baʿdi mā bayyannāhu li-n-nāsi fī al-kitāb, 'those who conceal what We have sent down of clear proofs and guidance, after We made it clear for the people in the Book', a verse whose divine curse (laʾanahumu Allāh) falls upon the rabbis who obscured Muhammad's prophecy. The same root appears in 3:71 and 6:91, where the People of the Book are accused of 'twisting words' and 'concealing' the Torah's prophecy of Islam, a verb the Qurʾān reserves almost exclusively for theological concealment rather than mere secrecy.

quranic_analysis.theme: Concealing truth condemned
quranic_analysis.detail: Inna alladhina yaktumuna—those who conceal revelation are cursed.

hadith_evidence.ar: خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ
hadith_evidence.en: The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it.

meaning.en: Small, insignificant; to belittle, scorn
meaning.en_detailed: Occurring 13 times in the Quranic text, the root ص غ ر (ص غ ر) conveys the essential concept of Small, insignificant; to belittle, scorn. Occurring 13 times, the root's morally weighty use is 9:29 — 'fight those who do not believe... until they pay the jizya willingly while they are humbled [wa-hum ṣāghirūn]' — locating ṣaghār in the politics of submission rather than mere size. The abstract ṣighār in 3:178 names the 'humiliation' with which the disbelievers are promised to be disgraced before God. Semantically, ṣaghara preserves the slide from quantitative smallness to qualitative belittlement, with the active belittler (al-mustaṣghirūn) and the humiliated (al-muṣtaghirūn) sharing the same verbal axis.
meaning.ar_definition: جذر ص غ ر — 13 مرة — Small

etymology.semantic_evolution: Smallness → belittlement. Ṣighār as being diminished in status or esteem.

hadith_evidence.ar: ص غ ر — وَرَدَ ذِكْرُهُ فِي الْقُرْآنِ 13 مَرَّةً
hadith_evidence.en: The root Sgr (ص غ ر) appears 13 times in the Quran, including 9:29.

meaning.en: To spread. 21x. Nashara=spread, publish. Nushur=resurrection. 25:40: that is how Allah revives the earth after death—resurrection. 2:259: look at the bones—how We set them then clothe them in flesh (nunshizuha).
meaning.en_detailed: The root ن-ش-ر carries the semantic range of 'spreading out, unfolding, publishing', and by metonymic extension, 'resurrection' as the 'spreading-forth' of the dead from their graves. With roughly twenty-one occurrences, its most theologically charged use is 25:40, wa-qad ʿalimtumā al-nashʾata al-ūlā, 'you already know the first spreading-forth (i.e., first creation)', referring to the resurrection that mirrors the primal unfolding of being. The same root appears in 2:259, fa-unẓur ilā al-ʿiẓāmifa kīfa nunshizuḥā thumma nakussūhā laḥman, 'look at the bones, how We raise them and clothe them with flesh', the verb nunshizu being Form IV causative of nashara. Classical lexicographers connect nashr with the unfolding of a scroll (nashr al-ṣaḥīfah), and Arabic retains nashr to mean 'publication'.

quranic_analysis.theme: Spread/resurrection
quranic_analysis.detail: Kadhallika al-nushur—thus will be the resurrection.

etymology.semantic_evolution: P-Semitic *nšr = 'to spread, disseminate'. Arabic nashara = to spread, publish, resurrect. The nushūr (resurrection) is the 'spreading forth' of the dead from graves. The modern Arabic nashr (publication/publishing) preserves the root.

hadith_evidence.ar: خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ
hadith_evidence.en: The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it.

meaning.en_short: To arrange in rows, rank; row, line
meaning.en: To arrange in rows, rank; row, line
meaning.en_detailed: The Arabic root ص ف ف (ص ف ف) appears 14 times in the Quran, governing the semantic domain of To arrange in rows, rank; row, line. Occurring 14 times, the root's central Qurʾānic instance is 61:4 — 'God loves those who fight in His cause in rows [ṣaffan] as if they were a solid structure [bunyānan marṣūṣ]' — using the architectural metaphor to valorize disciplined communal solidarity. Surah Ṣaff (61) is named from this root. The semantic field spans ordered prayer (ṣufūf in 39:18 describing the rows of those prostrating) and battle formation (ṣufūf in 89:22 referring to the hellfire ranks). The root consistently privileges collective order over individual action, presenting discipline and unity as devotional virtues.
meaning.trilateral_meaning: To arrange in rows, rank; row, line
meaning.ar_definition: جذر ص ف ف — 14 مرة — To arrange in rows

etymology.semantic_evolution: Row → formation. Ṣaff as the ordered line of worshippers or warriors — discipline and unity.

derived_forms.meaning: to arrange in rows, line up

hadith_evidence.ar: ص ف ف — وَرَدَ ذِكْرُهُ فِي الْقُرْآنِ 14 مَرَّةً
hadith_evidence.en: The root Sff (ص ف ف) appears 14 times in the Quran, including 61:4.

meaning.en: Party, faction. 20x. Hizb=party, group. Hizb Allah=party of God. 58:22: those are the party of Allah (hizba Allah)—they are the successful. 5:56: the party of Allah (hizba Allah) is victorious.
meaning.en_detailed: The noun ḥizb ('party, faction, group') derives from the root ح-ز-ب and occurs twenty times in the Qurʾān. Its defining theological use is 58:22, laqad ʿalimta mā lanā fī hizbi Allāh min ḥāliyyin, 'you will find no faction of God failing', paired with 5:56, hizbu Allāhi humu al-muʾminūn, 'the party of God, they are the believers', in which the political vocabulary of faction is sacralised into a binary of divine alignment versus opposition. The same root recurs in 18:12 (wa-awḥaynā ilayhim annahum ḥizbun min al-jibillīn, the seven sleepers being 'a party'), and in 23:51 (yā ayyuhā al-rusulu kulū mina al-ṭayyibāti wa-iʿmalū ṣāliḥan, innī bimā taʿmalūna ʿalīm), the messengers being one party under divine command.

quranic_analysis.theme: Party of Allah
quranic_analysis.detail: Ula'ika hizbu Allah—those are the party of Allah.

hadith_evidence.ar: خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ
hadith_evidence.en: The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it.

meaning.en_short: Pure, clear, chosen; ṣafwat (elite, chosen ones)
meaning.en: Pure, clear, chosen; ṣafwat (elite, chosen ones)
meaning.en_detailed: Occurring 17 times in the Quranic text, the root ص ف و (ص ف و) conveys the essential concept of Pure, clear, chosen; ṣafwat (elite, chosen ones). Occurring 17 times, the root's most theologically decisive verse is 3:33 — 'God chose [iṣṭafā] Adam, Nūḥ, the family of Ibrāhīm, and the family of ʿImrān above all the worlds' — establishing iṣṭifāʾ as the Qurʾānic term for preferential divine selection. The nominal ṣafwa ('elite, chosen ones,' 1 occurrence) and the related muṣṭafā ('chosen') elaborate the semantic core. The evolution from natural purity (ṣafā, 'to be pure, clear') to chosenness reflects the Qurʾānic logic that divine election presupposes purification — God chooses only what He has cleansed. The root is thus central to the theology of prophethood and special divine favor.
meaning.ar_definition: جذر ص ف و — 17 مرة — Pure

etymology.semantic_evolution: Purity → chosenness. Iṣṭafā is divine election — God purifies and chooses His prophets and servants.

hadith_evidence.ar: ص ف و — وَرَدَ ذِكْرُهُ فِي الْقُرْآنِ 17 مَرَّةً
hadith_evidence.en: The root Sfw (ص ف و) appears 17 times in the Quran, including 3:33.

meaning.en_short: Prayer (ṣalāh); to pray, bless; place of prayer
meaning.en: Prayer (ṣalāh); to pray, bless; place of prayer
meaning.en_detailed: The Arabic root ص ل و (ص ل و) appears 99 times in the Quran, governing the semantic domain of Prayer (ṣalāh); to pray, bless; place of prayer. Ṣalāh is the second pillar of Islam, defined in the Qurʾān as the central identifying act of faith: 2:3 names 'those who establish prayer [al-ṣalāh]' among the believers' defining qualities. The semantic core unites human prayer (the believer's devotional address to God) and divine blessing (God's gracious address to the Prophet and the righteous, e.g., 33:56 — 'God and His angels bless [yuṣallūna ʿalā] the Prophet'). The Qurʾān roots ṣalāh in divine command rather than human invention, and its verbal density reflects its ritual centrality.
meaning.ar_definition: جذر ص ل و — 99 مرة — Prayer (ṣalāh)

etymology.semantic_evolution: Prayer → blessing. Ṣalāh as the ritual prayer; ṣalawāt as blessings. One of the most frequent Quranic roots.

derived_forms.meaning: to pray, perform ṣalāh; to bless (God blesses the Prophet)

hadith_evidence.ar: الصَّلَاةُ نُورٌ
hadith_evidence.en: Prayer is light.

meaning.en: Play. 20x. La'iba=play. 6:32: the life of this world is but play and diversion (la'ibun wa lahwun). Worldly life characterized as transient amusement.
meaning.en_detailed: Occurring 20 times in the Quranic text, the root ل ع ب (لَعِبَ) conveys the essential concept of Play, amusement. Its central formulation is 6:32, wa-mā al-ḥayātu al-dunyā illā laʿibun wa-lahwun, 'the life of this world is but play and diversion', a verdict paired in 29:64 and 47:36 with the contrast that this worldly laʿib is 'imitation' of the afterlife's enduring weight. The same root appears in 7:176 (la-ka-'annahu khashībatun mustawfiratun, the donkey carrying books), 5:57 (la-takhūdhannahu wa-mā yakādu), and 62:2, where laʿib and lahīn function as a near-synonymous pair for ephemeral, purposeless activity.

quranic_analysis.theme: Worldly life as play
quranic_analysis.detail: Wa ma al-hayat al-dunya illa la'ibun wa lahwun—this life is play and diversion.

hadith_evidence.ar: خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ
hadith_evidence.en: The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it.

meaning.en_short: To burn, roast; to enter fire (Hell); to warm
meaning.en: To burn, roast; to enter fire (Hell); to warm
meaning.en_detailed: Occurring 25 times in the Quranic text, the root ص ل ي (ص ل ي) conveys the essential concept of To burn, roast; to enter fire (Hell); to warm. The root is reserved almost exclusively for the punishment of the wicked in Hellfire: 92:15 warns that 'none will enter it [yaṣlāhā, the fire] except the most wretched (al-ashqā).' The semantic core is the engulfment of the damned in eternal fire, with the active ṣallayā ('two scorchers') in 55:44 naming the two gardens of Hell. Despite the surface meaning of 'burning,' the root's Qurʾānic usage never describes positive fire (light, warmth) — only the negative fire of divine punishment.
meaning.trilateral_meaning: To burn, roast; to enter fire
meaning.ar_definition: جذر ص ل ي — 25 مرة — To burn

etymology.semantic_evolution: Burning → entering Hell-fire. Taṣliya is being made to enter and burn in Hell.

derived_forms.meaning: to burn; to enter the Fire (Hell)
to cause to burn, make enter Hell

hadith_evidence.ar: اتَّقُوا النَّارَ وَلَوْ بِشِقِّ تَمْرَةٍ
hadith_evidence.en: Save yourselves from the Fire, even with half a date.

meaning.en: To blow. 20x. Nafakha=blow. 15:29: I breathed (nafakhtu) into him of My spirit—Adam. 39:68: the trumpet (al-sur) will be blown (nufikha)—eschatological blast. The root spans divine breathing of life and the trumpet of judgment.
meaning.en_detailed: The root ن-ف-خ (nūn-fāʾ-khāʾ) denotes 'to blow, breathe, puff', and yields both the verbal nafakha and the nomen nafkhan ('a single blow'). Occurring roughly twenty times in the Qurʾān, it spans the two poles of divine breath and eschatological blast. The creative breath of life into Adam is described in 15:29, idh qāla rabbi-ka li-l-malāʾikati innī khāliqun basharan min ṣalṣālin min ḥamāʾin masnūnīn, fa-idhā sawwaytuhu wa-nafakhtu fīhi min rūḥī, 'when I have formed him and breathed into him of My spirit', a creation by divine breath that confers life. The same root serves the eschatological 39:68, wa-nufikha fī al-ṣūri fa-ṣaʿiqa man fī al-samāwāti wa-man fī al-arḍ, 'the trumpet is blown and all in the heavens and earth are struck down', where the noun al-ṣūr names the trumpet itself.
meaning.ar_definition: جذر نَفَخَ — 20 مرة — blow; trumpet blast

quranic_analysis.theme: Trumpet blast
quranic_analysis.detail: Wa nufikha fi al-suri—the trumpet blown. Divine breath of life and death.

hadith_evidence.ar: خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ
hadith_evidence.en: The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it.

meaning.en: Deafness; deaf; to be deaf
meaning.en_detailed: The triconsonantal root ص م م (ص م م) — 15 Quranic occurrences — fundamentally expresses Deafness; deaf; to be deaf. The root's defining verse is 2:18 — 'deaf [ṣummun], dumb, blind — they will not return' — applying all three sensory deprivations to the disbelievers as a trinity of willful spiritual closure. The verbal ṣamma ('to be deaf, refuse to hear') occurs once. Crucially, the Qurʾān's deafness is not physiological but moral-cognitive: 6:39 asks 'is one who is deaf [yuqillu al-samʿ] equal to one who hears?' and 41:44 pairs the deaf with the 'best nation' to whom the Qurʾān is addressed in vain. The root thus becomes a metaphor for the closure of the heart to truth.
meaning.ar_definition: جذر ص م م — 15 مرة — Deafness

etymology.semantic_evolution: Deafness → spiritual deafness. The Quranic deaf are not physically deaf but willfully refusing to hear truth.

derived_forms.meaning: to be deaf, refuse to hear

hadith_evidence.ar: ص م م — وَرَدَ ذِكْرُهُ فِي الْقُرْآنِ 15 مَرَّةً
hadith_evidence.en: The root Smm (ص م م) appears 15 times in the Quran, including 2:18.

meaning.en_short: To form, shape, fashion; image, form; trumpet blast
meaning.en: To form, shape, fashion; image, form; trumpet blast
meaning.en_detailed: Root ص و ر (ص و ر), attested 19 times in the Quran, derives its core meaning of To form, shape, fashion; image, form; trumpet blast from Proto-Semitic sources. With 19 total root occurrences, the root's most celebrated verse is 40:64 — 'He shaped you [ṣawwarakum] and made your shapes excellent [wa-ahṣana ṣuwarakum]' — locating God's creative artistry in the fashioning of human form. The semantic parallel with the trumpet of judgment (al-ṣūr) is striking: 39:68 describes 'the trumpet will be blown [nuḍira fī l-ṣūr] and all in the heavens and earth will fall stunned except whom God wills,' with 6:99 and 18:99 repeating the apocalyptic blast. The root thus unites divine artistry (taṣwīr) with divine summons (al-ṣūr).
meaning.trilateral_meaning: To form, shape, fashion; image, form; trumpet blast
meaning.ar_definition: جذر ص و ر — 19 مرة — To form

etymology.semantic_evolution: Forming → image → trumpet. Ṣūr as the trumpet blown on Judgment Day; taṣwīr as divine fashioning.

hadith_evidence.ar: ص و ر — وَرَدَ ذِكْرُهُ فِي الْقُرْآنِ 19 مَرَّةً
hadith_evidence.en: The root Swr (ص و ر) appears 19 times in the Quran, including 40:64.

meaning.en: To increase; usury. 20x. Riba=usury, interest. 2:275: Allah has permitted trade and forbidden usury (al-riba). 2:276: Allah destroys usury and increases charity (al-sadaqat). The root denotes forbidden increase—exploitation.
meaning.en_detailed: The triconsonantal root ر ب و (رَبَّى) — 20 Quranic occurrences — fundamentally expresses To increase; usury (riba). Its foundational prohibition is 2:275, alladhīna yaʾkulūna al-ribā lā yaqūmūna illā kamā yaqūmu alladhī yatakhabbaṭuhu al-shayṭānu mina al-mass, 'those who consume usury will not stand except as one whom Satan has driven to madness by his touch', a verse whose prohibition is categorically applied. The same root appears in 2:276, Allāh yamḥu al-ribā wa-yurbi al-ṣadaqāt, 'God annihilates usury and increases charity', a verbal pun on yurbi/yambaḥu that places ribā and ṣadaqah in antithetical contrast. Classical fiqh elaborates the prohibition extensively (Mālikī, Shāfiʿī traditions), distinguishing the canonical ribā from legitimate commerce (bayʿ).

quranic_analysis.theme: Prohibition of riba
quranic_analysis.detail: Wa ahalla Allahu al-bay'a wa harrama al-riba—trade permitted, usury forbidden.

hadith_evidence.ar: خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ
hadith_evidence.en: The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it.

meaning.en_short: Shout, cry, scream; ṣayḥa (the Cry, punishment shout)
meaning.en: Shout, cry, scream; ṣayḥa (the Cry, punishment shout)
meaning.en_detailed: ص ي ح (ص ي ح), a root appearing 13 times in the Quran, encodes the notion of Shout, cry, scream; ṣayḥa (the Cry, punishment shout) across its various verbal and nominal forms. The root is reserved for the divine 'sonic weapon' — the single devastating shout that destroys entire nations: 11:67 records that 'the shout [al-ṣayḥa] seized the wrongdoers,' narrating the destruction of Lūṭ's people; 11:94 reports that 'the shout seized [ṣayḥa] the people of Shuʿayb'; and 36:29 mentions 'a single Cry' that silences the doomed. The root's semantic evolution from ordinary human shout to the apocalyptic Punishment Cry (al-ṣayḥa) marks a striking elevation of vocal force into the divine destruction mechanism. The pattern — 'the shout seized' (aḍḥat/al-ṣayḥa aḍḥat) — becomes a stock narrative formula for sudden annihilative punishment.
meaning.ar_definition: جذر ص ي ح — 13 مرة — Shout

etymology.semantic_evolution: Shout → the Eschatological Cry. Al-Ṣayḥa is the sudden, devastating shout that destroys nations — the divine 'sonic weapon'.

key_nominals.meaning: shout, cry, scream; the Punishment Cry

hadith_evidence.ar: ص ي ح — وَرَدَ ذِكْرُهُ فِي الْقُرْآنِ 13 مَرَّةً
hadith_evidence.en: The root SyH (ص ي ح) appears 13 times in the Quran, including 11:67.

meaning.en: To laugh; to mock, deride
meaning.en_detailed: The triconsonantal root ض ح ك (ض ح ك) — 10 Quranic occurrences — fundamentally expresses To laugh; to mock, deride. The root's two principal senses are moral opposites: believers laughing in Paradise (43:71 — 'their faces radiant, laughing') and disbelievers laughing in mockery (e.g., 23:110 — 'you used to laugh at them [taḍḥakūna]' and 53:60 — 'you laugh and do not weep?'). The semantic evolution from natural laughter to derisive mockery and finally to blessed Paradise-laughter makes the root a moral barometer: laughter's character depends entirely on who is laughing, at whom, and in what eschatological setting. The Form IV aḍḥaka ('to cause to laugh') is reserved for divine bestowal of delight.
meaning.ar_definition: جذر ض ح ك — 10 مرة — To laugh

etymology.semantic_evolution: Laughter → mockery. Ḍaḥika as genuine laughter (of believers in Paradise) and as derisive mockery (of disbelievers).

hadith_evidence.ar: ض ح ك — وَرَدَ ذِكْرُهُ فِي الْقُرْآنِ 10 مَرَّةً
hadith_evidence.en: The root DHk (ض ح ك) appears 10 times in the Quran, including 23:110.

meaning.en: City, land. 19x. Balad=city, land. 90:1: I swear by this city (al-balad)—Makkah. 2:126: make this a secure city (baladan aminan)—Abraham's prayer.
meaning.en_detailed: The noun balad ('city, town, settled land') derives from the root ب-ل-د and carries connotations of civilisation, urbanity, and human habitation in contrast to wilderness (sahrāʾ). Occurring roughly nineteen times in the Qurʾān, its most theologically charged use is in 90:1, lā uqsimu bi-hādhā al-balad, 'I swear by this city', an oath whose object is Makkah itself, the sacred precinct of Abraham and Muḥammad. The same noun appears in 2:126, rabbi ijʿal hādhā baladan āminan, 'Lord, make this a city of safety', Abraham's prayer over the sanctuary, and in 4:75 (wa-mā la-kum lā tuqātilūna fī sabīl Allāh wa-lā al-mustaḍʿafīna mina al-rijāli wa-al-nisāʾi wa-al-wildān), where al-balad also denotes territoriality and belonging.

quranic_analysis.theme: This sacred city
quranic_analysis.detail: La uqsimu bi-hadha al-balad—I swear by this city (Makkah).

hadith_evidence.ar: خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ
hadith_evidence.en: The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it.

meaning.en_short: Harm, injury, damage; to harm; necessity
meaning.en: Harm, injury, damage; to harm; necessity
meaning.en_detailed: ض ر ر (ض ر ر), a root appearing 74 times in the Quran, encodes the notion of Harm, injury, damage; to harm; necessity across its various verbal and nominal forms. The root's signature verse is 10:12 — 'when harm [al-ḍurr] touches man, he calls upon Us' — locating ḍurr as the trigger for human supplication. The VIII form iḍṭarra is the basis for the jurisprudential category of ḍarūra ('necessity, emergency'), e.g., 2:173's allowance of forbidden foods 'when one is compelled by necessity [iḍṭurra].' The semantic evolution from physical harm (ḍarar) to legal emergency (ḍarūra) reflects the root's journey from descriptive injury to prescriptive exception — ḍarūra as the legal loophole that transforms prohibition into permission.
meaning.ar_definition: جذر ض ر ر — 74 مرة — Harm

etymology.semantic_evolution: Harm → necessity → emergency. Ḍarar as the spectrum from physical injury to legal necessity (ḍarūra).

derived_forms.meaning: to be compelled, forced by necessity

hadith_evidence.ar: ض ر ر — وَرَدَ ذِكْرُهُ فِي الْقُرْآنِ 74 مَرَّةً
hadith_evidence.en: The root Drr (ض ر ر) appears 74 times in the Quran, including 10:12.

meaning.en_short: To lose, waste, let perish; to neglect
meaning.en: To lose, waste, let perish; to neglect
meaning.en_detailed: Occurring 10 times in the Quranic text, the root ض ي ع (ض ي ع) conveys the essential concept of To lose, waste, let perish; to neglect. Occurring 10 times, the root's defining verse is 18:28 — 'do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance and who follows his desire, and whose affair is ever in neglect [furūṭan]' — using the related furūṭ to depict the moral failure of self-loss. The semantic core is the negligent or willful forfeiture of something entrusted — whether wealth (4:5 — 'do not give the weak-minded [al-sufahāʾ] your wealth'), prayer (19:59 — 'then there came after them successors who neglected [aḍāʿū] prayer'), or the self itself (39:15 — 'he lost [aḍāʿa] himself and his family'). The root consistently treats loss as a moral failure rather than mere accident.
meaning.ar_definition: جذر ض ي ع — 10 مرة — To lose

etymology.semantic_evolution: Losing → wasting → neglecting. Iḍāʿa as the negligent loss of something entrusted.

derived_forms.meaning: to lose, waste, let perish, neglect

hadith_evidence.ar: ض ي ع — وَرَدَ ذِكْرُهُ فِي الْقُرْآنِ 10 مَرَّةً
hadith_evidence.en: The root DyE (ض ي ع) appears 10 times in the Quran, including 18:28.

meaning.en: Narrow, tight, constricted; distress
meaning.en_detailed: Root ض ي ق (ض ي ق), attested 13 times in the Quran, derives its core meaning of Narrow, tight, constricted; distress from Proto-Semitic sources. The root's theological weight lies in its pairing of physical constriction with psychological anguish: 6:125 describes God making one's chest 'tight and constricted [ḍayyiqan ḥarajan]' as the condition of those rejecting faith, while 65:6 warns 'let those who can find accommodation marry, lest God make your means and your offspring narrow [ḍīq].' The semantic evolution flows from literal spatial narrowness to spiritual anguish to socio-economic distress — ḍīq as the antonym of yusra (ease) and the descriptive state of the condemned.
meaning.ar_definition: جذر ض ي ق — 13 مرة — Narrow

etymology.semantic_evolution: Narrowness → distress. Ḍayq as physical constriction and psychological anguish.

hadith_evidence.ar: ض ي ق — وَرَدَ ذِكْرُهُ فِي الْقُرْآنِ 13 مَرَّةً
hadith_evidence.en: The root Dyq (ض ي ق) appears 13 times in the Quran, including 6:125.

meaning.en_short: To seal, stamp, imprint; nature, disposition
meaning.en: To seal, stamp, imprint; nature, disposition
meaning.en_detailed: ط ب ع (ط ب ع), a root appearing 11 times in the Quran, encodes the notion of To seal, stamp, imprint; nature, disposition across its various verbal and nominal forms. The root's defining theological use is 2:7 — 'God has sealed [ṭabaʿa] upon their hearts and upon their hearing, and over their vision is a covering' — locating ṭabʿ as God's punitive response to repeated disbelief. The semantic evolution from physical sealing (closing a letter) to moral imprinting (the heart's acquired nature) makes this root the technical term for the Quranic doctrine of divine hardening of hearts (cf. 4:155; 6:46; 7:100; 9:87). The Qurʾān treats ṭabʿ as the consequence, not the cause, of human rejection — sealing is God's judicial response to the sinner's self-imposed closure to truth.
meaning.ar_definition: جذر ط ب ع — 11 مرة — To seal

etymology.semantic_evolution: Sealing → imprinting. Ṭabaʿa Allāhu ʿalā qulūbihim — God's sealing of disbelievers' hearts as consequence of their choice.

derived_forms.meaning: to be imprinted, take on a nature

hadith_evidence.ar: ط ب ع — وَرَدَ ذِكْرُهُ فِي الْقُرْآنِ 11 مَرَّةً
hadith_evidence.en: The root TbE (ط ب ع) appears 11 times in the Quran, including 2:7.

meaning.en_short: Edge, side, extremity; eye, glance; to look furtively
meaning.en: Edge, side, extremity; eye, glance; to look furtively
meaning.en_detailed: Root ط ر ف (ط ر ف), attested 11 times in the Quran, derives its core meaning of Edge, side, extremity; eye, glance; to look furtively from Proto-Semitic sources. The root's Qurʾānic semantic range covers both spatial edges ('the extremities of the earth') and the eye as the organ of seeing and glancing. The root's moral weight lies in the visual: 24:30 instructs 'tell the believing men to lower their gaze [abṣārihim] and guard their private parts,' and 24:31 commands women to 'lower their gaze and not display their adornment.' The related ṭarfa in 2:65 ('had you seen what We made the sabbath-breakers suffer' — taṭtawwaʿa or ṭarfah) and the edge-image of ṭaraf in 30:41 ('corruption has appeared on land and sea for what the hands of men have earned, that He may make them taste some of what they have done') shows the root consistently moralizing perception.
meaning.ar_definition: جذر ط ر ف — 11 مرة — Edge

etymology.semantic_evolution: Edge → glance. Ṭarf as the corner of the eye — the furtive glance. Also 'edge' of something.

hadith_evidence.ar: ط ر ف — وَرَدَ ذِكْرُهُ فِي الْقُرْآنِ 11 مَرَّةً
hadith_evidence.en: The root Trf (ط ر ف) appears 11 times in the Quran, including 24:30.

meaning.en_short: Path, way; to come by night; ṭāriq (night-comer, piercing star)
meaning.en: Path, way; to come by night; ṭāriq (night-comer, piercing star)
meaning.en_detailed: Occurring 11 times in the Quranic text, the root ط ر ق (ط ر ق) conveys the essential concept of Path, way; to come by night; ṭāriq (night-comer, piercing star). The root's most celebrated use is 86:1–3 — 'by the sky and al-ṭāriq, the piercing star [al-ṭāriq]' — naming surah al-Ṭāriq, where ṭāriq becomes a cosmic symbol of revelation breaking into the darkness of human unknowing. The nominal ṭarīq ('path') occurs in the famous al-ṭarīq verses (e.g., 1:6 'the path of those upon whom You have bestowed favor'), while the verbal ṭaraqa ('to knock at night') frames the ethical instruction of 24:58 — 'children should ask permission [taṣturū] at three times, and those before the dawn prayer.' The semantic core combines night-arrival (as revelation piercing darkness) with path-following (as moral direction).
meaning.ar_definition: جذر ط ر ق — 11 مرة — Path

etymology.semantic_evolution: Path → night-comer. Al-Ṭāriq is the 'piercing star' — that which comes by night. Ṭarīq is the path.

derived_forms.meaning: to come by night; to knock; to travel a path

hadith_evidence.ar: اهْدِنَا الصِّرَاطَ الْمُسْتَقِيمَ
hadith_evidence.en: Guide us to the straight path.

meaning.en_short: To transgress, exceed limits, oppress; ṭughyān
meaning.en: To transgress, exceed limits, oppress; ṭughyān
meaning.en_detailed: ط غ ي (ط غ ي), a root appearing 39 times in the Quran, encodes the notion of To transgress, exceed limits, oppress; ṭughyān across its various verbal and nominal forms. The root's defining narrative use is 79:17 — 'go to Firʿawn — indeed he has transgressed [ṭaghā]' — making ṭughyān the technical term for the tyrant ruler's arrogance. Nūḥ's flood is described (71:11) as water that 'transgressed [ṭaghā] ʿalā,' overflowing beyond all bounds, suggesting the root also names physical as well as moral excess. With ṭughyān as the Qurʾānic synonym for political-religious oppression, the root consistently diagnoses the sin of nations (Pharaoh, ʿĀd, the people of Lūṭ) as exceeding divinely set limits — moral, political, and cosmic.
meaning.ar_definition: جذر ط غ ي — 39 مرة — To transgress

etymology.semantic_evolution: Transgressing → tyranny. Ṭughyān as the arrogant crossing of divine boundaries — the sin of Firʿawn and mighty nations.

hadith_evidence.ar: ط غ ي — وَرَدَ ذِكْرُهُ فِي الْقُرْآنِ 39 مَرَّةً
hadith_evidence.en: The root Tgy (ط غ ي) appears 39 times in the Quran, including 79:17.

meaning.en_short: To rise, appear; to look upon, overlook; dawn
meaning.en: To rise, appear; to look upon, overlook; dawn
meaning.en_detailed: Root ط-ل-ع (ṭ-l-ʿ), 19 occurrences: the semantic core is rising or ascending into view, the emergence of a celestial body or information into perception. Form I ṭalaʿa (4×) names the physical rising of the sun and stars, Form VIII iṭṭalaʿa (6×) the cognitive act of being informed or examining the unseen, and the nominal maṭlaʿ (3×) marks a place of appearance. Key Quranic usage: 18:90 ḥattā idhā balagha maṭliʿa al-shamsi ('until he reached the rising-place of the sun') in the Dhū al-Qarnayn pericope, paired with 18:86's maghrib; 18:17 wa-tarā al-shamsa idhā talaʿat taẓharu ʿan kahfihim (the sun's rising at the Cave of the Sleepers) shows the physical sense, while the iṭṭalaʿa usage in Sūrat al-Kahf acquires the technical meaning of esoteric knowledge ('to be informed of the unseen'). Scholarly precision: Lane distinguishes ṭulūʿ al-shams (astronomical rising) from iṭṭalāʿ (cognitive acquaintance), and Qāmūs and Tāj al-ʿArūs note the root's range in classical Arabic—from the heliacal rising of stars (ṭulūʿ al-nujūm) to being privy to secrets (iṭṭalaʿa ʿalā).
meaning.trilateral_meaning: To rise, appear; to look upon, overlook; dawn
meaning.ar_definition: جذر ط ل ع — 19 مرة — To rise

etymology.semantic_evolution: Rising → looking. Ṭulūʿ as the rising of sun and stars. Iṭṭalāʿa as looking into or being informed of.

derived_forms.meaning: to inform, make known; to cause to rise
to look into, be informed of, examine

hadith_evidence.ar: ط ل ع — وَرَدَ ذِكْرُهُ فِي الْقُرْآنِ 19 مَرَّةً
hadith_evidence.en: The root TlE (ط ل ع) appears 19 times in the Quran, including 18:90.

meaning.en: To establish, empower. 18x. Makkana II=establish firmly. 6:6: We established them (makkannahum) in the earth more than We established you. The root denotes divine empowerment and establishment.
meaning.en_detailed: The triconsonantal root م ك ن (مَكَنَ) — 18 Quranic occurrences — fundamentally expresses To establish, empower (tamkin). Occurring eighteen times, its central use is 6:6, wa-makannāhum fī al-arḍi mā lam numakkin lakum, 'We established them [former peoples] in the earth, in a manner We have not established you', a verse that frames tamkīn as a divine bestowal contingent on moral fidelity. The same Form II appears in 7:10 (wa-laqad makkannākum fī al-arḍi wa-jaʿalnā lakum fīhā maʿāyisha) and 18:84 (wa-makannā lahu fī al-arḍi), where divine strategy equips prophets and nations for civilizational leadership.

quranic_analysis.theme: Divine establishment
quranic_analysis.detail: Makkannahum fi al-ardi—We established them firmly in the earth.

hadith_evidence.ar: خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ
hadith_evidence.en: The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it.

meaning.en_short: To release, set free, divorce; free, unbound
meaning.en: To release, set free, divorce; free, unbound
meaning.en_detailed: Root ط-ل-ق (ṭ-l-q), 23 occurrences: the semantic field clusters around release and consequent freedom, with the specialised juristic sense of ṭalāq as the dissolution of the marriage bond. Form I ṭalaqa (7×) governs both the act of releasing (a captive, an obligation) and the verbal pronouncement of divorce, with the noun ṭalāq (4×) appearing in the codified procedure of Sūrat al-Ṭalāq (chapter 65). Key Quranic usage: 2:229 al-ṭalāqu marratān ('divorce is twice—then retention in kindness or release with generosity') establishes the revocable/revocable/final structure, while 65:1 lays down the legal mechanics of the ʿidda waiting-period, and 4:130 wa-in yatallaqā ('if they separate') rounds out the theme. Scholarly precision: classical fiqh lexicons (al-Jāṣṣāṣ, Ibn Qudāma) derive the noun's marriage-specific meaning by synecdoche—releasing the wife from the conjugal bond is the most consequential form of itlāq; al-Zajjāj notes that ṭalāq in the Qurʾān is exclusively human action (never divine), confirming it as the polar opposite of nikāḥ (marriage).
meaning.trilateral_meaning: To release, set free, divorce; free, unbound
meaning.ar_definition: جذر ط ل ق — 23 مرة — To release

etymology.semantic_evolution: Release → freedom → divorce. Ṭalāq as the dissolution of marriage — a grave but lawful act.

hadith_evidence.ar: ط ل ق — وَرَدَ ذِكْرُهُ فِي الْقُرْآنِ 23 مَرَّةً
hadith_evidence.en: The root Tlq (ط ل ق) appears 23 times in the Quran, including 2:229.

meaning.en: Travel. 13x. Sara=travel. 6:11: travel (siru) through the earth and see what was the end of the deniers.
meaning.en_detailed: The root س-ي-ر (sīn-yāʾ-rāʾ) carries the core sense of 'going, travelling, flowing', and yields both the verbal sāra ('to travel, journey, move') and the nomen sayr ('journey'). With roughly twenty-seven occurrences, its most paradigmatic Quranic use is 6:11, qul sīrū fī al-arḍi thumma unẓurū kayfa kāna ʿāqibatu al-mujrimīn, 'say: travel through the earth and see how was the end of the criminals', a verb whose imperative form invites empirical reflection on the ruins of past peoples. The same root recurs in 30:9 (wa-tarā al-arḍa hāmiyatan fa-idhā anzalnā ʿalayhā al-māʾa idhtāddat wa-rabat), 30:42 (wa-law anna kuffūru ʿan al-jibāl taqallathu bihi al-arḍu), and 22:46, where sayr describes both physical and spiritual motion.

quranic_analysis.theme: Travel and see
quranic_analysis.detail: Qul siru fi al-ardi—say: travel through the earth.

hadith_evidence.ar: السَّفَرُ قِطْعَةٌ مِنَ الْعَذَابِ
hadith_evidence.en: Travel is a portion of torment.

meaning.en: To deputize. 18x. Naba=deputize. Inaba IV=turn to God. Munib=one who turns repentantly. 50:8: insight and reminder for every repentant servant (munib). The root spans deputation and turning to God.
meaning.en_detailed: نَابَ (ن و ب), a root appearing 18 times in the Quran, encodes the notion of To deputize, substitute across its various verbal and nominal forms. Occurring eighteen times in the Qurʾān, the central theological use is 50:8, tabṣīratan wa-dhikrā li-kulli ʿabdin munīb, 'insight and reminder for every servant who turns [to God]', where munīb denotes the constant, habitual returner to God. Classical tafsīr distinguishes munīb (one who turns repeatedly) from tāʾib (one who repents from sin), the former connotes a permanent disposition of turning-toward-God while the latter connotes a moment of repentance from transgression. The same root appears in 11:75, 13:27, and 39:17 describing the receptive believer.

quranic_analysis.theme: Turning to God
quranic_analysis.detail: Tabhiratan wa dhikra li-kulli abdin munib—for every repentant servant.

hadith_evidence.ar: خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ
hadith_evidence.en: The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it.

meaning.en_short: To hope, covet, aspire; greed; expectation
meaning.en: To hope, covet, aspire; greed; expectation
meaning.en_detailed: Root ط-م-ع (ṭ-m-ʿ), 12 occurrences: the semantic core is intense yearning (ḥarīṣ al-nafs), ranging from legitimate hope for divine mercy to blameworthy covetousness for worldly gain. Form I ṭamiʿa (8×) denotes the soul's stretching toward a target, and the noun ṭamaʿ (4×) carries a pejorative overtone in the Qurʾān (Lisān al-ʿArab: aṭmaʿahu aḥraqahu—coveting consumes). Key Quranic usage: 7:46 lam yadkhulūhā wa-hum yaṭmaʿūna (the people of the Heights longing to enter Paradise while barred from it), 70:19–22 describes the covetous human as manūʿ (niggardly when graced), and 17:18 contrasts those who desire the immediate (al-ʿājila) with those who seek the eternal. Scholarly precision: al-Rāghib differentiates ṭamaʿ (covetous hope, blameworthy) from rajāʾ (hopeful expectation, praiseworthy)—the first stretches toward that whose attainment is uncertain, the second toward that which is promised; al-Qurṭubī notes the root pairs naturally with khashya (hope of fear) in ethical discourse, while the hadith echoes al-ṭamaʿ al-fāḍil a partial recompense in 9:79. The form yaṭmaʿūna in 7:46 is sometimes rendered 'coveting' in translation but al-Ṭabarī glosses it as 'longing expectantly' (tarajjī).
meaning.trilateral_meaning: To hope, covet, aspire; greed; expectation
meaning.ar_definition: جذر ط م ع — 12 مرة — To hope

etymology.semantic_evolution: Hoping → coveting. Ṭamaʿa as eager desire — can be positive (hope in God) or negative (greed for worldly gain).

hadith_evidence.ar: ط م ع — وَرَدَ ذِكْرُهُ فِي الْقُرْآنِ 12 مَرَّةً
hadith_evidence.en: The root TmE (ط م ع) appears 12 times in the Quran, including 7:46.

meaning.en: To dispute. 18x. Khasima=dispute. Khasm=opponent, adversary. 2:204: the most quarrelsome opponent (aladdu al-khisam). 4:105: do not be an advocate for the treacherous. The root denotes adversarial argument.
meaning.en_detailed: The Arabic root خ ص م (خَصِمَ) appears 18 times in the Quran, governing the semantic domain of To dispute, litigate. With eighteen occurrences, its most theologically diagnostic use is 2:204, wa-huwa aladdu al-khiṣām, 'he is the fiercest of adversaries', a phrase describing the munāfiqūn (hypocrites) whose combative litigiousness exceeds that of ordinary enemies. The same root appears in 4:105 (innā anzalnā ilayka al-kitāba bi-l-ḥaqqi li-taḥkuma bayna al-nāsi bimā arāka Allāh), in 4:113 (wa-law lā fadlu Allāhi ʿalayka wa-raḥmatuhu la-hāmat ṭāʾifatun minhum an yuḍillūka), and 39:31, where the verb connotes hostile contestation rather than lawful judicial contention (which uses ḥāka-ma and qaḍā).

quranic_analysis.theme: Quarrelsome opponent
quranic_analysis.detail: Wa huwa aladdu al-khisam—he is the most fierce in dispute.

hadith_evidence.ar: خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ
hadith_evidence.en: The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it.

meaning.en_short: To be pure, clean; purification; ṭahāra (ritual purity)
meaning.en: To be pure, clean; purification; ṭahāra (ritual purity)
meaning.en_detailed: Root ط-ه-ر (ṭ-h-r), 31 occurrences: the semantic core is purification, encompassing physical cleanliness, ritual ṭahāra, and the spiritual state of being cleansed from sin. Form II ṭahhara (13×) is the causative purification (divine or human), Form V taṭahhara (8×) the reflexive striving to purify oneself, and the noun ṭahūr (1×, in 9:108) names the purifying agent; the active muṭahhar (purified, 2×) names the cleansed state. Key Quranic usage: 2:222 inna Allāha yuḥibbu al-tawwābīn wa-yuḥibbu al-muṭahhirīn ('God loves those who repent and those who purify themselves'); 5:6 lays down the wuḍūʾ ablution in connection with worship; 9:108 praises the mosque founded upon taqwā as the dwelling of men who love to yuṭahharū. Scholarly precision: Lane traces the bifurcation between ẓāhiri (external) and bāṭinī (internal) ṭahāra; classical tafsīr (al-Ṭabarī, al-Qurṭubī) takes 2:222's muṭahhirīn to mean those who cleanse themselves from sin (taṭahhur ʿan al-maʿāṣī), while Abū Ḥayyān notes 9:108 is the verse in which the root is most explicitly a divine love-object—equating taṭahhur with taqwā.
meaning.ar_definition: جذر ط ه ر — 31 مرة — To be pure

etymology.semantic_evolution: Purity → ritual purity. Ṭahāra as both spiritual and physical cleansing — central to Islamic ritual.

hadith_evidence.ar: الطُّهُورُ شَطْرُ الْإِيمَانِ
hadith_evidence.en: Purity is half of faith.

meaning.en: To return, repent. 17x. Aba=return. Awwab=oft-returning (to God). 38:30: excellent servant—David was awwab (always returning). 38:44: Job—patient servant, awwab.
meaning.en_detailed: أَوَبَ (أ و ب), a root appearing 17 times in the Quran, encodes the notion of To return, repent across its various verbal and nominal forms. Occurring seventeen times, its paradigmatic use is 38:30, wa-waḥabnā li-Dāwūda Sulaymāna niʿma al-ʿabdu innahu awwābun, 'and We gave to David Solomon; excellent servant, for he was awwāb', where the polygenous active form signals constant, reiterated return to God. The same root appears in 38:44, describing Job as awwāb and patient, and 38:17 concerning David himself; classical Sufi tafsīr (Sahl al-Tustarī, al-Qushayrī) interprets awwāb as the servant who returns constantly between fear and hope, while ānibīn in 4:146 names those who turn (to God) repeatedly.

quranic_analysis.theme: Awwab: oft-returning
quranic_analysis.detail: Ni'ma al-abdu innahu awwabun—excellent servant, always returning.

hadith_evidence.ar: التَّائِبُ مِنَ الذَّنْبِ كَمَنْ لَا ذَنْبَ لَهُ
hadith_evidence.en: The one who repents from sin is like one who has no sin.

meaning.en: Mountain (ṭūr); stage, phase; Ṭūr Sīnā
meaning.en_detailed: Root ط-و-ر (ṭ-w-r), 11 occurrences: the root, a non-verbal noun, denotes a mountain, with particular Quranic resonance as Ṭūr Sīnāʾ—the sacred elevation of revelation to Mūsā. The single noun ṭūr (11×) appears as a marker of divine theophany, paired with sīnāʾ/sīnīn as a topographic and covenantal sign. Key Quranic usage: 23:20 wa-shajaratin takhruju min Ṭūri Saynāʾ (the olive tree of Mount Sinai, near Tuwā); 95:2 wa-ṭūri sīnīn; 52:1 wa-l-ṭūri; 4:154/2:63 recall al-Ṭūr as the place where God raised the mount over Banū Isrāʾīl (wa-rafaʿnā fawqahum al-ṭūr). Scholarly precision: classical geographers (al-Maqrīzī, Yāqūt) debate whether ṭūr is generic (any elevated massif) or proper (Sinai specifically); Lisān al-ʿArab and al-Rāghib treat it as both, with the Qurʾān favouring the proper sense in four Ṭūr Sīnāʾ references and the generic in others. The Ṭūr in Sūrat al-Ṭūr (52) is paired with kitāb masṭūr (52:2)—the inscribed book of revelation, suggesting the mountain itself is a locus of divine inscription.
meaning.ar_definition: جذر ط و ر — 11 مرة — Mountain (ṭūr)

etymology.semantic_evolution: Mountain → the mountain of revelation. Ṭūr Sīnāʾ as the sacred mountain where God spoke to Mūsā.

hadith_evidence.ar: ط و ر — وَرَدَ ذِكْرُهُ فِي الْقُرْآنِ 11 مَرَّةً
hadith_evidence.en: The root Twr (ط و ر) appears 11 times in the Quran, including 23:20.

meaning.en_short: To go around, circumambulate; ṭawāf; flood (ṭūfān)
meaning.en: To go around, circumambulate; ṭawāf; flood (ṭūfān)
meaning.en_detailed: Root ط-و-ف (ṭ-w-f), 41 occurrences: the semantic core is circular movement around a centre, from which it branches into ritual circumambulation (ṭawāf), the overwhelming encircling flood (ṭūfān), and the specter/nightmare visitor (ṭāʾif) that comes round about a sleeper. Form I ṭāfa (20×) and Form II taṭawwafa govern the sacred circumambulation of the Kaʿba; key Quranic usage: 22:29 thumma li-yaṭṭawwafū ʿalā al-bayti al-ʿatīq (the canonical ṭawāf verse, 'let them circumambulate the Ancient House'), 2:125 with al-ṭāʾifīn/al-ʿākifīn, while 7:133 fa-arsalnā ʿalayhim al-ṭūfāna describes the deluge that drowned Pharaoh's hosts, and the ṭāʾif verses (7:201, 23:97, 4:103) describe the whispering suggestions of spirits approaching the believer. Scholarly precision: Lisān al-ʿArab identifies ṭawāf as the earthly echo of the angels' circling (ṭawāf al-malāʾika) around the ʿArsh (Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim); the semantic bifurcation ṭawāf/ṭūfān is reconciled by Lane as two aspects of one encircling motion—ritual versus overwhelming.
meaning.ar_definition: جذر ط و ف — 41 مرة — To go around

etymology.semantic_evolution: Going around → circumambulation → flood. Ṭawāf as the ritual circling of the Kaʿba; ṭūfān as the overwhelming flood.

key_nominals.meaning: that which goes around; specter, nightmare visitor

hadith_evidence.ar: ط و ف — وَرَدَ ذِكْرُهُ فِي الْقُرْآنِ 41 مَرَّةً
hadith_evidence.en: The root Twf (ط و ف) appears 41 times in the Quran, including 22:29.

meaning.en: Good, pleasant, pure; ṭayyib (wholesome, lawful)
meaning.en_detailed: Root ط-ي-ب (ṭ-y-b), 50 occurrences: the semantic core is goodness in its concrete sensory, moral, and legal dimensions, with ṭayyib functioning as the moral category of what is wholesome, fragrant, and divinely sanctioned—the antithesis of khabīth. Form I ṭāba (12×) expresses intrinsic goodness or natural agreeableness, Form II ṭayyaba (1×) the act of making wholesome; the noun ṭayyib (41×) is the dominant form, often paired with its opposite khabīth. Key Quranic usage: 2:168 yā ayyuhā al-nāsu kulū mimmā fī al-arḍi ḥalālan ṭayyiban ('O mankind, eat of the earth's produce, lawful and wholesome'); 7:157 yuḥillu lahum al-ṭayyibāt wa-yuḥarrimu ʿalayhim al-khabāʾith ('He permits them the wholesome and forbids them the foul'); 5:5 lists ṭayyibāt of food and marriage with women of the book. Scholarly precision: al-Rāghib distinguishes three sub-senses of ṭayyib—physical (clean food), ethical (good deeds), and spiritual (ṣāliḥ/nāfiʿ); al-Zamakhsharī notes the legal-technical usage in which ṭayyib wa ṭāhir collapses into ḥalāl and into ritual purity (ṭāhir), and the Qurʾān itself blurs these registers in 5:6/9:108.
meaning.ar_definition: جذر ط ي ب — 50 مرة — Good

etymology.semantic_evolution: Goodness → wholesomeness → lawful. Al-Ṭayyib as the divinely approved — opposite of khabīth (foul).

hadith_evidence.ar: إِنَّ اللَّهَ طَيِّبٌ لَا يَقْبَلُ إِلَّا طَيِّبًا
hadith_evidence.en: Allah is pure and accepts only what is pure.

meaning.en: Easy. 45x. Yusra=ease. 94:5: indeed with hardship comes ease (yusran).
meaning.en_detailed: Root ي س ر (يَسُرَ), attested 44 times in the Quran, derives its core meaning of To be easy; left side from Proto-Semitic sources. Its most quoted verse is 94:5, fa-inna maʿa al-ʿusri yusrā, 'indeed with hardship comes ease', a doubled assertion in 94:6 that 'with every hardship comes ease', establishing the principle that ease is structurally consequent to hardship. The same root appears in 92:7 (fa-annā la-hu al-isrā, the question of what will make him know the nature of the steep ascent), in the verb yassara ('to make easy', 87:8; 80:20), and the negative 'usr in 65:7, the verses forming the theological cornerstone of hopeful endurance in Islam.

quranic_analysis.theme: With hardship, ease
quranic_analysis.detail: Fa-inna ma'a al-'usri yusra—with hardship comes ease.

hadith_evidence.ar: خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ
hadith_evidence.en: The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it.

meaning.en: Clay, mud; ṭīn (clay, earth)
meaning.en_detailed: Root ط-ي-ن (ṭ-y-n), 12 occurrences: a non-verbal noun root naming clay/mud, the primordial matter of human creation. The single noun ṭīn (12×) clusters in the creation narratives as the substance from which God shaped Ādam. Key Quranic usage: 7:12 khalaqtanī min nārin wa-khalaqtahu min ṭīnin (Iblīs' boast to God: 'You created me from fire and created him from clay'); 32:7 badāʾa khilqata al-insāna min ṭīnin ('He began the creation of man from clay'); 15:26 wa-la-qad khalaqnā al-insāna min ṭīnin; 23:12 wa-la-qad khalaqnā al-insāna min sulālatin min ṭīnin. Scholarly precision: classical lexicographers (al-Rāghib, al-Zajjāj) frame ṭīn as moist mouldable earth, distinguished from ʿarḍ (dry earth, in 30:20), turāb (loose dust, in 30:20), and ṣalṣāl (dry ringing clay, 55:14); al-Qurṭubī connects the root to tīn al-khazafī (potter's clay) and notes the theological implication of human humility—the ṭīn origin as the rationale for the mercy (raḥma) God shows fallen progeny.
meaning.ar_definition: جذر ط ي ن — 12 مرة — Clay

etymology.semantic_evolution: Clay → earth. The primordial substance from which humans were created.

hadith_evidence.ar: ط ي ن — وَرَدَ ذِكْرُهُ فِي الْقُرْآنِ 12 مَرَّةً
hadith_evidence.en: The root Tyn (ط ي ن) appears 12 times in the Quran, including 7:12.

meaning.en: To cross; tears; lesson. 12x. Abara=cross. Ibrah=warning lesson. Abrah=tear. 12:84: his eyes whitened from sorrow—withheld tears. 59:2: take a lesson (fa'tabiru) O people of vision.
meaning.en_detailed: The triconsonantal root ع ب ر (عَبَرَ) — 9 Quranic occurrences — fundamentally expresses To cross; tears; lesson (ibrah). The verb ʿabara and its derived noun ʿibrah appear in the Qur'an both as a noun (lesson, warning) and in the imperative form. A striking imperative is 59:2, "fa-ʿtabirū yā ulī al-abṣār"—take lesson, O people of vision—inviting reflection upon the Banū al-Naḍīr's expulsion. At 12:84 the verb describes Yaʿqūb's eyes turning white from "sorrow that he restrained" (min al-ḥuzni alladhī ʿaḥṣana—yet he withheld his tears, ʿubārah). Occurs 9 times in the Qur'an. The semantic field connects physical crossing, the flowing of tears, and the intellectual extraction of moral meaning—a triad unique to this triliteral.

quranic_analysis.theme: Taking lessons
quranic_analysis.detail: Fa'tabiru ya uli al-absar—take a lesson, O people of vision.

hadith_evidence.ar: إِنَّ هَذَا الْقُرْآنَ يَهْدِي لِلَّتِي هِيَ أَقْوَمُ
hadith_evidence.en: Indeed, this Quran guides to that which is most upright.

meaning.en_short: To remain, continue, keep doing; shade, shadow (ẓill)
meaning.en: To remain, continue, keep doing; shade, shadow (ẓill)
meaning.en_detailed: Root ظ-ل-ل (ẓ-l-l), 33 occurrences: the semantic core bifurcates between temporal continuation (the verb ẓalla 'kept doing, remained') and the physical reality of shade (ẓill); both senses share the notion of persistent presence, whether temporal or spatial. Form I ẓalla (29×) carries the function of indicating durative/continuous action in past tense (al-ḍumūr al-mutawaṣṣil); the noun ẓill (9×) names shadow or shade, both literal and metaphorical. Key Quranic usage: 25:45 al-lam tara ilā rabbika kayfa madda al-ẓilla wa-law shāʾa la-jaʿalahu sākinan ('Have you not seen how your Lord extends the shade? If He willed, He could have made it still'); 56:30 wa-ẓillin mamdūdin ('extended shade' of Paradise); 7:171 wa-iḍ nāṭaqnā al-jibāla fawqahum ẓillan (the shadow of Sinai raised over Banū Isrāʾīl); 4:57 ẓululan mamdūdah. Scholarly precision: al-Zamakhsharī and Sibawayh note that ẓalla in ẓalla yafʿalu is a defective verb (jāʾiz/ʿāmil) whose grammatical role is purely aspectual/continuous; in classical Arabic it is closely parallel to mā zāla, with the shade meaning being a homonymous semantic branch (Lane, s.v.).
meaning.trilateral_meaning: To remain, continue, keep doing; shade, shadow
meaning.ar_definition: جذر ظ ل ل — 33 مرة — To remain

etymology.semantic_evolution: Continuation → shade. Ẓalla means both 'he remained, kept doing' and 'shade' — the constant companion of the desert traveler.

hadith_evidence.ar: ظ ل ل — وَرَدَ ذِكْرُهُ فِي الْقُرْآنِ 33 مَرَّةً
hadith_evidence.en: The root Zll (ظ ل ل) appears 33 times in the Quran, including 25:45.

meaning.en: To return; incur. 17x. Ba'a=return. 2:90: they incurred (ba'u) wrath upon wrath. 5:29: I would rather you bear (tabu'a) my sin and yours.
meaning.en_detailed: بَاءَ (ب و أ), a root appearing 17 times in the Quran, encodes the notion of To return; to incur (wrath) across its various verbal and nominal forms. The verb bāʾa bi- takes a direct object, yielding the sense of self-incurred punishment. At 2:90, "fa-bāʾū bi-ghaḍabin ʿalā ghaḍabin"—they incurred wrath upon wrath—describes the Children of Israel's cumulative sin. At 5:29, "yaqūlū a-takuffuru wa tabūʾū bi-ithmī wa ithmikum"—I would rather you bear my sin and yours, in Hābīl's hypothetical. Occurs 17 times in the Qur'an. The verbal noun baʾīʾ (destroyer) also appears at 2:192, intensifying the active sense of self-destruction through wrongdoing. The root semantically pairs with khaṭīʾah (sin) and ʿiqāb (punishment).

quranic_analysis.theme: Incurring divine wrath
quranic_analysis.detail: Fa-ba'u bi-ghadabin ala ghadabin—they incurred wrath upon wrath.

hadith_evidence.ar: لَا تَغْضَبْ وَلَكَ الْجَنَّةُ
hadith_evidence.en: Do not become angry, and Paradise is yours.

meaning.en_short: To think, suppose, conjecture; ẓann (opinion, suspicion)
meaning.en: To think, suppose, conjecture; ẓann (opinion, suspicion)
meaning.en_detailed: Root ظ-ن-ن (ẓ-n-n), 69 occurrences: the semantic core is thinking/assumptive cognition, with ẓann spanning neutral thought (opinion), tentative conjecture, and blameworthy suspicion. Form I ẓanna (62×) is the dominant form, governing belief-states from near-certainty to presumptive inference; the noun ẓann (7×) is the most ethically loaded—ranging from lawful supposition to sin. Key Quranic usage: 49:12 yā ayyuhā alladhīna āmanū ajtanibū kathīran mina al-ẓanni inna baʿḍa al-ẓanni ithm ('O you who believe, avoid much suspicion—indeed some suspicion is sin'); 2:78 wa-mā hum illā yaẓunnūna ('they think [they know], but they do not'); 3:154 ẓanantum anna lan yanqaliba al-rasūlu. Scholarly precision: al-Rāghib distinguishes four sub-senses—yaqīn (certainty), ẓann (over 50% probability), shakk (under 50%), and wahm (baseless fancy)—with the Qurʾān often contrasting ẓann with yaqīn to undermine the cognitive pretensions of kufr; the prophetic ḥadīth 'al-ẓannu akdhabu al-ḥadīth' (Bukhārī) reflects the Qurʾānic semantic polemic against unfounded conjecture.
meaning.ar_definition: جذر ظ ن ن — 69 مرة — To think

etymology.semantic_evolution: Thinking → suspicion. Ẓann bridges neutral thought, negative suspicion, and the sin of assuming without knowledge.

hadith_evidence.ar: ظ ن ن — وَرَدَ ذِكْرُهُ فِي الْقُرْآنِ 69 مَرَّةً
hadith_evidence.en: The root Znn (ظ ن ن) appears 69 times in the Quran, including 49:12.

meaning.en_short: To blame, reproach; threshold; repentance, returning
meaning.en: To blame, reproach; threshold; repentance, returning
meaning.en_detailed: Root ع-ت-ب (ʿ-t-b), 5 occurrences: the root gathers the cognate senses of reproach, threshold, and turning away, with the semantic drift running from 'reproaching one who has erred' to 'the door-step where one turns back'. The noun ʿitāb (2×) names blame/reproach, with the secondary sense of 'threshold' attaching to a rarer nominal form. Key Quranic usage: 18:73 qāla lā tuʾākhidhnī bimā nasītu wa-lā turhiqnī fī amrī ʿusran ('Do not blame me for what I forgot'), Mūsā to al-Khiḍr in the pericope of Sūrat al-Kahf, where ʿitāb is implicit in tuʾākhidh, and the verbal cluster ʿitāb recurs in the narrative of covenantal rebuke; classical commentators also note ʿataba in the sense of 'turning away from' which colors the meaning. Scholarly precision: Lisān al-ʿArab (s.v. ʿ-t-b) records that the original sense is 'gentle reproach with one's hand', from the action of touching and pushing back at the door-threshold; al-Zamakhsharī distinguishes ʿitāb (blame) from ʿiqāb (punishment) by the moral gravity of the latter, the former being corrective rather than retributive—a distinction al-Rāghib maintains in his Mufradāt.
meaning.trilateral_meaning: To blame, reproach; threshold; repentance, returning
meaning.ar_definition: جذر ع ت ب — 5 مرة — To blame

etymology.semantic_evolution: Blame → threshold → returning. ʿItāb as gentle reproach; ʿataba as the doorstep where one turns back.

derived_forms.meaning: To blame, reproach; threshold; repentance, returning

hadith_evidence.ar: التَّائِبُ مِنَ الذَّنْبِ كَمَنْ لَا ذَنْبَ لَهُ
hadith_evidence.en: The one who repents from sin is like one who has no sin.

meaning.en: Just. 30x. Adala=be just. Adl=justice. 4:58: when you judge between people, judge with justice (bi-al-adli).
meaning.en_detailed: عَدَلَ (ع د ل), a root appearing 28 times in the Quran, encodes the notion of To be just, equitable (adl) across its various verbal and nominal forms. The verb ʿadala means to act justly or equitably, while the noun ʿadl denotes justice as the proper mean. At 4:58, "idhā ḥakamtum bayna al-nāsi an taḥkumū bi-l-ʿadl"—when you judge between people, judge with justice—is one of the most quoted judicial principles of the Qur'an. The ʿaṣ-ṣirāṭ al-mustaqīm (the straight path) is the lexically-balanced mean (taʿdīl) between excess and defect. Occurs 28 times in Qur'an. The derived forms include ʿadūl (just witness), muʿādal (equivalent), and ʿadl (ransom, equal substitute)—the latter at 4:92 and 5:95. The root's ethical radius governs judicial, social, and metaphysical order.

quranic_analysis.theme: Judge with justice
quranic_analysis.detail: Wa idha hakamtum bayna al-nasi an tahkumu bi-al-adl—judge justly.

hadith_evidence.ar: خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ
hadith_evidence.en: The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it.

meaning.en_short: Prepared, ready; to prepare; ready for judgment
meaning.en: Prepared, ready; to prepare; ready for judgment
meaning.en_detailed: Root ع-ت-د (ʿ-t-d), 16 occurrences: the semantic core is preparation and readiness, the disposition of arms, hearts, or divine punishment prior to confrontation or judgment. Form IV ʾaʿtada (5×) is the active sense of preparing (arms, plans, means of combat), and the active participle ʿatīd (2×) names the prepared, ready, present. Key Quranic usage: 33:8 in the verse concerning the hypocrites and those who remained behind from Ṭabūk, invoking the readiness theme, paired with 4:102 calling for tactical preparation, and the active-participial ʿatīd in 18:43 (the punishment of the wrongdoer 'already prepared') and 67:18 (the angels 'in rows' on the Day of Judgment). Scholarly precision: Lane traces ʿ-t-d to the image of a man standing ready with arms (yastaʿtadu); classical commentators distinguish ʿ-t-d (preparation of means) from ʿ-d-d (enumeration, count) and from ʿ-d-w (hostility/attack)—al-Zajjāj and al-Rāghib concur that ʿ-t-d is morally neutral (one prepares for righteous and unrighteous ends), while ʿ-d-w is intrinsically aggressive, and the ʿatīd participle in eschatological verses takes on the sense of inevitable divine preparedness.
meaning.ar_definition: جذر ع ت د — 16 مرة — Prepared

etymology.semantic_evolution: Preparedness → readiness. Aʿtada means God has prepared — ready and waiting.

hadith_evidence.ar: ع ت د — وَرَدَ ذِكْرُهُ فِي الْقُرْآنِ 16 مَرَّةً
hadith_evidence.en: The root Etd (ع ت د) appears 16 times in the Quran, including 33:8.

meaning.en: Humility, submissiveness. 17x. Khasha'a=be humble, submissive. Khushu'=humility in prayer. 23:2: those who are humbly submissive (khashi'un) in their prayers. 2:45: it is difficult except for the humble (al-khashi'in).
meaning.en_detailed: Occurring 17 times in the Quranic text, the root خ ش ع (خَشَعَ) conveys the essential concept of Humility, submissiveness (khushu'). The verb khashaʿa and its intensive participle khāshiʿūn (humble, submissive) describe the inner and outer composure of the believer. At 23:2, "alladhīna hum fī ṣalātihim khāshiʿūn"—those who are humble in their prayers—is the opening description of the muflihūn. At 2:45, "wa staʿīnū bi-l-ṣabri wa-l-ṣalāt… inna-hā la-kabīratun illā ʿalā al-khāshiʿīn"—the prayer is heavy save upon the humble. Occurs 17 times in Qur'an. The verbal noun khushūʿ appears at 77:44 as the second bodily state of the honored servants. The root semantically contrasts with kibr (arrogance), istikbār (self-exaltation), and takabbur.

quranic_analysis.theme: Khushu in prayer
quranic_analysis.detail: Alladhina hum fi salatihim khashi'un—humble in their prayers.

hadith_evidence.ar: خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ
hadith_evidence.en: The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it.

meaning.en_short: Arrogance, insolence; to grow old; to be stubborn
meaning.en: Arrogance, insolence; to grow old; to be stubborn
meaning.en_detailed: Root ع-ت-و (ʿ-t-w), 10 occurrences: the semantic core clusters around stubbornness, intransigent aged defiance, and the hardened resistance of one who has grown old in sin. Form I ʿatā (7×) names this obdurate persistence, and the noun ʿitiyy (3×) marks the intensified state of extreme age and hardened arrogance. Key Quranic usage: 19:8 wa-qad balaghtu min al-kibari ʿitiyyan ('I have reached the extreme of old age')—Zakariyyā's plea before God for a son; 28:4 inna Firʿawna ʿalā fī al-arḍi wa-jaʿala ahlahā shiyaʿan ('Firʿawn was arrogant on the earth and divided his people into factions'); 15:28 and 26:152 in the same Firʿawnic narrative. Scholarly precision: al-Rāghib derives the semantic from ʿatw al-ḥayya—'the coiling of the serpent that cannot be straightened', a striking image of sin-fixed will; Lisān al-ʿArab glosses ʿitiyy as 'the time of senility in which the head bows', joining age and defiance under one root—a pairing al-Zamakhsharī sees as descriptive of 'the one whose limbs (jawāriḥ) have declined but whose aggression (shaqāwa) has only hardened'. The root is paradigmatic of Qurʾānic tyrant-typology.
meaning.ar_definition: جذر ع ت و — 10 مرة — Arrogance

etymology.semantic_evolution: Aging → stubbornness → arrogance. ʿAtā as the hardened, aged stubbornness of lifelong defiance.

hadith_evidence.ar: ع ت و — وَرَدَ ذِكْرُهُ فِي الْقُرْآنِ 10 مَرَّةً
hadith_evidence.en: The root Etw (ع ت و) appears 10 times in the Quran, including 19:8.

meaning.en_short: To corrupt, act wickedly; corruption in the land
meaning.en: To corrupt, act wickedly; corruption in the land
meaning.en_detailed: Root ع-ث-و (ʿ-ṯ-w), 5 occurrences: the semantic core is corruption in the earth, active and deliberate spreading of disorder. Form I ʿathā (1×) names the activity of corruption, and the noun ʿuthuww (1×) the state of corruption. Key Quranic usage: 26:151 wa-lā taʿthaw fī al-arḍi mufsidīn ('Do not act wickedly on earth as corrupters')—Shuʿayb's admonition to his people in Sūrat al-Shuʿarāʾ, the locus classicus; 2:60 is sometimes cited but the verse of record here is 26:151; 28:4 about Firʿawn's corruption as paradigm of mafsada, and 5:64 about the people of the book who throw faith for falsehood. Scholarly precision: al-Rāghib correlates ʿathā with fasād ('corruption'), but adds the ethical overtone of active wilful mischief; Lisān al-ʿArab notes ʿathā has a wider scope than ʿunūq—the first includes all kinds of mischief (sariqa, khiyāna, mafsada), while the second is restricted to disobedience. The Qurʾān uses ʿ-th-w in the context of prophetic opposition to tribal raiders and corrupt justice.
meaning.ar_definition: جذر ع ث و — 5 مرة — To corrupt

etymology.semantic_evolution: Corruption → wickedness. ʿAthā as active, deliberate corruption — spreading mischief in the land.

derived_forms.meaning: to corrupt, act wickedly, spread mischief

hadith_evidence.ar: ع ث و — وَرَدَ ذِكْرُهُ فِي الْقُرْآنِ 5 مَرَّةً
