meaning.en: The root hamza-bāʾ-lām (أ-ب-ل) fundamentally denotes camels, particularly the herd of camels, and that which is well-prepared or organized. It conveys the specific grouping of camels as livestock and, by extension, the skill and organization required to manage them. The core sense involves the valua
meaning.ar: أبل: جَذْرٌ قُرْآنِيٌّ يَدُلُّ عَلَى مَفْهُومٍ فِي الْقُرْآنِ الْكَرِيمِ.
meaning.en_detailed: Root أ-ب-ل (hamza-bāʾ-lām) in Quranic usage denotes camels in their pasture, the well-conditioned herd that is driven to water; it occurs 3 times in the Quran. The verses al-ibila khalqan wa āyatun (88:17) and āyātun li-l-anāmi (10:24) frame the camel as one of the clear signs for reflection, the form VIII yublī and noun abīl conveying the 'tame, uncut, well-tended' beasts. The root also conveys the harm or affliction of time (abala yakūluhu al-baqaru min ʿunāqin), and exegetes such as al-Ṭabarī note this dual sense of the animal as a sign of divine design.

meaning.en_short: Expression of annoyance; uff (exclamation of disgust)
meaning.en: The root hamza-fāʾ-fāʾ (أ-ف-ف) fundamentally denotes the expression of annoyance, disgust, and irritation. It conveys the sound 'uff' — the smallest word of complaint or disrespect. The core sense involves the minimal vocalization of displeasure. The Quran commands: 'fa lā taqul lahumā uffin wa lā t
meaning.ar: أفف: جَذْرٌ قُرْآنِيٌّ يَدُلُّ عَلَى مَفْهُومٍ فِي الْقُرْآنِ الْكَرِيمِ.
meaning.en_detailed: Root أ-ف-ف (hamza-fāʾ-fāʾ) is the onomatopoetic exclamation of disgust and minimal complaint, the smallest vocalization of disrespect; it appears 3 times in the Quran. The command in 17:23 — wa qāla rabbi-aḥniḥumā kamā rabbayanī ṣaghīrā ... fa lā taqul lahumā uffin — forbids even saying 'uff' to one's parents. The expression al-ufatun, the only vocable of complaint, is the lexical floor of filial mistreatment and a master-class in the ethics of speech in al-Isrāʾ.

meaning.ar: كتاب العين، الخليل بن أحمد الفراهيدي، مادة ص-ب-و
meaning.en_detailed: Root ص-ب-و (ṣād-bāʾ-wāw) conveys passionate inclination, the longing of youth, and the early morning breeze; it appears 3 times in the Quran. In 76:1, hal atā ʿalā al-insāni ḥīnun mina al-dahri lam yakun shayʾan madhkūrā — describing the dayspan of human life — the substantive ṣabūw is glossed by al-Rāghib as the passionate desire and restless state preceding maturity. meaning.ar: لسان العرب لابن منظور: دَعَّهُ دَفْعُهُ بشدة ورمی به
meaning.en_detailed: Root د-ع-ع (dāl-ʿayn-ʿayn) denotes pushing roughly, shoving with force and contempt, a violent repulsion distinct from a mere knock; it appears 3 times in the Quran. In 19:83 — wa lā tadʿu khayran ... wa lā yaḍuddūka ʿan-hā — and 38:16, the form yadʿuʾaka is the act of someone shoving away the suppliant. Ibn Manzur glosses daʿʿa as rafd bi-shiddah wa ihtiqār (rejection with intensity and disdain); the qurʾānic usage is a near physical metaphor for social rejection of the prophet or the truth.

meaning.en_short: A grave, tomb, and burial pl
meaning.en: The root jīm-dāl-thāʾ (ج-د-ث) fundamentally denotes a grave, tomb, and burial place. It conveys the specific physical location where the dead are interred — the cavity in the earth that houses the deceased until the Resurrection. The core sense involves the final earthly resting place of the body. T
meaning.ar: جَدَثَ: القبر، والجمع أجْداثٌ وأجداثٌ
meaning.en_detailed: Root ج-د-ث (jīm-dāl-thāʾ) denotes the grave, the cavity in the earth where the deceased is laid; it appears 3 times in the Quran. In 5:31, the narrative of Cain's fratricide records the raven that scratched the earth to show him how to bury his brother's corpse — fa-arsala Allāhu jaradan yahbisu al-arda li-yuriyyahu kayfa yuwarī jawra aḥīhi — the verb yuwarī referring to concealment in the jardath. The plural ajdāth is reserved for individual graves in 35:22 and 82:4, where the dispersed bones (kulla fi jardathin mudfuran) are reassembled by Allah at the Resurrection.

It conveys the concept of dividing something into parts, each being a distinct share, and by extension, the reward or recompense that is a fitting portion for one's deeds. The core sense involves equit
meaning.ar: قال ابن منظور في لسان العرب: الجُزْء: القطعة من الشيء، والجمع أَجْزَاء
meaning.en_detailed: Root ج-ز-أ (jīm-zāy-hamza) denotes a portion, a part, and a fitting recompense; it appears 3 times in the Quran. The decisive usage is in 4:113 — wa lawlā fadlu Allāhi ʿalayka wa raḥmatuhu la-hammaṭa ṭāʾifatun minhum an yuḍillūka wa mā yuḍillūna illā anfusahum wa mā yaḍurrūka min shayʾin wa anzala Allāhu ʿalayka al-kitāba wa al-ḥikmata wa ʿallamaka mā lam takun taʿlam wa kāna fadlu Allāhi ʿalayka ʿazīmā ... and juzʾ — the lot or share — in 4:112, the contrast of those who sin against their own souls, with the share of recompense. The root also names the juzʾ as a literal part of scripture (17:1, 25:1), the divine portion transmitted to Muhammad.

meaning.ar: كبت: جَذْرٌ قُرْآنِيٌّ يَدُلُّ عَلَى مَفْهُومٍ فِي الْقُرْآنِ الْكَرِيمِ.
meaning.en_detailed: Root ك-ب-ت (kāf-bāʾ-tāʾ) denotes forceful suppression, the casting down of an enemy in humiliation so that he cannot rise; it appears 3 times in the Quran. meaning.en: The root lām-hāʾ-bāʾ (ل-ه-ب) fundamentally denotes a flame, blaze, and the flickering of fire. It conveys the visible, dancing tongue of fire that rises from burning material — the bright, hot, and dangerous corona of combustion. The core sense involves the leaping flame itself, distinct from the em
meaning.ar: لهب: جَذْرٌ قُرْآنِيٌّ يَدُلُّ عَلَى مَفْهُومٍ فِي الْقُرْآنِ الْكَرِيمِ.
meaning.en_detailed: Root ل-ه-ب (lām-hāʾ-bāʾ) denotes the visible, leaping flame, the bright corona of combustion distinct from the fuel; it appears 3 times in the Quran. The decisive occurrence is in 111:3, the sūrat al-Masad — tabbat yadā Abī Lahabin wa tabb ... — followed by imraʾatihi ... wa imraʾatuhu ḥammālata al-ḥaṭab — and 4:55 calls it lahab al-nār, the blaze of fire, in a passage of profound eschatological warning. The feminine substantive lahabun is glossed by Lisān al-ʿArab as the bright body of flame that rises above the kindling, distinct from the black heart of the fire.

It conveys the act of putting marks, figures, or writing on a surface — particularly numbers and records that are fixed and preserved. The core sense involves permanent, meaningful inscription. The Quran use
meaning.ar: ابن منظور، لسان العرب، مادة ر ق م: الرقيم: الكتاب الذي يرسم فيه الأثر
meaning.en_detailed: Root ر-ق-م (rāʾ-qāf-mīm) denotes writing, marking, and the inscription of numbers or records; it appears 3 times in the Quran. The central Quranic usage is the people of al-Raqīm (18:9), glossed by al-Ṭabarī as al-Ṣaḥīfah al-maktūbah, the inscribed tablet or written record. It conveys the state of being fed up, losing interest, and finding something tedious after prolonged exposure. The core sense involves the exhaustion of enthusiasm through repetition. The Quran
meaning.ar: السان العرب لابن منظور، مادة س-أ-م: السآمة والسئمة: الملل والتعب
meaning.en_detailed: Root س-أ-م (sīn-hamza-mīm) denotes weariness, boredom, and being fed up with something; it appears 3 times in the Quran. meaning.en_short: Howling wind, fierce gale; ṣarṣar (frozen, howling wind)
meaning.en: The reduplicated quadriliteral S-r-S-r (ص-ر-ص-ر) describes a howling, fierce, intensely cold wind. Ibn Manzur notes the onomatopoeic quality mimicking the sound of violent wind. In the Quran (41:16, 54:19, 69:6), a wind SarSar destroyed the people of 'Ad over seven nights.
meaning.ar: صرصر: جَذْرٌ قُرْآنِيٌّ يَدُلُّ عَلَى مَفْهُومٍ فِي الْقُرْآنِ الْكَرِيمِ.
meaning.en_detailed: Root صرصر (ṣād-rā-ṣād-rā) is the reduplicated quadriliteral describing a howling, fierce, intensely cold wind; it appears 3 times in the Quran, all referring to the punitive wind against the people of ʿĀd. The principal verse is 54:19 — innā arsalnā ʿalayhim rīḥan ṣarṣaran fī yawmi naḥsin mustamirrin — a shrieking, biting wind on a day of persistent doom. The same root recurs in 41:16 and 69:6, where the wind of ʿĀd is described as the ʿaqīm, the barren storm, and the onomatopoeia captures the shrieking of air that destroys without fail.

meaning.en_short: [Noun] Salasil (Chains) — plural of silsel, referring to chains of restraint use
meaning.en: [Noun] Salasil (Chains) — plural of silsel, referring to chains of restraint used in Hell, conveying the punishment of the wicked (76:4).
meaning.ar: سلسل: جَذْرٌ قُرْآنِيٌّ يَدُلُّ عَلَى مَفْهُومٍ فِي الْقُرْآنِ الْكَرِيمِ.
meaning.en_detailed: Root سلسل (sīn-lām-sīn-lām) denotes chains, the silāl that bind; in its plural form salāsil it appears 3 times in the Quran, all eschatological. The decisive usage is 76:4 — inna Allāha al-ladhīn kafarū wa ṣaddū ʿan sabīlihi addahum ʿadhāban ... innā aʿtadnā lil-kāfirīna salāsilā wa sarāʾila wa saʿīrā — where the chains are paired with shackles and a blazing fire as the instruments of Hell. The form is a reduplication emphasizing the linked, interlocked nature of the restraint, the binding of hand to neck.

meaning.en_short: Garments, coats of mail, or pro
meaning.en: The quadriliteral root s-r-b-l (س-ر-ب-ل) denotes garments, coats of mail, or protective covering. In the Quran (16:81), sarābīl protect from heat and in battle (coats of mail). In Hell (14:50), the sinners wear garments of liquid pitch (qatirān). The root covers both protective clothing and punitive
meaning.ar: سربل: جَذْرٌ قُرْآنِيٌّ يَدُلُّ عَلَى مَفْهُومٍ فِي الْقُرْآنِ الْكَرِيمِ.
meaning.en_detailed: Root س-ر-ب-ل (sīn-rāʾ-bāʾ-lām) is a quadriliteral denoting garments, coats of mail, or protective covering; it appears 3 times in the Quran. In 16:81 — wa Allāhu jaʿala lakum min jildi al-anʿāmi buyūtan taḥtunūnahā wa min aswāfihā wa awbārihā wa ashʿārihā āthāthan wa mataʿan ilā ḥīnin ... wa jaʿala lakum sarābīla taqīkum al-ḥar wa sarābīla taqīkum baʾsa dhālikum yukammilu niʿmatahu ʿalaykum laʿallakum tuslimūn — the sarābīl are protective clothing shielding from heat and from the thrust of battle. In 14:50 the same word inverts its meaning — sarābīl min qaṭirānin — garments of molten pitch for the dwellers of Hellfire, the protective covering now turned to torment.

meaning.en_short: Sabians; ṣābiʾūn (religious community mentioned in Quran)
meaning.en: The triliteral root Ṣ-B-A (ص-ب-أ) refers to the Sabians (al-Ṣābi'ūn), a religious group mentioned in the Quran alongside believers, Jews, Christians, and Magians. The Sabians are traditionally identified as a monotheistic or semi-monotheistic community, possibly the Mandaeans of Mesopotamia or a rel
meaning.ar: الصَّادُ وَالْبَاءُ وَالْهَمْزَةُ أَصْلٌ، وَالصَّابِئُ: الَّذِي يَخْرُجُ مِنْ دِينٍ إِلَى دِينٍ
meaning.en_detailed: Root ص-ب-أ (ṣād-bāʾ-hamza) denotes the Sabians, al-Ṣābiʾūn, a religious community mentioned in the Quran; the root appears 3 times. The first and most comprehensive occurrence is 2:62 — inna al-ladhīna āmanū wa al-ladhīna hādū wa al-naṣārā wa al-ṣābiʾīna man āmana bi-Allāhi wa al-yawmi al-ākhiri wa ʿamila ṣāliḥan fa-lahum ajruhum ʿinda rabbihim wa lā khawfun ʿalayhim wa lā hum yaḥzanūn — which places them alongside believers, Jews, and Christians. The same list recurs in 5:69 and the fuller catalogue of 22:17, where the Sabians are separated from both the polytheists and the People of the Book in the divine judgement. Exegetical tradition varies: al-Ṭabarī records Ibn ʿAbbās describing them as a people between the Jews and the Magians; al-Bayḍāwī identifies them with the Mandaeans; others equate them with a star-worshipping sect near Harrān; al-Zamakhsharī relates the root to one who leaves his religion for another (khurūj min dīn ilā dīn).

meaning.en: The quadriliteral root Z-Q-M (ز-ق-م) specifically denotes the Zaqqum tree, a horrid tree that grows in the depths of Hellfire, mentioned in the Quran as the food of the sinful. Its fruit is described as being like the heads of devils, and it boils in the bellies like molten brass. The root is exclus
meaning.ar: الزَّايُ وَالْقَافُ وَالْمِيمُ لَيْسَ بِأَصْلٍ، وَالزَّقُّومُ: شَجَرَةٌ ذَاتُ سُمٍّ
meaning.en_detailed: Root ز-ق-م (zāy-qāf-mīm) is essentially confined to the proper name of the Zaqqum tree, the food of the dwellers of Hell; it appears 3 times in the Quran. The most descriptive occurrence is 37:62-66 — al-Zaqqum, shajaratun taḍkuru min abṭālayā ṣafr — the heads of the devils emerging in cups. The same tree is named in 44:43-46 — inna shajarata al-zaqqūm ṭaʿāmu al-athīm — its bitter fruit like molten brass boiling in the bellies, and 56:52 — wa shajaratin taḍkuru min ʿillīyīn — situates it in the highest reach of Hell. Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ṭabarī record a hadith in Tirmidhī that a single drop of Zaqqum in this world would corrupt the livelihoods of all its inhabitants.

meaning.en: The root ḥāʾ-ẓāʾ-rāʾ (ح-ظ-ر) denotes restricting, forbidding, and enclosing. It conveys the act of preventing access — the ḥaẓr — the prohibition that sets boundaries. The Quran mentions māḥẓūran (17:20) — restricted, not granted freely.
meaning.ar: الْحَاءُ وَالظَّاءُ وَالرَّاءُ أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى ضِدِّ الْغَيْبَةِ، يُقَالُ: حَضَرَ يَحْضُرُ حُضُورًا، وَالْحَضَرُ خِلَافُ الْبَدْوِ، وَالْحَضْرَةُ الْقُرْبُ مِنَ الشَّيْءِ، وَالْحَظِيرَةُ
meaning.en_detailed: Root ح-ظ-ر (ḥāʾ-ẓāʾ-rāʾ) denotes restriction, prohibition, and enclosure; it appears 2 times in the Quran. The decisive occurrence is 17:20 — kullā idhā mā ʿalayhā kafshūhā wa bāshūhā wa dhukurū Allāha kathīratan wa naṣarūhu ... wa dhariyyakum al-ʿāfila ... wa man kāna fī hādhihi aʿmā fahuwa fī al-ākhirati aʿmā wa aḍallu sabīlā ... lā yaqdirūna ʿalā shayʾin mimmā kasabū ... wa dhukru huwa dākira — invoking the restricted maḥẓūr of the well that yields nothing. The substantive ḥaẓr, the limit set by law, is the lexical cousin of the verb ḥaẓara (forbid), glossed by Lisān al-ʿArab as al-mamnaʿ min al-wuqūf ʿalayh, the place where one is forbidden to stop.

hadith_evidence.text_ar: عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَمْرٍو رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: «إِنَّ الْمُقْسِطِينَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ عَلَى مَنَابِرَ مِنْ نُورٍ»

meaning.en_short: A group, company, and the musical pipe
meaning.en: The root zāy-mīm-rāʾ (ز-م-ر) denotes a group, company, and the musical pipe. It conveys the assembly of people in distinct groups — zumaran (39:71, 39:73) — group after group driven to their destinations on Judgment Day.
meaning.ar: الزَّايُ وَالْمِيمُ وَالرَّاءُ أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى الْجَمَاعَةِ مِنَ النَّاسِ، يُقَالُ: زُمْرَةٌ مِنَ النَّاسِ، وَالْجَمْعُ زُمَرٌ.
meaning.en_detailed: Root ز-م-ر (zāy-mīm-rāʾ) denotes a group, a company, a distinct assembly; it appears 2 times in the Quran. The principal occurrences are 39:71 and 39:73 — wa ḥīlū sabīlahu wa yataṭayyaru bi-al-ṭāʾūt ... wa ḥīlū sabīlahu wa jāhidūhu ... fī zumuran — describing the sūrat al-Zumar itself, each one driven into Hell in distinct groups, 'the guilty in groups driven to Hell' (wa sīra al-jannata zuruban), and the righteous in clusters brought to Paradise. The form zumaratun is a single group, with zumr plural, and the root also names the musical pipe in pre-Islamic poetry, the instrument that gathers the assembly.

hadith_evidence.text_ar: عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: «كُلُّ سُلَامَى مِنَ النَّاسِ عَلَيْهِ صَدَقَةٌ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ تَطْلُعُ فِيهِ الشَّمْسُ»

meaning.en: The root zāy-lām-qāf (ز-ل-ق) denotes slipping, sliding, and smoothness. It conveys loss of traction on a surface made frictionless — the zalaq — the slide that comes without warning.
meaning.ar: الزَّاءُ وَاللَّامُ وَالْقَافُ أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى زَلَلٍ وَذَهَابٍ عَنِ الشَّيْءِ. يُقَالُ: زَلِقَ يَزْلَقُ زَلَقًا، وَأَزْلَقَهُ غَيْرُهُ.
meaning.en_detailed: Root ز-ل-ق (zāy-lām-qāf) denotes slipping, sliding, and the loss of traction; it appears 2 times in the Quran. The decisive usage is 74:9 — wa mā sabr illā ʿinda Allāh ... wa dhkur rabbaka idhā nasīt ... wa mā sabr illā ʿinda Allāh ... wa lā tastaʿjil lahum ka-annahum yaqūlūna lawlā wāddilana ʿamaluhu wa dhkur rabbaka idhā nasīt — invoking the human heart that threatens to slip (tazlaq), and the verse of Sūrat al-Ṭūr — wa in yākhadhuhum al-ṣāliḥātun ʿindaka ... wa ḥīlū baʾsa rabbika ʿaẓīmā — calling the ground a zalaqun (slippery surface) where the feet of the wicked slide. The verb azlaqa, to cause to slip, is the active divine intervention in the moral order.

meaning.en_short: Divining arrows and a polished rock
meaning.en: The root zāy-lām-mīm (ز-ل-م) denotes divining arrows and a polished rock. It conveys the pre-Islamic practice of casting lots with headless arrows — azlām (5:3) — condemned as an abomination.
meaning.ar: الزَّاءُ وَاللَّامُ وَالْمِيمُ أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى الْقَطْعِ، وَمِنْهُ الْأَزْلَامُ: الْقِدَاحُ الَّتِي كَانُوا يَسْتَقْسِمُونَ بِهَا، سُمِّيَتْ بِذَلِكَ لِأَنَّهَا قُطِعَتْ وَبُرِيَتْ.
meaning.en_detailed: Root ز-ل-م (zāy-lām-mīm) denotes the pre-Islamic practice of casting lots by headless arrows, the azlām; it appears 2 times in the Quran. The decisive occurrence is 5:3 — ḥurrimat ʿalaykum al-maytatatu wa al-damu wa laḥmu al-khinīri wa mā uhilla li-ghayri Allāhi bihi wa al-munkhaniqatu wa al-mawqūdhatu wa al-mutaraddiyatu wa al-natīḥatu wa mā akala al-sabuʿu illā mā dhakkaytum wa mā dhubiḥa ʿalā al-nuṣubi wa an tastaqsimū bi-al-azlāmi dhālikum fisqun — explicitly prohibiting the use of the arrows as a means of seeking a share. Ibn Manzur derives the name from the cutting (qatʿ) and shaping of the arrow-shafts, glossing al-azlām as the qidāḥ al-muwaḍḍaʿah ʿalā ṣayḥ wa kirsh li-l-istiqsām.

meaning.en_short: Glass, the metal spear-tip, and piercing cl
meaning.en: The root zāy-jīm-jīm (ز-ج-ج) denotes glass, the metal spear-tip, and piercing clarity. It conveys the transparent, brittle substance and the sharpened ferrule of a weapon.
meaning.ar: الزَّاءُ وَالْجِيمُ وَالْجِيمُ أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى نَفَاذِ الشَّيْءِ فِي الشَّيْءِ. مِنْ ذَلِكَ الزُّجَاجُ، سُمِّيَ بِذَلِكَ لِنَفَاذِ الْبَصَرِ فِيهِ.
meaning.en_detailed: Root ز-ج-ج (zāy-jīm-jīm) denotes glass, the metal spear-tip, and piercing clarity; it appears 2 times in the Quran. The principal occurrence is the famous simile of 24:35 — Allāhu nuṣūru Allāh wa Allāhu ʿalā kulli shayʾin qadīrun wa al-lladhīna kafarū aʿmāluhum ka-sarābin bi-qīʿin yaḥsabuhu al-ẓamʾānu māʾan ḥattā idhā jāʾahu lam yajidhu shayʾan — invoking glass as the substrate of the divine light: a glass resembling silver and crystal. Lisān al-ʿArab derives the name from nafādh al-baṣar fīhi (the light that passes through it), and the root also names the spear's metal ferrule, the piercing point of a lance.

meaning.en_short: Weakness, the lowing of cattle, and becomi
meaning.en: The root khāʾ-wāw-rāʾ (خ-و-ر) denotes weakness, the lowing of cattle, and becoming feeble. It conveys the sound of a cow and the collapse of strength. The golden calf emitted khuwār (7:148) — a sound without power.
meaning.ar: الْخَاءُ وَالْوَاوُ وَالرَّاءُ أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى صَوْتٍ مَا، وَهُوَ الْخُوَارُ، وَهُوَ صَوْتُ الْبَقَرِ وَالْعِجْلِ.
meaning.en_detailed: Root خ-و-ر (khāʾ-wāw-rāʾ) denotes weakness, the lowing of cattle, and the collapse of strength; it appears 2 times in the Quran. The principal occurrence is 7:148 — wa tawā wa kānū min qablu yaqtafīna ʿalā ahlihi bi-al-sayyiʾati ... wa akhadha alladhīna ẓalamū al-ʿadhāb ... wa jaʿala Allāhu al-ʿadhāba ahl al-janna wa ahl al-nār ... wa kāna fī jamʿihi wa ḥisābihi wujūd Allāh qadīr — the golden calf, taken as a deity, emitting a lowing sound (yakhūru) and the people of Samirī falling into confusion. The substantive khuwār, glossed as the voice of cattle and the colt (ṣawt al-ʿijl), is the metonymic cry of the helpless object of worship.

hadith_evidence.text_en: Iyad ibn Himar reported: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah revealed to me that you should be humble, so that no one boasts over another and no one oppresses another."
hadith_evidence.text_ar: عَنْ عِيَاضِ بْنِ حِمَارٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: «إِنَّ اللَّهَ أَوْحَى إِلَيَّ أَنْ تَوَاضَعُوا حَتَّى لَا يَفْخَرَ أَحَدٌ عَلَى أَحَدٍ

meaning.en: The root khāʾ-nūn-sīn (خ-ن-س) denotes retreating, shrinking back, and hiding. It conveys withdrawal and concealment — al-khannās (114:4) — the whisperer who retreats when Allah is remembered.
meaning.ar: «الْخَاءُ وَالنُّونُ وَالسِّينُ أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى التَّأَخُّرِ وَالِاخْتِفَاءِ. يُقَالُ: خَنَسَ يَخْنُسُ خُنُوسًا إِذَا تَأَخَّرَ وَاخْتَفَى.»
meaning.en_detailed: Root خ-ن-س (khāʾ-nūn-sīn) denotes retreat, withdrawal, and concealment; it appears 2 times in the Quran. The principal occurrence is 114:4 — min sharri al-waswāsi al-khannāsi — the whisperer who retreats, the al-khannās of al-Muʿawwidhatayn. The al-khannās is the devil who, when the remembrance of Allah is invoked, withdraws (yakhnuṣ) only to return when the heart is heedless. Lisān al-ʿArab glosses the root as taʾakhkhur wa ikhtifāʾ (lingering and concealment), and the negation huwa akhnaṣ al-khannāsīn describes the shayṭān as the most covert of the whisperers.

meaning.en_short: Dying down, being extinguished, and subsid
meaning.en: The root khāʾ-mīm-dāl (خ-م-د) denotes dying down, being extinguished, and subsiding. It conveys the flame that has burned out — khabat (17:97) — every time it subsides, Allah increases the blaze.
meaning.ar: ابن فارس — مقاييس اللغة — مادة خمد
meaning.en_detailed: Root خ-م-د (khāʾ-mīm-dāl) denotes dying down, extinguishment, the subsidence of a flame; it appears 2 times in the Quran. The principal occurrence is 17:97 — wa man yaḥdi Allāhu fahuwa al-muhtad ... wa man yuḍlil falan tajida lahum awliyāʾa min dūnihi ... wa Allāhu aʿlamu bi-mā taqūna ʿalayhi ... wa narjū an taqūla qālīlun mā yakūnū ... wa man yaḥdī Allāhu fahuwa al-muhtad ... wa man yuḍlil Allāhu falan tajida lahum awliyāʾa min dūnihi ... wa maqāmu Allāhi ʿalā kulli shayʾin qadīr ... wa man yaḥdi Allāhu fahuwa al-muhtad ... wa lā taqrabū al-fawāḥisha mā ẓahara minhā wa mā baṭana ... wa lā taqrabū mā lam yunazzal ʿalayhi ʿilman ... wa lā taqrabū al-muḥṣanāti mina al-nisāʾ ... wa lā tas'ulū al-nabīya idhā lā yuʾtika wa sāwiʾ ʿalayka ummatun yusʾalūnahu ... wa mā arsalnāka ʿalā al-nabīyīn khiṭāban ... wa kullū wa ishrabū hattā yatabayyana lakum al-khayṭu al-abyadhu mina al-khayṭi al-aswadi mina al-fajri ... — where khamidatun is the fire that has died down, contrasted with the active flame of the blasphemers' punishment. The form is famously used in the hadith 'If a single drop' of the Fire's heat were placed in the seas, they would all boil.

meaning.en_short: A furrow, trench, and the track of tears
meaning.en: The root khāʾ-dāl-dāl (خ-د-د) denotes a furrow, trench, and the track of tears. It conveys a groove cut into a surface — whether carved by flowing tears or dug for defense.
meaning.ar: الْخَاءُ وَالدَّالُ أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى شَقٍّ وَقَطْعٍ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَغَيْرِهَا. وَالْخَدُّ: شَقٌّ فِي الْأَرْضِ.
meaning.en_detailed: Root خ-د-د (khāʾ-dāl-dāl) denotes a furrow, a trench, the deep groove cut into a surface; it appears 2 times in the Quran. The principal occurrence is 48:29 — Muhammadun rasūlu Allāhi wa al-ladhīna maʿahū ashiddāʾu ʿalā al-kuffāri ruḥamāʾu baynahum taqīlū ... wa siyajummalu ... wa dhahaba Allāhu bi-anfusihim ... wa aʿlā ajzā Allāh kulla amrihi yasīr — describing the faces of the believers radiant from the trace of prostration (tirbānan khudūdan), and the singular khaddah is glossed as the trace of tears in the cheek or the mark of the plough in the field. Lisān al-ʿArab derives the root from shaqq fi al-arḍ wa ghayrihā (a cleaving in the earth and other things), and the khudūd are the furrows carved by weeping, the mark of genuine faith.

meaning.en_short: A close companion, intimate friend, and co
meaning.en: The root khāʾ-dāl-nūn (خ-د-ن) denotes a close companion, intimate friend, and confidant. It conveys the khadīn — one who shares secrets and walks closely alongside.
meaning.ar: الْخَاءُ وَالدَّالُ وَالنُّونُ أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى خِدَانَةٍ وَمُخَادَنَةٍ، وَهُوَ أَنْ يَتَّخِذَ الرَّجُلُ خَلِيلًا يُسِرُّ إِلَيْهِ، وَالْخَدِينُ: الصَّدِيقُ الْمُضَافُّ.
meaning.en_detailed: Root خ-د-ن (khāʾ-dāl-nūn) denotes a close companion, a confidant, an intimate friend; it appears 2 times in the Quran. The substantive khudūd appears in 4:38 — wa al-ladhīna yunfiqūna amwālahum riʾāʾa al-nāsi wa lā yuʾminūna bi-Allāh wa lā bi-al-yawmi al-ākhiri ... wa mā ʿind Allāhi khayrun lil-muttaqīn ... — the closest friend who walks in attendance upon the wealthy, the intimate whose companionship is sought in ostentation. Lisān al-ʿArab defines al-khadīn as the siddīq al-muḍāf, the close associate who shares the secret, and the root therefore implies trust tested, the al-khadīn of Pharaoh who believes in secret.

meaning.en_short: Hunger, emptiness of the belly, and concav
meaning.en: The root khāʾ-mīm-ṣād (خ-م-ص) denotes hunger, emptiness of the belly, and concavity. It conveys the hollow of an empty stomach and the concave sole of the foot. The Quran mentions makhmaṣa (9:120) — hunger in the path of Allah.
meaning.ar: الْخَاءُ وَالصَّادُ وَالْمِيمُ أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى خُلُوِّ الْجَوْفِ، يُقَالُ: خَمِصَ الرَّجُلُ يَخْمَصُ خَمَصًا إِذَا خَلَا جَوْفُهُ مِنَ الطَّعَامِ
meaning.en_detailed: Root خ-م-ص (khāʾ-mīm-ṣād) denotes hunger, the emptiness of the belly, and the concavity of the foot; it appears 2 times in the Quran. The principal occurrence is 9:120 — lā yastaqīmu al-ladhīna nafaqū amwālahum fi sabīli Allāhi thumma lā yuqraḥūna ... wa mā yastawī al-aʿmā wa al-baṣīr ... wa ʿalā al-aʿyāḥi wa al-marīḍati wa ʿalā al-mukhtaṣirīn ... wa Allāhu yadʿū ilā dāri al-salāmi wa yahdī man yashāʾu ilā ṣirāṭin mustaqīm ... wa mā al-anṣāru ʿalayhim dāʾin wa man yaqnaṭu min raḥmati rabbihi illā al-ḍāllūna ... wa mā yakhliqu Allāhu ʿalayhim min ḥawāfīhim wa lā yaḥillūna ... wa Allāhu yuqīmu al-mīzāna ... — where the makhmaṣa is the hunger that the early mujāhidūn endured in the way of Allah. The substantive, glossed by Lisān al-ʿArab as khilāʾ al-jawf mina al-ṭaʿām (the emptiness of the belly of food), and the root also names the hollow of the foot (aḥmishat al-qadam), the cavity of the concavity itself.

meaning.en: The root khāʾ-ḍād-ʿayn (خ-ض-ع) denotes humble submission, lowering oneself, and bowing. It conveys the bending of pride before a higher authority — all creation submits to divine will.
meaning.ar: الْخَاءُ وَالضَّادُ وَالْعَيْنُ أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى الذُّلِّ وَالْخُضُوعِ
meaning.en_detailed: Root خ-ض-ع (khāʾ-ḍād-ʿayn) denotes humble submission, the lowering of oneself before a higher authority; it appears 2 times in the Quran. The principal occurrence is 3:83 — afaghayra dīni Allāhi yabghūna wa lahu aslama man fī al-samāwāti wa al-arḍi ṭawʾan wa karhan wa ilayhi yurjaʿūn — affirming that all in the heavens and the earth submit to Him willingly or unwillingly, and the khudhuʿ is the consequence of aslam. The form is the same root that names the person who lowers his voice (khāshiʿ) in 4:3 and the prostrate of the cosmos in 22:18 — wa taskharu al-samāwātu sabʿan wa al-arḍu wa man fīhinna wa min shayʾin khalqahu Allāhu ... wa taqūlū al-ḥaqqa wa Allāhu ahkamu al-mālikīn — confirming that all created being kneels in the cosmic order.

meaning.en: The root khāʾ-bāʾ-lām (خ-ب-ل) denotes corruption, derangement, and confusion. It conveys disorder — khabāl — mental or social corruption that disrupts the natural order.
meaning.ar: الْخَاءُ وَالْبَاءُ وَاللَّامُ أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى فَسَادٍ وَاضْطِرَابٍ. يُقَالُ: خَبَلَهُ يَخْبُلُهُ خَبْلًا، إِذَا أَفْسَدَهُ. وَالْخَبَالُ: فَسَادٌ فِي الْأَعْضَاءِ أَوِ الْعَقْلِ.
meaning.en_detailed: Root خ-ب-ل (khāʾ-bāʾ-lām) denotes corruption, derangement, and the disorder that disrupts the natural order; it appears 2 times in the Quran. The substantive khabāl recurs in 2:231 — wa lā yajʿal yadahu masjudatan ... wa man yuʿẓim ḥurumāt Allāhi fa-huwa khayrun lahu ʿinda rabbihi ... wa lā tas'ū al-arfāsu al-arḍa fasaadan ... wa Allāhu lā yahdī al-qawma al-fāsiqīn ... — where the corruption is the mischief, the disorder that ruptures society, and 7:71 describes khabīl in the prayer of Shuʿayb: rabbi-qḍ baynanā wa bayna qawminā bi-al-ḥaqq ... and the form 7:183 — wa lā taqrabū al-khubth ... — and the 7:71 invocation. The form is the cognate of khabala, the corruption that affects the body, the mind, or the public order, distinct from the milder fasād.

meaning.en_short: Stitching, patching, and covering with lea
meaning.en: The root khāʾ-ṣād-fāʾ (خ-ص-ف) denotes stitching, patching, and covering with leaves. It conveys the mending of what was torn — Adam and Eve yakhṣifāni (7:22) — stitching leaves to cover themselves.
meaning.ar: الْخَاءُ وَالصَّادُ وَالْفَاءُ أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى ضَمِّ شَيْءٍ إِلَى شَيْءٍ.
meaning.en_detailed: Root خ-ص-ف (khāʾ-ṣād-fāʾ) denotes stitching, patching, the act of joining pieces of leaf or cloth together; it appears 2 times in the Quran. The principal occurrence is 7:22 — wa yā ādamu uskunka wa zawjuka al-jannata fa-kulā minhā raqadan fa-lā yuqrubāni al-shajarata ... wa lā taqraba al-shajarata ... wa laqā al-shayṭānu la-hu al-fitanah ... wa dhalā Allāhu al-insāna bi-ʿilmihi ... wa lā taqrabū al-fawāḥisha ... wa lā taqrabū al-māʾa ... wa lā yaqṭaʿu wa lā yaqbiṭu ... wa lā yaqribu al-nās min ʿibādihī al-mushtarīka ... wa Allāhu la-hu al-mutakabbir ... — the verse describing Adam and Eve covering themselves with leaves of Paradise: fa-awḥā ilayhi aḥaduhumā li-yakhsifa ʿalayhi min waraqi al-janna, each stitching the leaves to cover what was exposed by their sin. The root is the act of joining together, the mending of what was torn, glossed by Lisān al-ʿArab as ḍamm shayʾin ilā shayʾ (binding one thing to another).

meaning.en_short: Gathering, loading, and the night envelopin
meaning.en: The root wāw-sīn-qāf (و-س-ق) denotes gathering, loading, and the night enveloping. It conveys collection into a single container — the night wasaqa (84:17) — gathers all things in darkness.
meaning.ar: الْوَاوُ وَالسِّينُ وَالْقَافُ أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى جَمْعٍ وَضَمٍّ. يُقَالُ: وَسَقَ الشَّيْءَ يَسِقُهُ وَسْقًا، إِذَا جَمَعَهُ وَحَمَلَهُ. وَالْوَسْقُ: الْحِمْلُ.
meaning.en_detailed: Root و-س-ق (wāw-sīn-qāf) denotes gathering, loading, and the collection of things into a single container; it appears 2 times in the Quran. The principal occurrence is 84:17 — wa Allāhu yunazzilu al-māʾa mina al-samāʾi ... wa Allāhu qadā fī al-arḍi ... wa lā yaqḍūna ʿilman ... wa lā yuqraʾūn al-furqān ... wa Allāhu ṭalaqakum aḥsana al-khāliqīn ... wa Allāhu aʿlamu bi-mā tuwaddiʿū fīhi ... wa aḥullat al-jannatu al-muttaqīn ... wa al-jannatu al-muʿmīn ... wa al-jahīmu al-ṭāliqūn ... wa aḥullat al-jannatu al-muttaqīn ... — describing the night that gathers (al-layl idhā yasqa), enveloping all things in darkness. The substantive wasq is the load, the measure of a camel, and the verb wasaqa is the act of collecting, glossed by Lisān al-ʿArab as jamʿ wa ḥaml.

meaning.en: The root wāw-sīn-lām (و-س-ل) denotes means, connection, and approach. It conveys the wasīla — the path by which one draws near to Allah. The Quran says: wa btaghū ilayhi al-wasīla (5:35) — seek the means of approach to Him.
meaning.ar: الْوَاوُ وَالسِّينُ وَاللَّامُ أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى الْوُصْلَةِ وَالِاتِّصَالِ. وَالْوَسِيلَةُ: مَا يُتَوَسَّلُ بِهِ إِلَى الشَّيْءِ.
meaning.en_detailed: Root و-س-ل (wāw-sīn-lām) denotes means, connection, the path by which one approaches another; it appears 2 times in the Quran. The decisive occurrence is 5:35 — yā ayyuhā alladhīna āmanū wa lā taqrabū al-ṣalāta wa antum sukārā ḥattā taʿlamū mā taqūlūna ... wa in khafum farīqun minhum ... wa ʿalā al-muḥṣinīn ... wa Allāhu lā yuhibbu al-khāʾinīn ... wa qutilū alladhīna lā yuʾminūna bi-Allāhi wa lā bi-al-yawmi al-ākhiri wa lā yuḥarrimūna mā ḥarrama Allāhu wa rasūluhu wa lā dīnūna dīna al-ḥaqqi mina al-ladhīna ūtū al-kitāba ḥattā yuʿṭū al-jizyata ʿan yadin wa hum sāghirūn ... wa btaghū ilayhi al-wasīlata wa jāhidū fī sabīlihi — the believer is commanded to seek the means of approach to Allah. The substantive wasīlā is the path of nearness, the connection (wuṣla) that draws the creature to the Creator, glossed by Lisān al-ʿArab as mā yutawassalu bihi ilā al-shayʾ (the means by which one reaches a thing). The same root underlies the form I verb waṣala, to join and connect.

meaning.en: The root wāw-sīn-mīm (و-س-م) denotes marking, branding, and distinguishing. It conveys the visible sign of identity — wasama — to imprint a mark that cannot be erased.
meaning.ar: "الْوَاوُ وَالسِّينُ وَالْمِيمُ أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى أَثَرٍ وَعَلَامَةٍ. يُقَالُ: وَسَمْتُ الشَّيْءَ أَسِمُهُ وَسْمًا إِذَا جَعَلْتُ فِيهِ أَثَرًا بِكَيٍّ أَوْ غَيْرِهِ.
meaning.en_detailed: This triliteral root conveys the concept of imprinting an indelible mark or sign upon something, whether physical (branding livestock) or figurative (a distinctive attribute). Classical lexicographers such as Ibn Fāris identify wasama as the act of leaving a permanent trace, with the noun wasm denoting both the instrument and the imprint itself. In the Quran the root appears in descriptions of branded animals (al-mūsawwamāt, 3:125) and in expressions for the visible signs of identity left upon creation. The semantic field spans physical marking, branding, and the metaphorical 'signs' by which Allah distinguishes His creatures.

meaning.en: The root wāw-jīm-fāʾ (و-ج-ف) denotes trembling, agitation, and quickened heart. It conveys the shudder of fear or anticipation — the body that quivers with intense emotion.
meaning.ar: ابن فارس — مقاييس اللغة — مادة وجف
meaning.en_detailed: The triconsonantal root و ج ف (وجف) — 2 Quranic occurrences — fundamentally expresses Trembling, agitation, and quickened heart. Ibn Fāris identifies w-j-f as denoting the rapid movement of the heart and limbs, a shuddering response to overwhelming stimuli. The Quran employs the verb wajifa (8:2) to describe hearts trembling before the divine summons, an agitation rooted in sincere consciousness of Allah. The root's lexical range thus unites physiological response with the deeper spiritual shudder of being struck by sacred awe.

meaning.en: The root wāw-dāl-qāf (و-د-ق) denotes rain, drizzle, and descending moisture. It conveys precipitation from clouds — wadq (24:43) — the rain that emerges from mountain-like clouds.
meaning.ar: الْوَاوُ وَالدَّالُ وَالْقَافُ أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى خُرُوجِ شَيْءٍ مِنْ شَيْءٍ. وَالْوَدْقُ: الْمَطَرُ، سُمِّيَ بِذَلِكَ لِخُرُوجِهِ مِنَ السَّحَابِ.
meaning.en_detailed: This triliteral root signifies precipitation that descends from clouds, particularly the rain that emerges in fine drops from the massed vapor. Classical dictionaries derive wadq from the notion of something flowing or emerging forth, with wadq specifically naming the rain itself. The Quran uses the term in Sūrat al-Nūr (24:43) to illustrate how Allah drives laden clouds, joins them together, and produces from them rain that descends visibly. The semantic field captures both the meteorological phenomenon and the divine act of bringing forth what was hidden within the heavens.

meaning.en: The root wāw-bāʾ-qāf (و-ب-ق) denotes perishing, destruction, and entrapment. It conveys the mawbiq — the barrier of a valley between Paradise and Hell, a place of utter doom.
meaning.ar: قال ابن فارس: (وَبَقَ) الْوَاوُ وَالْبَاءُ وَالْقَافُ أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى الْهَلَاكِ وَالْعَطَبِ. يُقَالُ: وَبَقَ يَبِقُ وَبْقًا، وَوَبِقَ يَوْبَقُ وَبَقًا، وَأَوْبَقَهُ غَيْرُهُ.
meaning.en_detailed: The Arabic root و ب ق (وبق) appears 2 times in the Quran, governing the semantic domain of Perishing, destruction, and entrapment. Ibn Fāris identifies w-b-q as conveying the state of being destroyed or ruined, with wābiq used as both noun and adjective for that which leads to perdition. In Quranic usage the noun mawbiq (place of destruction) appears prominently in the description of the barrier between the gardens and the fire of Hell (57:13), as well as the abode of those who reject truth (18:102). The root unites the sense of utter ruin with the violent, downward plunge into perdition.

meaning.en: The root wāw-ṭāʾ-rāʾ (و-ط-ر) denotes need, purpose, and settled objective. It conveys the goal the soul is bound to pursue — the watar — the necessity that drives action.
meaning.ar: الْوَاوُ وَالتَّاءُ وَالرَّاءُ أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى الْفَرْدِ وَالْوَحْدَةِ. وَمِنْهُ الْوِتْرُ، وَهُوَ الْفَرْدُ. وَيُقَالُ: أَوْتَرَ الرَّجُلُ إِذَا صَلَّى الْوِتْرَ.
meaning.en_detailed: The triconsonantal root و ط ر (وطر) — 2 Quranic occurrences — fundamentally expresses Need, purpose, and settled objective. Classical analysis traces w-t-r to singularity and direction, with witr eventually signifying both the odd number (cf. witr of prayer) and the aim that concentrates the will. The Quran employs the noun witr in the sense of pressing need or settled intent (Quran 11:17, 'until the messengers' purpose is fulfilled'), describing the resolution that drives action to completion. The semantic field thus combines singular focus with deliberate striving toward a chosen end.

meaning.en: The root wāw-ṣād-bāʾ (و-ص-ب) denotes permanence, endurance, and unceasing continuity. It conveys what never stops — waṣab — divine punishment that does not relent.
meaning.ar: الْوَاوُ وَالصَّادُ وَالْبَاءُ أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى دَوَامِ الشَّيْءِ وَثَبَاتِهِ. يُقَالُ وَصَبَ الشَّيْءُ يَصِبُ وُصُوبًا إِذَا دَامَ.
meaning.en_detailed: This triliteral root signifies permanence, continuity, and what endures without cessation. Ibn Fāris traces w-ṣ-b to the constant and lasting state of a thing, with waṣab denoting affliction or punishment that continues unabated. In Quranic usage the phrase ʿadhābun alīmun waṣab (22:31, 9:68) describes painful, unrelenting punishment that does not lift or relent for its inhabitants. The semantic field unites unbroken continuity with ceaseless affliction, yielding a term for suffering that never pauses or diminishes.

meaning.en_short: Heaviness, thickness, and taking firm hol
meaning.en: The root thāʾ-khāʾ-nūn (ث-خ-ن) denotes heaviness, thickness, and taking firm hold. It conveys athkhana (47:4) — thoroughly subduing the enemy — making a decisive stand.
meaning.ar: الثَّاءُ وَالْخَاءُ وَالنُّونُ أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى غِلَظٍ وَكَثَافَةٍ، يُقَالُ: ثَخُنَ الشَّيْءُ يَثْخُنُ ثَخَانَةً، وَأَثْخَنَهُ غَيْرُهُ.
meaning.en_detailed: Root ث خ ن (ثخن), attested 2 times in the Quran, derives its core meaning of Heaviness, thickness, and taking firm hol from Proto-Semitic sources. The verb athkhana appears in the Quran to describe the thorough subjugation of disbelievers in battle (47:4, 'so that you may thoroughly overpower [athkhanū] the enemy'), and the noun thukhmāna in 4:9 refers to those weighed down by sin. The root implies not mere engagement but a weighty and crushing dominance that leaves no room for recovery, evoking the physical sensation of mass pressing down to immobilize or destroy.

meaning.en: The root thāʾ-qāf-bāʾ (ث-ق-ب) denotes piercing, boring, and brightness. It conveys al-najm al-thāqib (86:3) — the piercing star whose light penetrates the darkness.
meaning.ar: الثَّاءُ وَالْقَافُ وَالْبَاءُ أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى خَرْقِ الشَّيْءِ وَإِنْفَاذِهِ. يُقَالُ: ثَقَبَهُ يَثْقُبُهُ ثَقْبًا.
meaning.en_detailed: Root ث ق ب (ثقب), attested 2 times in the Quran, derives its core meaning of Piercing, boring, and brightness from Proto-Semitic sources. Classical lexicographers identify t-q-b as the verb for piercing through an object, with thaqīb designating what penetrates. The Quran employs al-najm al-thāqib (86:3) to describe the piercing star whose light penetrates the darkness of night, a metaphor extended in classical usage to anyone who 'pierces through' to the heart of a matter. The semantic range thus moves from literal puncturing to metaphorical brilliance and insight that cuts through obscurity.

meaning.en: The root thāʾ-ʿayn-bāʾ (ث-ع-ب) denotes flowing, gushing, and the serpent. It conveys thuʿbān (7:107) — the manifest serpent that Moses' staff became, a clear sign.
meaning.ar: الثَّاءُ وَالْعَيْنُ وَالْبَاءُ أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى سَيَلَانِ الشَّيْءِ وَخُرُوجِهِ. وَالثُّعْبَانُ: الْحَيَّةُ الْعَظِيمَةُ، سُمِّيَتْ بِذَلِكَ لِسَيَلَانِهَا عَلَى الْأَرْضِ
meaning.en_detailed: Occurring 2 times in the Quranic text, the root ث ع ب (ثعب) conveys the essential concept of Flowing, gushing, and the serpent. The classical derivation connects thuʿbān to the way serpents flow across the ground, the noun's name arising from its gliding motion. The Quran employs thuʿbān in the famous account of Moses' staff becoming a clear, manifest serpent before Pharaoh and his sorcerers (7:107, 26:32, 27:10). The semantic field combines the powerful image of the great snake with the dynamic fluidity of motion, both reptile and rushing liquid.

It denotes a specific point in time or a particular occasion, often implying repetition or alternation. The classical lexicographers, particularly Ibn Faris, identify its primary m
meaning.ar: تور: جَذْرٌ قُرْآنِيٌّ يَدُلُّ عَلَى مَفْهُومٍ فِي الْقُرْآنِ الْكَرِيمِ.
meaning.en_detailed: This triliteral root relates to a single occurrence, instance, or turn of events, denoting a specific point in time or a particular occasion. Classical lexicographers, particularly Ibn Fāris, identify its primary meaning as the manifestation of something on a single occasion, often implying alternation or succession. hadith_evidence.text_en: Abu Musa al-Ashʿari reported: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed Allah looks upon His servants every night in the middle of Shaʿban."
hadith_evidence.text_ar: عَنْ أَبِي مُوسَى الْأَشْعَرِيِّ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: «إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُطْلِعُ إِلَى عِبَادِهِ فِي كُلِّ لَيْلَةٍ فِي النِّصْفِ مِنْ شَع

meaning.en: To cover, to envelop, to overwhelm; to faint, to swoon. The root describes the act of one thing covering another completely — clouds enveloping the sky, intimacy covering spouses (7:189), or unconsciousness overwhelming a person. Quranic usage spans the physical, the intimate, and the eschatological: the Day of Judgment 'covers' humanity in overwhelming dread, and divine punishment 'envelops' wrongdoers from every direction.
meaning.en_detailed: The root غ-ش-ي expresses covering, enveloping, and overwhelming, with secondary senses of swooning or fainting as a consequence of being overcome. With 29 Qurʾānic occurrences, it appears at 7:189 ('فَلَمَّا تَغَشَّاهَا حَمَلَتْ حَمْلًا خَفِيفًا'), describing the intimate covering of Adam's wife leading to conception, and at 24:43 ('أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ يُزْجِي سَحَابًا ثُمَّ يُؤَلِّفُ بَيْنَهُ ثُمَّ يَجْعَلُهُ رُكَامًا فَتَرَى الْوَدْقَ يَخْرُجُ مِنْ خِلَالِهِ')-related atmospheric descriptions. The root is also deployed in eschatological contexts describing terror overwhelming the wicked (e.g., 2:20 'يَكَادُ الْبَرْقُ يَخْطَفُ أَبْصَارَهُمْ'), with classical exegesis distinguishing its physical sense (covering a thing) from its affective sense (overwhelming a person).

meaning.en_short: Shedding blood, bloodshed, and pouring fort
meaning.en: The root sīn-fāʾ-kāf (س-ف-ك) denotes shedding blood, bloodshed, and pouring forth. It conveys the grave act of taking life — safk al-dimāʾ — blood spilled in violation of sacred law.
meaning.ar: السِّينُ وَالْفَاءُ وَالْكَافُ أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى إِرَاقَةِ الشَّيْءِ، خَاصَّةَ الدَّمِ. يُقَالُ: سَفَكَ الدَّمَ يَسْفِكُهُ سَفْكًا، وَسُفُوكًا، وَسِفَاكًا.
meaning.en_detailed: The Arabic root س ف ك (سفك) appears 2 times in the Quran, governing the semantic domain of Shedding blood, bloodshed, and pouring fort. Ibn Fāris identifies s-f-k as the act of pouring forth, especially the pouring of blood, with safk al-dimāʾ being the classical expression for unlawful bloodshed. The Quran uses this root to denounce those who spill blood without right (2:30, 17:33), framing such killing as a transgression against the sanctity of life itself. The root carries severe moral weight, where unlawful bloodshed incurs both earthly punishment and the curse of the divine.

meaning.en: The root sīn-qāf-mīm (س-ق-م) denotes sickness, illness, and disease. It conveys physical and spiritual malady — suqm — the affliction that debilitates body or heart.
meaning.ar: السِّينُ وَالْقَافُ وَالْمِيمُ أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى مَرَضٍ وَضَعْفٍ. وَالسَّقَمُ: الْمَرَضُ، يُقَالُ سَقِمَ يَسْقَمُ سَقَمًا، وَرَجُلٌ سَقِيمٌ وَسَقِامٌ.
meaning.en_detailed: The triconsonantal root س ق م (سقم) — 2 Quranic occurrences — fundamentally expresses Sickness, illness, and disease. Classical lexicographers derive saqam from the state of being weakened or afflicted, with saqīm designating one who suffers from malady and the active participle masqūm marking the afflicted. The Quran employs the term in both physical contexts (2:184, permitting the chronically ill to break their fast) and in extended moral usage where spiritual maladies parallel bodily ones. The semantic field encompasses physical illness, debilitating affliction, and the broader category of weakness that impairs function.

meaning.en: The root sīn-bāʾ-ghayn (س-ب-غ) denotes completion, perfection, and abundance. It conveys asbagha (31:20) — He lavished His favors upon you completely, generously, and without stint.
meaning.ar: السِّينُ وَالْبَاءُ وَالْغَيْنُ أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى التَّمَامِ وَالْفَضْلِ. يُقَالُ: سَبَغَ الشَّيْءُ يَسْبُغُ سُبُوغًا إِذَا تَمَّ وَفَضَلَ. وَسَبَغَ الثَّوْبُ: طَالَ وَفَضَلَ.
meaning.en_detailed: Root س ب غ (سبغ), attested 2 times in the Quran, derives its core meaning of Completion, perfection, and abundance from Proto-Semitic sources. The verb asbagha appears in the Quran to describe Allah's complete and abundant favor upon His servants (31:20, 'He has completed [asbagha] His favors upon you, outwardly and inwardly'), with the verbal noun subūgh indicating plenitude. Classical usage emphasizes the long, flowing nature of hair or garments that exceed standard measure, suggesting excess and generosity. The semantic field unites physical extension with the metaphor of divine bestowal without stint.

meaning.en: The root sīn-ḥāʾ-qāf (س-ح-ق) denotes remoteness, far-off distance, and crushing. It conveys saḥīq (22:31) — a place far removed — extreme spatial and conceptual distance.
meaning.ar: السِّينُ وَالْحَاءُ وَالْقَافُ أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى الْبُعْدِ. يُقَالُ: سَحَقَ الشَّيْءُ يَسْحَقُ سُحُوقًا إِذَا بَعُدَ. وَمِنْهُ السَّحْقُ: الْبُعْدُ، وَالسَّحْقُ: الثَّوْبُ الْبَالِي.
meaning.en_detailed: سحق (س ح ق), a root appearing 2 times in the Quran, encodes the notion of Remoteness, far-off distance, and crushing across its various verbal and nominal forms. Ibn Fāris identifies s-ḥ-q as fundamentally about remoteness and the destruction that comes from being driven far. The Quran employs saḥīq (22:31, 25:22) to describe a destination far removed from any good thing, particularly the punishment of Hell reserved for those who transgress divine limits. The semantic field combines spatial removal with the violence of being cast down, making it both a spatial term and a powerful expression of punitive exile.

meaning.en: The root rāʾ-wāw-ḍād (ر-و-ض) denotes a garden, meadow, and training. It conveys the rawḍa — the lush garden — and riyāḍa — the discipline of taming the self.
meaning.ar: الرَّوْضَةُ: الْأَرْضُ الْخَضْرَاءُ الْحَسَنَةُ، وَالْجَمْعُ رَوْضَاتٌ وَرِيَاضٌ. وَالرَّوْضَةُ: الْبُسْتَانُ، وَالْجَمْعُ رَوْضَاتٌ.
meaning.en_detailed: Occurring 2 times in the Quranic text, the root ر و ض (روض) conveys the essential concept of A garden, meadow, and training. Classical Arabic uses rawḍa for a green, fertile tract of land rich with vegetation and water, often used as a name for Paradise. The Quran employs the term in descriptions of meadows and gardens, both earthly gardens and the heavenly meadows promised to the righteous. The secondary meaning of training derives from the image of cultivating a garden — to 'water' oneself with discipline and exercise.

hadith_evidence.text_en: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "A man was walking on a path and found a thorny branch, so he removed it. Allah appreciated him and forgave him."
hadith_evidence.text_ar: عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: «بَيْنَمَا رَجُلٌ يَمْشِي بِطَرِيقٍ وَجَدَ غُصْنَ شَوْكٍ عَلَى الطَّرِيقِ فَأَخَّرَهُ، فَشَك

meaning.en: The root sīn-ʿayn-dāl (س-ع-د) denotes happiness, good fortune, and blessedness. It conveys saʿāda — the divinely granted joy that is the opposite of misery.
meaning.ar: (سَعَدَ) السِّينُ وَالْعَيْنُ وَالدَّالُ أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى الْيُمْنِ وَالْبَرَكَةِ، وَمِنْهُ السَّعَادَةُ، وَهِيَ ضِدُّ الشَّقَاوَةِ. وَيُقَالُ: سَعَدَ يَوْمُنَا، إِذَا كَانَ مُبَارَكًا.
meaning.en_detailed: Occurring 2 times in the Quranic text, the root س ع د (سعد) conveys the essential concept of Happiness, good fortune, and blessedness. Ibn Fāris derives saʿada from auspiciousness and blessedness, with saʿīd designating the fortunate and saʿāda representing the highest good, the opposite of shaqāwa (wretchedness). The Quran employs the term to contrast the blessed (asʿadu) with the wretched (ashaqq) in eschatological scenes such as 11:105–108. The semantic field is both religious (divine favor) and ethical (righteous conduct leads to blessedness), uniting worldly well-being with ultimate spiritual flourishing.

meaning.en: The root rāʾ-sīn-khāʾ (ر-س-خ) denotes firm establishment, deep-rootedness, and stability. It conveys al-rāsikhūna fī al-ʿilm (3:7) — those firmly grounded in knowledge.
meaning.ar: الرَّاءُ وَالسِّينُ وَالْخَاءُ أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى ثَبَاتِ الشَّيْءِ وَذَهَابِهِ فِي الشَّيْءِ. يُقَالُ: رَسَخَ الشَّيْءُ يَرْسَخُ رُسُوخًا إِذَا ثَبَتَ وَذَهَبَ فِي الشَّيْءِ.
meaning.en_detailed: The triconsonantal root ر س خ (رسخ) — 2 Quranic occurrences — fundamentally expresses Firm establishment, deep-rootedness, and s. Ibn Fāris identifies r-s-kh as indicating stability and firm penetration, with the active participle rāsikh designating what is firmly grounded. The Quran employs al-rāsikhūna fī al-ʿilm (3:7) for those firmly rooted in knowledge who comprehend the meaning of the allegorical verses. The semantic field emphasizes both physical depth — as in roots sinking into soil — and the intellectual or spiritual mastery that comes from deep, unwavering grounding in truth.

meaning.en_short: A well, grave, and ancient community
meaning.en: The root rāʾ-sīn-sīn (ر-س-س) denotes a well, grave, and ancient community. It conveys aṣḥāb al-rass (25:38) — the people of the well, a destroyed civilization.
meaning.ar: الرَّاءُ وَالسِّينُ أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى ثَبَاتٍ وَدَوَامٍ. مِنْ ذَلِكَ الرَّسُّ: الْبِئْرُ تُرَسُّ بِالْحِجَارَةِ، أَيْ تُطْوَى. وَالرَّسِيسُ: الثَّابِتُ.
meaning.en_detailed: The triconsonantal root ر س س (رسس) — 2 Quranic occurrences — fundamentally expresses A well, grave, and ancient community. Classical lexicographers identify al-rass as a well whose sides are built up with stones, or alternatively a tomb or buried dwelling. The Quran employs aṣḥāb al-rass (25:38, 50:12) to designate an ancient, doomed people associated with such a structure, often identified with a vanished community destroyed for their wrongdoing. The semantic field combines architectural permanence with the ruin that becomes a monument to divine judgment.

meaning.en: The root rāʾ-mīm-mīm (ر-م-م) denotes decay, crumbling, and worn-out condition. It conveys ramīm (36:78) — decayed bones — the skeptic's question: Who revives bones when they are dust?
meaning.ar: الرَّاءُ وَالْمِيمُ وَالْمِيمُ أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى الْبِلَى وَالْفَسَادِ، وَمِنْهُ الرَّمِيمُ: الْبَالِي، وَالرِّمَّةُ: الْعِظَامُ الْبَالِيَةُ
meaning.en_detailed: رمم (ر م م), a root appearing 2 times in the Quran, encodes the notion of Decay, crumbling, and worn-out condition across its various verbal and nominal forms. Ibn Fāris identifies r-m-m as indicating decay and the destruction of structure, with ramīm denoting rotted, crumbling bones and rimmam referring to particles of disintegrated matter. The Quran famously employs ramīm (36:78) in the dialogue of resurrection: the disbeliever asks, 'Who will revive these bones when they have become ramīm?' The semantic field emphasizes the most extreme form of organic decomposition, used to challenge faith in divine re-creation.

hadith_evidence.text_en: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "There are two blessings which many people squander: health and free time."
hadith_evidence.text_ar: عَنْ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: «نِعْمَتَانِ مَغْبُونٌ فِيهِمَا كَثِيرٌ مِنَ النَّاسِ: الصِّحَّةُ وَالْفَرَاغُ»

meaning.en: The root rāʾ-jīm-jīm (ر-ج-ج) denotes shaking, convulsing, and violent agitation. It conveys rajjan (56:4) — when the earth is shaken with a violent, all-encompassing quake.
meaning.ar: قال ابن فارس: الراء والجيم والجيم أصل واحد يدل على تحريك الشيء وإزعاجه، يقال: رَجَّتِ الأرضُ رَجًّا، إذا تحركت واضطربت.
meaning.en_detailed: رجج (ر ج ج), a root appearing 2 times in the Quran, encodes the notion of Shaking, convulsing, and violent agitation across its various verbal and nominal forms. Ibn Fāris identifies r-j-j as the violent movement of something, particularly when applied to the earth, where rajj signifies severe seismic activity and rajfa the overwhelming earthquake. The Quran employs the noun rajfa (56:4, 69:5) for the great earthquake of the Last Day, the convulsion that strikes all creation. The semantic field captures both natural catastrophe and the eschatological quake that signals divine judgment, a shuddering that nothing and no one can withstand.

meaning.en: The root rāʾ-qāf-dāl (ر-ق-د) denotes sleep, slumber, and lying down. It conveys ruqūd (18:18) — deep sleep — the Companions of the Cave appeared awake but were asleep.
meaning.ar: الرَّاءُ وَالْقَافُ وَالدَّالُ أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى السُّكُونِ وَالْهُجُوعِ. يُقَالُ رَقَدَ يَرْقُدُ رُقُودًا، وَالْمَرْقَدُ: الْمَوْضِعُ. وَالرَّقْدَةُ: النَّوْمَةُ.
meaning.en_detailed: رقد (ر ق د), a root appearing 2 times in the Quran, encodes the notion of Sleep, slumber, and lying down across its various verbal and nominal forms. Classical Arabic employs raqada for the act of sleeping and ruqūd for the state of being asleep, with marqad designating the place of rest. The Quran uses ruqūd (18:18) in the famous narrative of the Sleepers of the Cave, whose sleep appeared to onlookers as a state between waking and death. The semantic field emphasizes both ordinary nightly sleep and the extraordinary suspended animation that becomes a sign of divine power, blending rest with miraculous preservation.

hadith_evidence.text_en: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The merciful will be shown mercy by the Most Merciful. Be merciful to those on earth, and the One in heaven will have mercy upon you."
hadith_evidence.text_ar: عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَمْرٍو رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: «الرَّاحِمُونَ يَرْحَمُهُمُ الرَّحْمَنُ، ارْحَمُوا مَنْ فِي الْأَرْضِ يَرْحَمْ

meaning.en: The root rāʾ-kāf-sīn (ر-ك-س) denotes turning back, reversing, and plunging. It conveys the reversal of direction — being cast back into what was forbidden.
meaning.ar: قال ابن فارس في معجم مقاييس اللغة: الراء والكاف والسين أصل واحد يدل على رد الشيء وقلبه. يقال: رَكَسْتُ الشيءَ أَرْكُسُهُ رَكْسًا، إذا رَدَدْتَهُ.
meaning.en_detailed: ركس (ر ك س), a root appearing 2 times in the Quran, encodes the notion of Turning back, reversing, and plunging across its various verbal and nominal forms. Ibn Fāris identifies r-k-s as denoting the reversal of a thing and turning it on its head, with raks used for the act of overturning. The Quran employs forms of the verb in contexts describing the plunging of the disbelievers into error and ruin, the active casting down into perdition. The semantic field unites the spatial image of headlong descent with the moral image of being cast into reversal and ruin.

hadith_evidence.text_en: Ali reported: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: "Say: O Allah, guide me and direct me."
hadith_evidence.text_ar: عَنْ عَلِيٍّ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: قَالَ لِي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: «قُلِ: اللَّهُمَّ اهْدِنِي وَسَدِّدْنِي»

meaning.en_short: Crushing, crumbling, and reducing to powder
meaning.en: The root rāʾ-fāʾ-tāʾ (ر-ف-ت) denotes crushing, crumbling, and reducing to powder. It conveys rufātan (17:49) — bones crumbled to dust — the disbeliever's mockery of resurrection.
meaning.ar: الرَّاءُ وَالْفَاءُ وَالتَّاءُ أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى تَكَسُّرِ الشَّيْءِ وَتَفَتُّتِهِ. وَمِنْهُ الرُّفَاتُ: مَا تَكَسَّرَ مِنَ الْعِظَامِ وَغَيْرِهَا.
meaning.en_detailed: The triconsonantal root ر ف ت (رفت) — 2 Quranic occurrences — fundamentally expresses Crushing, crumbling, and reducing to powder. Ibn Fāris identifies r-f-t as the breaking and fragmenting of something, with rufāt denoting crumbled, pulverized fragments of bones. The Quran uses rufātan (17:49, 17:98) to describe the state of bones reduced to powder, appearing in the disbeliever's mockery of resurrection: 'When we have become rufātan, shall we really be raised as a new creation?' The semantic field emphasizes complete physical disintegration, a vivid image designed to challenge faith in the resurrection.

meaning.en_short: Obscene speech, lewdness, and sexual relat
meaning.en: The root rāʾ-fāʾ-thāʾ (ر-ف-ث) denotes obscene speech, lewdness, and sexual relations. It conveys rafath (2:187) — marital intimacy permitted on the nights of fasting.
meaning.ar: الرَّاءُ وَالْفَاءُ وَالثَّاءُ أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى الْفُحْشِ فِي الْقَوْلِ. يُقَالُ: رَفَثَ يَرْفِثُ رَفَثًا، إِذَا أَفْحَشَ فِي الْمَنْطِقِ.
meaning.en_detailed: رفث (ر ف ث), a root appearing 2 times in the Quran, encodes the notion of Obscene speech, lewdness, and sexual relat across its various verbal and nominal forms. Classical dictionaries identify r-f-th as indecent speech, particularly in matters of sexual relations, with rafath embracing both the speech and the act. The Quran uses rafath (2:197 in the pilgrimage context, 2:187 in the fasting context) for marital relations, in both cases permitting lawful intimacy while warning against public obscene talk. The semantic field unites moral degradation in speech with the legitimate private sphere of intimate relations.

hadith_evidence.text_en: Abu Dharr reported: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Do not consider any act of goodness insignificant, even if it is meeting your brother with a cheerful face."
hadith_evidence.text_ar: عَنْ أَبِي ذَرٍّ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: «لَا تَحْقِرَنَّ مِنَ الْمَعْرُوفِ شَيْئًا وَلَوْ أَنْ تَلْقَى أَخَاكَ بِوَجْهٍ طَلْقٍ»

meaning.en_short: Moisture, freshness, and the ripe date
meaning.en: The root rāʾ-ṭāʾ-bāʾ (ر-ط-ب) denotes moisture, freshness, and the ripe date. It conveys ruṭaban janiyyan (19:25) — fresh ripe dates that fall for Maryam at the blessed tree.
meaning.ar: الرَّاءُ وَالطَّاءُ وَالْبَاءُ أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى نَقِيضِ الْيُبْسِ. يُقَالُ: رَطُبَ الشَّيْءُ يَرْطُبُ رُطُوبَةً وَرَطَابَةً. (مقاييس اللغة)
meaning.en_detailed: Root ر ط ب (رطب), attested 2 times in the Quran, derives its core meaning of Moisture, freshness, and the ripe date from Proto-Semitic sources. The classical opposition of raṭb to yābis (dry) places this root at the heart of the moisture-dryness dichotomy, with raṭb signifying what is alive, supple, and free from desiccation. The Quran employs ruṭab (2:265, 19:25) for ripe dates, with the famous image of fresh ripe dates falling upon Maryam as a miraculous provision at the blessed tree. The semantic field emphasizes vitality and freshness, the opposite of decay and aridity.

meaning.en: The root rāʾ-fāʾ-dāl (ر-ف-د) denotes support, assistance, and a gift. It conveys the rifd — the grant that strengthens and enables the recipient.
meaning.ar: الرَّاءُ وَالْفَاءُ وَالدَّالُ أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى الْإِعَانَةِ وَالْعَطَاءِ. وَالرِّفْدُ: الْعَطَاءُ وَالصِّلَةُ. وَالْمِرْفَدُ: الْوِسَادَةُ وَمَا يُتَّكَأُ عَلَيْهِ.
meaning.en_detailed: The triconsonantal root ر ف د (رفد) — 2 Quranic occurrences — fundamentally expresses Support, assistance, and a gift. Classical dictionaries identify r-f-d as aid and provision, with rifd denoting a gift or grant and mirfad designating a cushion or support. The Quran uses forms of the root in contexts of divine and angelic support, including the assistance given to the believers through heavenly reinforcement. The semantic field emphasizes beneficence and the reinforcement of another through giving, whether by humans in kindness or by divine decree in moments of trial.

hadith_evidence.text_ar: عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: «احْرِصْ عَلَى مَا يَنْفَعُكَ، وَاسْتَعِنْ بِاللَّهِ وَلَا تَعْجَزْ»

meaning.en: The root qāf-yāʾ-lām (ق-ي-ل) denotes midday rest, siesta, and repose. It conveys qaylūla — the noontime rest — and maqīl (25:24) — the best resting place in Paradise.
meaning.ar: قال ابن فارس في مقاييس اللغة: "القاف والياء واللام أصل واحد يدل على الراحة في نصف النهار، يقال: قَالَ يَقِيلُ قَيْلُولَةً، وهو النوم في القائلة"
meaning.en_detailed: The Arabic root ق ي ل (قيل) appears 2 times in the Quran, governing the semantic domain of Midday rest, siesta, and repose. Ibn Fāris identifies q-y-l as rest in the middle of the day, with qaylūla denoting the noontime nap and qāʾil one who takes such rest. The Quran uses maqīl (25:24) for the resting place afforded to the blessed on the Day of Resurrection, transforming this humble daytime rest into an eternal heavenly repose. The semantic field unites ordinary physical rest during the heat with the ultimate rest of Paradise promised to the righteous.

hadith_evidence.text_ar: عَنْ عُمَرَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: «لَوْ أَنَّكُمْ تَتَوَكَّلُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ حَقَّ تَوَكُّلِهِ لَرَزَقَكُمْ كَمَا يَرْزُقُ الطَّيْرَ،

meaning.en: The root rāʾ-ʿayn-dāl (ر-ع-د) denotes thunder, trembling, and rumbling. It conveys al-raʿd (13:13) — the thunder that glorifies Allah's praise as lightning strikes.
meaning.ar: ابن فارس — مقاييس اللغة — مادة رعد
meaning.en_detailed: The Arabic root ر ع د (رعد) appears 2 times in the Quran, governing the semantic domain of Thunder, trembling, and rumbling. Classical Arabic connects raʿd to the rumbling sound of thunder, with the verb raʿida describing the rumbling that shakes the sky. The Quran mentions al-raʿd (13:13) in a remarkable personification where the thunder itself glorifies Allah's praise, and the angels revere Him from awe of it. The semantic field unites meteorological phenomenon with eschatological awe, as thunder becomes both a natural sign and an index of divine majesty.

hadith_evidence.text_ar: عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: «كُلُّ سُلَامَى مِنَ النَّاسِ عَلَيْهِ صَدَقَةٌ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ تَطْلُعُ فِيهِ الشَّمْسُ»

meaning.en_short: Appointing a companion, the eggshell, and d
meaning.en: The root qāf-yāʾ-ḍād (ق-ي-ض) denotes appointing a companion, the eggshell, and destined pairing. It conveys nuqayyiḍ (43:36) — We assign a devil as companion to those who turn from the Reminder.
meaning.ar: الْقَافُ وَالْيَاءُ وَالضَّادُ أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى تَقْدِيرِ شَيْءٍ وَتَهْيِئَتِهِ. يُقَالُ: قَيَّضَ اللَّهُ لَهُ قَرِينًا، أَيْ هَيَّأَهُ وَقَدَّرَهُ.
meaning.en_detailed: Root ق ي ض (قيض), attested 2 times in the Quran, derives its core meaning of Appointing a companion, the eggshell, and d from Proto-Semitic sources. The verbal form qayyaḍa (to assign, destine) appears in the Quran (41:25, 43:36) to describe Allah's appointment of devils as companions (qurʾan) to those who reject the Reminder, a divine pairing with lasting consequence. The secondary meaning of eggshell connects to the curved form that encloses. The semantic field unites divine predestination with the natural imagery of pairing and enclosure, both the matched companion and the shell that contains.

meaning.en_short: A bare, flat expanse of ground
meaning.en: The root qāf-wāw-ʿayn (ق-و-ع) denotes a bare, flat expanse of ground. It conveys the broad, open plain — the level terrain that stretches uninterrupted to the horizon.
meaning.ar: الْقَافُ وَالْوَاوُ وَالْعَيْنُ أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى انْبِسَاطٍ وَاسْتِوَاءٍ فِي الْأَرْضِ. وَالْقَاعُ: الْأَرْضُ الْمُسْتَوِيَةُ الْمَلْسَاءُ
meaning.en_detailed: Occurring 2 times in the Quranic text, the root ق و ع (قوع) conveys the essential concept of A bare, flat expanse of ground. The Quran uses al-qāʿ (in verses such as those describing the place of gathering) to characterize the level, open terrain where the stones of Hell will be cast, marked by its bareness and openness. The semantic field emphasizes the absence of features — the open plain where one can see from horizon to horizon. The metaphor extends to emptiness and exposure before divine judgment, when all concealment is stripped away.

meaning.en: The root qāf-wāw-tāʾ (ق-و-ت) denotes sustenance, nourishment, and essential provision. It conveys the qūt — the minimal food that maintains life — enough to survive.
meaning.ar: الْقَافُ وَالْوَاوُ وَالتَّاءُ أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى الْقُوَّةِ. وَمِنْهُ الْقُوتُ، وَهُوَ مَا يَقُوتُ الْإِنْسَانَ أَيْ يَحْفَظُهُ وَيَقُومُ بِهِ. وَالْقَيِّمُ: الْقَائِمُ بِالْأَمْرِ.
meaning.en_detailed: Occurring 2 times in the Quranic text, the root ق و ت (قوت) conveys the essential concept of Sustenance, nourishment, and essential prov. Classical Arabic defines qūt as that which sustains and preserves life, the minimal but sufficient nourishment, as opposed to delicacies or luxuries. The Quran uses the term to describe the food or provision given to various communities, including Maryam's miraculous sustenance (3:37, 'every time Zechariah entered upon her in the sanctuary, he found her with provision') and the provisions of the blessed in Paradise (13:35). The semantic field emphasizes sufficiency and life-maintenance rather than excess.

meaning.en: The root qāf-nūn-ʿayn (ق-ن-ع) denotes contentment, satisfaction, and the mask. It conveys qanāʿa — being satisfied with what one has — and qināʿ — the face-covering veil.
meaning.ar: الْقَافُ وَالنُّونُ وَالْعَيْنُ أَصْلَانِ: أَحَدُهُمَا رَفْعُ الرَّأْسِ، وَالْآخَرُ الرِّضَا بِالشَّيْءِ. فَالْأَوَّلُ: أَقْنَعَ الرَّجُلُ رَأْسَهُ إِذَا رَفَعَهُ.
meaning.en_detailed: The Arabic root ق ن ع (قنع) appears 2 times in the Quran, governing the semantic domain of Contentment, satisfaction, and the mask. Ibn Fāris distinguishes two semantic strands in q-n-ʿ: one of raising or lifting the head, and another of satisfaction with what one has, with qanāʿa denoting contentment and qināʿ the face-covering veil. The Quran uses qināʿ (33:59) for the face-covering garment of Muslim women, while classical usage develops qanāʿa into a moral virtue of being satisfied with one's lawful provision. The semantic field unites the inward state of contentment with the outward veiling that conceals and protects.

meaning.en_short: Frying, parching, and intense dry heat

meaning.ar: الْقَافُ وَاللَّامُ وَالْيَاءُ أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى الْبُغْضِ وَالْكَرَاهَةِ. وَمِنْهُ الْقَلَى وَالْقِلَى، وَهُوَ الْبُغْضُ الشَّدِيدُ.
meaning.en_detailed: The Arabic root ق ل ي (قلي) appears 2 times in the Quran, governing the semantic domain of Frying, parching, and intense dry heat. The Quran employs forms connected to the cooking or scorching imagery of intense heat (cf. 18:29 where qaliya appears in the form meaning to be heated or burnt), and classical usage develops the metaphor of consuming hatred. The semantic field spans physical transformation through heat and the metaphor of being inwardly consumed by intense aversion, both senses marked by extremity.

meaning.ar: (نَحَلَ) النُّونُ وَالْحَاءُ وَاللَّامُ أَصْلَانِ: أَحَدُهُمَا الْعَطِيَّةُ، وَالْآخَرُ الْمَيْلُ. فَالْأَوَّلُ: نَحَلَهُ يَنْحَلُهُ نِحْلَةً، إِذَا أَعْطَاهُ.
meaning.en_detailed: Arabic root نحل. Quranic usage includes Bees, gift-giving, and emaciation.

hadith_evidence.text_en: Jabir ibn Abdullah reported: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "No Muslim plants a tree except that whatever is eaten from it is charity for him."
hadith_evidence.text_ar: عَنْ جَابِرِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: «مَا مِنْ مُسْلِمٍ يَغْرِسُ غَرْسًا إِلَّا كَانَ مَا أُكِلَ مِنْهُ لَهُ صَدَقَ

meaning.en: The root mīm-lām-qāf (م-ل-ق) denotes flattery, smooth speech, and ingratiation. It conveys tamalluq — the fauning tongue that feigns affection for gain.
meaning.ar: مَلَقَ: الْمِيمُ وَاللَّامُ وَالْقَافُ أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى الْفَقْرِ وَالْحَاجَةِ. يُقَالُ: أَمْلَقَ الرَّجُلُ إِذَا افْتَقَرَ، وَهُوَ مُمْلِقٌ.
meaning.en_detailed: Arabic root ملق. Quranic usage includes Flattery, smooth speech, and ingratiation.

hadith_evidence.text_en: Abu Dharr reported: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Do not consider any act of goodness insignificant, even if it is meeting your brother with a cheerful face."

meaning.en: The root nūn-shīn-ṭāʾ (ن-ش-ط) denotes activity, briskness, and untethering. It conveys nashīṭ — the energetic person full of life — and nashṭ — the act of untying.

meaning.en_detailed: Arabic root نشط. Quranic usage includes Activity, briskness, and untethering.

meaning.en_short: Middle age, the prime of life
meaning.en: The root kāf-hāʾ-lām (ك-ه-ل) denotes middle age, the prime of life. It conveys kahl — the stage between youth and old age — full maturity and peak capacity.
meaning.ar: الْكَافُ وَالْهَاءُ وَاللَّامُ أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى الْإِدْرَاكِ وَالْبُلُوغِ.
meaning.en_detailed: The triconsonantal root ك ه ل (كهل) — 2 Quranic occurrences — fundamentally expresses Middle age, the prime of life. Ibn Fāris classifies it under notions of attainment (idrāk) and full maturity, designating كَهْل the man who has reached his peak strength and judgment. In the Qurʾān it occurs at 22:5 (بَلَغَ أَشُدَّهُ وَبَلَغَ أَشُدَّهُ أَرْبَعِينَ سَنَةً), describing the physiological fulcrum at which physical vigour meets seasoned wisdom, and at 46:15 with the prayer لِمَنْ بَلَغَ أَرْبَعِينَ سَنَةً, marking the threshold of mature accountability before God.

meaning.en: The root kāf-dāl-ḥāʾ (ك-د-ح) denotes toiling, laboring strenuously, and striving. It conveys kādiḥun ilā rabbika (84:6) — O mankind, you are ever toiling toward your Lord.
meaning.ar: الْكَافُ وَالدَّالُ وَالْحَاءُ أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى الْعَمَلِ وَالْكَدِّ، يُقَالُ: كَدَحَ يَكْدَحُ كَدْحًا، وَهُوَ الْعَمَلُ بِالْيَدِ وَالْجِدِّ.
meaning.en_detailed: The root ك-د-ح conveys laborious striving and the sweat-inducing effort of sustained work, derived in the lexicons from يد عاملة مجتهدة. The Qurʾān twice employs كَادِحٌ to characterize the ceaseless trajectory of human existence toward its Lord: يَا أَيُّهَا الْإِنسَانُ إِنَّكَ كَادِحٌ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ كَدْحًا فَمُلَاقِيهِ (84:6), where the kadhḥ is a pilgrimage of deeds whose terminus is the meeting with God, and 56:14 and 88:3 in kindred constructions. Classical commentators (al-Ṭabarī, al-Qurṭubī) gloss كدح as العمل والجدّ المضني, juxtaposing the toil of the righteous and the hopeless labour of the disbeliever alike.

meaning.en_short: Barren land, devastation, and stripping bar
meaning.en: The root jīm-rāʾ-zāy (ج-ر-ز) denotes barren land, devastation, and stripping bare. It conveys juruzan (18:8) — earth left barren after divine punishment strips it of life.
meaning.ar: الْجِيمُ وَالرَّاءُ وَالزَّاءُ أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى الْيُبْسِ وَالْجَفَافِ. وَالْجُرُزُ: الْأَرْضُ الْيَابِسَةُ الَّتِي لَا نَبَاتَ فِيهَا.
meaning.en_detailed: The Arabic root ج ر ز (جرز) appears 2 times in the Quran, governing the semantic domain of Barren land, devastation, and stripping bar. Qurʾānic usage at 18:8 employs جُرُزًا for the scorched gardens of the impious owners whose fruit was annihilated between two nights, contrasted with gardens whose fruit is preserved by divine mercy. Ibn Fāris and al-Zajjāj derive the root from اليبس والجفاف, and the hadith tradition retains this imagery when describing apocalyptic devastation, where arable fields are reduced to a state indistinguishable from the primordial, lifeless earth.

meaning.en: The root jīm-rāʾ-dāl (ج-ر-د) denotes stripping, denuding, and the locust. It conveys jarād (7:133) — locusts that stripped Egypt bare as one of the plagues.
meaning.ar: الْجِيمُ وَالرَّاءُ وَالدَّالُ أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى تَجْرِيدِ الشَّيْءِ وَإِفْرَادِهِ، وَمِنْهُ الْجَرَادُ لِأَنَّهُ يَجْرُدُ الْأَرْضَ، وَالْجَرِيدَةُ مِنَ النَّخْلِ لِأَنَّهَا تُجَرَّدُ مِنَ
meaning.en_detailed: The root ج-ر-د embraces both the act of stripping or denuding and the creature that strips bare — the locust. In 7:133 Pharaoh's people are struck by locusts (الْجَرَادَ) as the third of the nine plagues, the insects devouring Egypt's produce before the finger of God withdrew them. Etymologically جريدة and مجرّد both preserve the image of removing what clings: the palm-frond stripped of leaves, the body stripped of covering. Classical tafsīr reads the locust plague as the literalisation of الجرد — the denuding hand of providence against those who had stripped others of their rights.

hadith_evidence.text_ar: عَنْ أَبِي ذَرٍّ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: «لَا تَحْقِرَنَّ مِنَ الْمَعْرُوفِ شَيْئًا وَلَوْ أَنْ تَلْقَى أَخَاكَ بِوَجْهٍ طَلْقٍ»

meaning.en: The root jīm-sīn-mīm (ج-س-م) denotes body, corporeality, and physical bulk. It conveys jism — the tangible, three-dimensional form of the living being.
meaning.ar: الْجِيمُ وَالسِّينُ وَالْمِيمُ أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى جِرْمِ الشَّيْءِ وَجُثَّتِهِ. وَالْجِسْمُ: الْجَسَدُ، وَالْجَمْعُ أَجْسَامٌ.
meaning.en_detailed: Root ج س م (جسم), attested 2 times in the Quran, derives its core meaning of Body, corporeality, and physical bulk from Proto-Semitic sources. Though rare in the Qurʾān, the root appears in references to substantiality and physical presence, as when disbelievers demand an angelic visitation in جِسْمٍ عَظِيمٍ — a glorious body — rather than submitting to the unseen word. Lisān al-ʿArab defines الجسم as الجسد، وكل ذي جثة من الحيوان, and the mufassirūn contrast جِسْم with رُوح, the latter being Allah's command while the former is the clay-formed vessel that houses it.

hadith_evidence.text_en: Ibn Abbas reported: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "There are two blessings which many people squander: health and free time."
hadith_evidence.text_ar: عَنْ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: «نِعْمَتَانِ مَغْبُونٌ فِيهِمَا كَثِيرٌ مِنَ النَّاسِ: الصِّحَّةُ وَالْفَرَاغُ»

meaning.en_short: Deviation, injustice, and inclining from tr
meaning.en: The root jīm-nūn-fāʾ (ج-ن-ف) denotes deviation, injustice, and inclining from truth. It conveys janaf (2:182) — deviation in a will — corrected by reconciliation.
meaning.ar: «الْجِيمُ وَالنُّونُ وَالْفَاءُ أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى مَيْلٍ وَعُدُولٍ عَنِ الشَّيْءِ. يُقَالُ جَنَفَ يَجْنَفُ جَنَفًا إِذَا مَالَ. وَالْجَنَفُ فِي الْوَصِيَّةِ: الْمَيْلُ عَنِ الْحَقِّ»
meaning.en_detailed: The root ج-ن-ف denotes moral and directional deviation, the tilting away from the upright path or the just mean. In 2:182 the Qurʾān uses جَنَفٌ of the testator whose bequest errs toward injustice (who tilts away from equity), commanding the community to rectify it (فَإِنْ عَلِمْتُمْ فِيهِمْ خَيْرًا). Al-Ṭabarī glosses جَنَف as ميل عن الحق وعدول, and Ibn Fāris places the root under الميل والعُدول. The lexeme surfaces in hadith language of wilāya — guardianship — where parents and guardians who incline from justice on behalf of orphaned wards are charged with avoiding janaf in their administration of trust.

hadith_evidence.text_en: Abdullah ibn Amr reported: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The just will be with Allah on pulpits of light."
hadith_evidence.text_ar: عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَمْرٍو رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: «إِنَّ الْمُقْسِطِينَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ عَلَى مَنَابِرَ مِنْ نُورٍ»

meaning.en_short: Cutting off, severing, and the deep well
meaning.en: The root jīm-bāʾ-bāʾ (ج-ب-ب) denotes cutting off, severing, and the deep well. It conveys both the act of amputation and the jubb — the well into which Joseph was thrown.
meaning.ar: الْجِيمُ وَالْبَاءُ أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى الْقَطْعِ. مِنْ ذَلِكَ الْجَبُّ: الْقَطْعُ. وَالْجُبُّ: الْبِئْرُ، سُمِّيَتْ بِذَلِكَ لِأَنَّهَا قُطِعَتْ فِي الْأَرْضِ قَطْعًا
meaning.en_detailed: The doubled-root ج-ب-ب, on the rarer pattern of identical radices, connotes severance and the cavity produced by cutting into the earth. Its two Qurʾānic senses are therefore striking in juxtaposition: at 12:10 the جُبّ is the dry well into which Joseph's brothers cast him, and at 12:15 the same word names the pit whose interior they described to the caravaners. Al-Zajjāj and the mufassirūn derive الجبّ from the cutting (قطع) of the earth, while Ibn Fāris traces it to a single semantic field of القطع. The root's bipartite meaning — cutting-off and the thing cut — produces an unusually concrete image: Joseph's descent is both an act of severance and a plunge into severed space.

hadith_evidence.text_en: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Every joint of a person has a charity due upon it each day the sun rises."
hadith_evidence.text_ar: عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: «كُلُّ سُلَامَى مِنَ النَّاسِ عَلَيْهِ صَدَقَةٌ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ تَطْلُعُ فِيهِ الشَّمْسُ»

meaning.en_short: Bringing, attracting, and the clamor of a c
meaning.en: The root jīm-lām-bāʾ (ج-ل-ب) denotes bringing, attracting, and the clamor of a crowd. It conveys jalaba — to fetch or draw toward — and jalbaba — the noise of assembly.
meaning.ar: الْجِيمُ وَاللَّامُ وَالْبَاءُ أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى سَوْقِ الشَّيْءِ وَجَمْعِهِ. مِنْ ذَلِكَ الْجَلَبُ، وَهُوَ مَا يُجْلَبُ مِنْ بَلَدٍ إِلَى بَلَدٍ.
meaning.en_detailed: The root ج-ل-ب carries the meaning of drawing or driving something from one place to another, whether by fetching, attracting, or driving forward as a flock or crowd. The Qurʾānic occurrence at 27:32 speaks of a speaker who carries or attracts an audience (فَمَنْ جَاءَهَا يَحْمِلُ قَوْمَهُ), and the noun جَلَب is used in pre-Islamic trade for goods fetched from afar. Ibn al-Athīr in al-Nihāya notes the lexical range: جلب المال — bringing wealth from afar, and جلب القوم — driving people to gather. The root preserves the image of motion compelled by desire, whether the lure of merchandise or the call of assembly.
